title: Dependence-Aware Label Aggregation for LLM-as-a-Judge via Ising Models
authors: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian; Aleksandr Podkopaev; Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan
venue: arXiv
subtopics: dependent LLM judges; Ising model; label aggregation; conditional independence violation
specdx_components: family effects/correlated errors; anchored cell model; identifiability
summary: Studies aggregation of binary judgments from K dependent LLM judges with a hierarchy of Ising and latent-factor models. Independence-based methods (Dawid-Skene, weighted majority) can flip the Bayes label and stay strictly suboptimal as K grows. The dependence-aware method improves on three real datasets.
relation_to_specdx: It formally shows the risk SpecDx's cross-family independence assumption carries, and offers a latent-factor correction that could serve as a family-effect extension of the anchored cell model.

title: Experts Rise Where LLMs Disagree: Using Cross-Model Disagreement to Target Expert Effort in LLM Codebook Revision for Large-Scale Annotation
authors: Zeyu He; Zhuqian Zhou; Kirk Vanacore; Rene F. Kizilcec; Ting-Hao 'Kenneth' Huang
venue: arXiv
subtopics: cross-LLM disagreement; codebook revision; annotation guidelines
specdx_components: baseline B4; defect taxonomy; active synthesis
summary: Applies an early annotation codebook with several LLMs, surfaces strong cross-LLM disagreement, and compares three ways of eliciting expert feedback on these cases (verifying LLM-generated codebook revisions, answering questions, labelling with rationales) on tutoring transcripts. Rationale labelling gives the best LLM labelling accuracy and cuts codebook revision from months to days.
relation_to_specdx: It uses disagreement across an LLM population to locate defects in a natural-language specification (the codebook), which partly overlaps SpecDx's claim. It relies on human experts, has no rater model, defect typing, executable checks or witnesses, whereas SpecDx is fully automatic and logic-backed.

title: N-Version Programming with Coding Agents
authors: Javier Ron; Benoit Baudry; Martin Monperrus
venue: arXiv
subtopics: N-version programming; coding agents; common-mode failures; specification ambiguity
summary: Repeats the Knight-Leveson experiment with 48 implementations from AI coding agents of the Launch Interceptor specification, tested on a million random inputs. It finds substantial common-mode failure, much of it traceable to where the specification is hard or ambiguous, yet majority-voted triples still reduce failures sharply.
relation_to_specdx: It is direct evidence that coincident failures of an LLM-agent population localise specification difficulty or ambiguity, which is SpecDx's core signal. It reports the phenomenon but offers no method to separate spec defects from agent errors or to type them.

title: Observational Equivalence of LLM and Human Annotation
authors: Kentaro Nakamura; Jing Ling Tan; George Yean
venue: arXiv
subtopics: LLM vs expert coding; ambiguity in coding rules; cross-LLM disagreement
specdx_components: baseline B4; defect taxonomy; set-valued truth
summary: Replicates 14 political-science text-classification studies with ten LLMs, three experts and 165 crowd workers. LLMs are observationally equivalent to experts, and the equivalence is driven by ambiguity in texts and coding rules: where LLMs disagree with experts, experts also disagree, and clarifying rules reduces both. Proposes using cross-LLM disagreement to find difficult cases and refine codebooks, plus ambiguity-aware bounds.
relation_to_specdx: It is empirical support for SpecDx's premise that cross-model disagreement concentrates on ambiguous rules, and it proposes refining the codebook (spec) from that disagreement. It is not a typed or localised diagnosis and has no anchor model or logic, so it overlaps SpecDx's ambiguity component only.

title: Quantifying and Correcting Measurement Error in LLM-Generated Classifications: A Beta-Binomial Latent Class Model for Correlated Repeated Judgments
authors: Yichi Zhang; Ignacio Martinez
venue: arXiv
subtopics: repeated LLM judgments; intraclass correlation; beta-binomial latent class; identifiability
specdx_components: family effects/correlated errors; identifiability; anchored cell model
summary: Using 52,500 judgments from seven open-weight LLMs, shows that repeated samples of the same model on the same item are strongly correlated (ICC 0.50 to 0.93), so binomial latent class models are miscalibrated and biased. Proposes a beta-binomial latent class model with one correlation parameter and proves its identifiability.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx draws several runs per model per cell. This paper shows that such runs are not independent readings and gives the beta-binomial fix, which SpecDx's likelihood should adopt or test against.

title: Validating LLM-as-a-Judge Systems under Rating Indeterminacy
authors: Luke Guerdan; Solon Barocas; Kenneth Holstein; Hanna Wallach; Zhiwei Steven Wu; Alexandra Chouldechova
venue: arXiv
subtopics: rating indeterminacy; multiple valid ratings; LLM-as-judge validation
summary: Introduces 'rating indeterminacy', where rating criteria admit several valid interpretations so a rater may deem multiple ratings correct. Gives a framework for validating LLM judges under it and shows that forced-choice elicitation and aggregation can heavily bias judge validation (NeurIPS 2025 per the arXiv comment).
relation_to_specdx: Rating indeterminacy is SpecDx's ambiguity defect (A_c = {x, y}) viewed from the evaluation side. It supports eliciting or modelling set-valued truth rather than forcing one label.

title: Learning from Crowds with Crowd-Kit
authors: Dmitry Ustalov; Nikita Pavlichenko; Boris Tseitlin
venue: Journal of Open Source Software
subtopics: crowd-kit; aggregation library; DS/GLAD/MACE/KOS/M-MSR
specdx_components: baseline B2; baseline B3; anchored cell model
summary: Software paper for Crowd-Kit, a Python library implementing common aggregation methods for crowdsourced categorical, multi-label, pairwise, textual and segmentation responses, plus quality metrics and dataset loaders (from the repository README and JOSS metadata).
relation_to_specdx: It is the most practical offline implementation of the classic truth-inference baselines SpecDx must beat in simulation and on real matrices.
baseline_notes: Input is a DataFrame with columns task, worker and label. Map task to cell id (table, row, column, scenario step), worker to model id (plus 'spec' for d_c), and label to the read value. Run MajorityVote, DawidSkene, OneCoinDawidSkene, GLAD, MACE, KOS, MMSR and ZeroBasedSkill, and flag cells where aggregate differs from d_c. BinaryRelevance gives a crude multi-label (set-valued) variant. All run offline on CPU.

title: Recovering Top-Two Answers and Confusion Probability in Multi-Choice Crowdsourcing
authors: Hyeonsu Jeong; Hye Won Chung
venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: top-two answers; confusion probability; task difficulty; minimax optimal
summary: Models multi-choice crowdsourcing tasks as having two plausible answers, with task difficulty as the confusion probability between them and worker reliability as the probability of answering within the top two. A two-stage algorithm recovers the truth, the most confusing answer and the confusion probability at a minimax-optimal rate.
relation_to_specdx: It is the closest crowdsourcing model to SpecDx's two-valued entailment set {x, y}: both posit items with two plausible answers. Jeong and Chung still assume one is the ground truth, whereas SpecDx treats both as entailed (ambiguity), adds the empty set and an anchor, and maps outcomes to spec-defect types.
baseline_notes: Per cell, it returns the top-two values and the confusion probability. High confusion with the spec value among the top two indicates ambiguity, and the spec value outside the top two indicates a mis-key. It needs a multi-choice table (cells x models). No official code verified; the algorithm is spectral plus refinement and moderate to re-implement.

title: Learning from Multiple Noisy Partial Labelers
authors: Peilin Yu; Tiffany Ding; Stephen H. Bach
venue: Proceedings of The 25th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
subtopics: partial labelers; set-valued outputs; identifiability; weak supervision
summary: Extends programmatic weak supervision to partial labelers that output subsets of classes, with a generative model that estimates their accuracies without ground truth, a scalable learning procedure, and a proof of generic identifiability up to label swapping.
relation_to_specdx: It handles set-valued rater outputs with identifiability, the mirror image of SpecDx's set-valued truth (sets on the latent side, not the observation side). It is useful for identifiability arguments.

title: Fast and Three-rious: Speeding Up Weak Supervision with Triplet Methods
authors: Daniel Fu; Mayee Chen; Frederic Sala; Sarah Hooper; Kayvon Fatahalian; Christopher Re
venue: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: FlyingSquid; triplet method; closed-form label model
summary: Shows that for a class of weak-supervision latent variable models the parameters have closed-form solutions via triplets of conditionally independent sources, giving FlyingSquid, which is far faster than SGD-based label models, has generalisation bounds without exact model specification, and matches or exceeds their quality.
relation_to_specdx: Triplet identifiability (three conditionally independent sources) contrasts with SpecDx's two-model-plus-anchor identification. FlyingSquid is a fast binary-label baseline.
baseline_notes: Binary encoding: for each cell and model, +1 if the reading equals d_c and -1 otherwise (0 when not executed). The FlyingSquid label model estimates model accuracies in closed form and a posterior that the anchor is right. Cells with low posterior become defect candidates. It needs three or more families for the triplets. Code is unmaintained since 2020 but pure Python.

title: Exploiting Worker Correlation for Label Aggregation in Crowdsourcing
authors: Yuan Li; Benjamin Rubinstein; Trevor Cohn
venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: worker correlation; EBCC; Bayesian classifier combination; tensor decomposition
specdx_components: family effects/correlated errors; anchored cell model
summary: Proposes Enhanced Bayesian Classifier Combination (EBCC), which induces inter-worker correlation through a mixture of intra-class reliabilities linked to tensor decomposition and item clustering, fitted by mean-field VI. It achieved the highest mean accuracy among ten methods on 17 real datasets.
relation_to_specdx: It is the strongest classic aggregator that models correlated raters, the crowd analogue of SpecDx's family effects. It is a natural simulation baseline to show what modelling correlation without anchors or set truth buys.
baseline_notes: Run EBCC on cell x model labels (the spec as an extra worker). It tests whether correlation modelling alone recovers SpecDx's spec-defect flags. Code: the authors' repository was not verified; a reimplementation of mean-field VI is moderate effort.

title: Comparing Bayesian Models of Annotation
authors: Silviu Paun; Bob Carpenter; Jon Chamberlain; Dirk Hovy; Udo Kruschwitz; Massimo Poesio
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
subtopics: Bayesian models of annotation; item difficulty; pooling; model comparison
summary: Compares six Bayesian annotation models, which differ in how they treat annotator ability, item difficulty and parameter pooling, on four datasets with spammy annotators. It evaluates gold-label recovery, predictive accuracy, annotator characterisation and item difficulty, and gives model-selection guidelines.
relation_to_specdx: It provides the design space (pooling, difficulty, annotator ability) in which SpecDx's anchored cell model sits. It is a good source for the simulation baselines (DS, MACE, hierarchical models). None of the compared models has set-valued truth or an anchor.

title: Domain-aware multi-truth discovery from conflicting sources
authors: Xueling Lin; Lei Chen
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment
subtopics: multi-truth discovery; domain expertise; Bayesian
summary: Models domain-specific source expertise (via data richness and influence) in a Bayesian framework that jointly infers expertise and value-set confidences, recovering multiple truths per object without supervision (from metadata and a search-result abstract snippet).
relation_to_specdx: Domain-dependent expertise is analogous to SpecDx's model ability varying with cell group difficulty (alpha_m - beta_g). Like LTM, it supports set-valued truth but has no anchor and no defect typing.

title: Estimating Accuracy from Unlabeled Data: A Probabilistic Logic Approach
authors: Emmanouil Platanios; Hoifung Poon; Tom M. Mitchell; Eric J Horvitz
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
subtopics: accuracy estimation; logical constraints; probabilistic logic; agreement
summary: Estimates classifier accuracies from unlabelled data across multiple related classification problems tied by logical constraints (e.g. mutual exclusion), using probabilistic logic. Agreement suggests correctness, and constraint violations imply at least one classifier errs.
relation_to_specdx: It is one of the few works combining statistics over a population of fallible predictors with logical constraints, close in spirit to SpecDx's statistics-plus-logic design. However, its constraints are assumed correct and the goal is to grade the classifiers, whereas SpecDx treats the constraints (the spec's checks) as the suspect and returns typed, witnessed defect diagnoses.

title: Learning the Structure of Generative Models without Labeled Data
authors: Stephen H. Bach; Bryan He; Alexander Ratner; Christopher Ré
venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: dependency structure learning; weak supervision; pseudolikelihood
summary: Learns the dependency structure among weak-supervision sources without labelled data by maximising l1-regularised marginal pseudolikelihood, with sample complexity sublinear in the number of possible dependencies, and is much faster and more precise than maximum likelihood.
relation_to_specdx: Learning which raters are dependent from unlabelled outputs could validate SpecDx's assumed family structure, i.e. whether errors are correlated within families and independent across them.

title: Snorkel: rapid training data creation with weak supervision
authors: Alexander Ratner; Stephen H. Bach; Henry Ehrenberg; Jason Fries; Sen Wu; Christopher Ré
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment
subtopics: Snorkel; labeling functions; label model; correlations
specdx_components: anchored cell model; family effects/correlated errors
summary: Presents Snorkel, an end-to-end system for data programming. Users write labelling functions with unknown accuracies and correlations, Snorkel denoises them without ground truth, and models train without hand labels (2.8x faster model building and +45.5% performance in a user study).
relation_to_specdx: Snorkel's label model is the standard tool for aggregating correlated programmatic raters. SpecDx's checks C are labelling-function-like, but SpecDx asks whether C itself is wrong.
baseline_notes: Snorkel LabelModel (matrix-completion label model, multi-class, abstains allowed) over L = cells x models with the spec value as an extra column. Optionally add family-level dependency structure. Cells with argmax different from d_c become defect candidates. It runs offline on CPU. It cannot express two-valued or empty truths, so ambiguity and contradiction show only as low-confidence posteriors.

title: Truth inference in crowdsourcing: is the problem solved?
authors: Yudian Zheng; Guoliang Li; Yuanbing Li; Caihua Shan; Reynold Cheng
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment
subtopics: truth inference survey; crowdsourcing benchmark; 17 algorithms
summary: Surveys 17 crowdsourcing truth-inference algorithms from the database and data-mining communities and evaluates them under one framework on five real datasets. No algorithm wins consistently, so the authors conclude the problem is not solved and release code and datasets.
relation_to_specdx: It is the main empirical survey of classic truth inference and the obvious source of simulation baselines. Its finding of instability across datasets motivates SpecDx's pre-registered simulation study instead of one benchmark.

title: Data Programming: Creating Large Training Sets, Quickly
authors: Alexander J Ratner; Christopher M De Sa; Sen Wu; Daniel Selsam; Christopher Ré
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
subtopics: data programming; labeling functions; generative label model
summary: Introduces data programming: users write noisy, conflicting labelling functions viewed as a generative noise model whose parameters are recovered without labels (with recovery guarantees in some settings), then a noise-aware discriminative loss trains the end model.
relation_to_specdx: Labelling functions are fallible programmatic raters, like SpecDx's executable clauses C. SpecDx inverts the setting: it uses LLM interpreters to audit the programmatic checks rather than using checks to label data.
baseline_notes: Snorkel LabelModel on a matrix L (cells x models, values encoded as class ids, -1 for abstain), with the spec as one 'LF'. It gives per-model accuracies and the cell posterior, so a mis-key is flagged where argmax differs from d_c. Limited to a fixed label space per task; set-valued truth is not representable. Offline, pip install snorkel.

title: Spectral Methods Meet EM: A Provably Optimal Algorithm for Crowdsourcing
authors: Yuchen Zhang; Xi Chen; Dengyong Zhou; Michael I. Jordan
venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research
subtopics: spectral initialisation; EM; optimal convergence rate; Dawid-Skene
summary: Gives a two-stage algorithm for multi-class Dawid-Skene: a spectral (tensor) method initialises the confusion matrices and EM then refines them. It achieves the optimal convergence rate up to a log factor, and is comparable to the best empirical methods (journal version of NeurIPS 2014).
relation_to_specdx: It is the reference for provable DS estimation via third-order moments, which needs three or more conditionally independent raters. SpecDx's identification route (accuracy gradient plus anchor) and its finite-sample Hoeffding bounds should be compared against this rate.

title: Unsupervised Ensemble Learning with Dependent Classifiers
authors: Ariel Jaffe; Ethan Fetaya; Boaz Nadler; Tingting Jiang; Yuval Kluger
venue: Proceedings of the 19th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
subtopics: dependent classifiers; conditional independence violation; unsupervised ensemble
summary: Introduces a statistical model that allows groups of dependent classifiers in unsupervised ensemble learning, with methods to detect strong violations of conditional independence without labels, estimate accuracies better and build an improved meta-learner.
relation_to_specdx: It is the closest unsupervised-ensemble treatment of SpecDx's family effects: dependent groups of raters detected without labels. SpecDx knows family membership a priori and should test within-family dependence as this paper does.

title: An Integrated Bayesian Approach for Effective Multi-Truth Discovery
authors: Xianzhi Wang; Quan Z. Sheng; Xiu Susie Fang; Lina Yao; Xiaofei Xu; Xue Li
venue: Proceedings of the 24th ACM International on Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
subtopics: multi-truth discovery; Bayesian; mutual exclusion
summary: Proposes an integrated Bayesian approach to multi-truth discovery that accounts for claims made of value sets, the differing implications of mutual exclusion between values, and richer source profiles (from the S2 TLDR).
relation_to_specdx: It is direct prior art for set-valued truth inference. SpecDx's entailment sets are a restricted, interpretable case ({x}, {x,y}, empty) tied to defect types, with an anchor rater that multi-truth discovery lacks.

title: Estimating the accuracies of multiple classifiers without labeled data
authors: Ariel Jaffe; Boaz Nadler; Yuval Kluger
venue: Proceedings of the Eighteenth International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
subtopics: spectral meta-learner; unsupervised ensemble; classifier accuracy without labels
summary: Shows that under conditional independence the accuracies of many binary classifiers can be estimated consistently from unlabelled predictions alone, because the off-diagonal covariance matrix and third-order tensor are rank-one. Gives efficient spectral algorithms and a better unsupervised ensemble.
relation_to_specdx: It is the canonical evidence that accuracy is identifiable from agreement structure alone. SpecDx's accuracy-gradient signatures play a similar role but separate spec defects (consistent deviations) from interpreter errors.
baseline_notes: Binarise each cell (reading == d_c or not) and run the spectral meta-learner on models x cells. It estimates model accuracies and an unsupervised consensus that flags cells where consensus rejects the anchor. About 30 lines of numpy to re-implement (no official package verified).

title: Modeling Truth Existence in Truth Discovery
authors: Shi Zhi; Bo Zhao; Wenzhu Tong; Jing Gao; Dian Yu; Heng Ji; Jiawei Han
venue: Proceedings of the 21th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
subtopics: no-truth questions; truth existence; truth discovery
summary: Addresses no-truth questions, whose true answer is absent from every source's candidate answers. It proposes a graphical model with a source quality that covers silence, which jointly infers truth existence, truths and source quality without ground truth, initialised by a truth-existence score.
relation_to_specdx: It is the truth-discovery counterpart of SpecDx's empty entailment set (A_c = empty): an item where no offered value is true. SpecDx ties this case to contradiction and hidden-requirement defects and adds the spec anchor.

title: Truth Is a Lie: Crowd Truth and the Seven Myths of Human Annotation
authors: Lora Aroyo; Chris Welty
venue: AI Magazine
subtopics: CrowdTruth; disagreement as signal; seven myths of annotation
summary: Argues that annotation practice rests on the outdated ideal of a single correct truth, dispels seven myths that follow from it, and proposes 'crowd truth': measuring annotations across a crowd captures subjectivity and the range of reasonable interpretations.
relation_to_specdx: It is the philosophical basis for treating disagreement as information about the item, which is SpecDx's core move (spatially concentrated disagreement means a spec defect). SpecDx formalises 'the range of reasonable interpretations' as the entailment set A_c.

title: Community-based bayesian aggregation models for crowdsourcing
authors: Matteo Venanzi; John Guiver; Gabriella Kazai; Pushmeet Kohli; Milad Shokouhi
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd international conference on World wide web
subtopics: community BCC; worker communities; Bayesian aggregation
specdx_components: anchored cell model; family effects/correlated errors
summary: Proposes CommunityBCC, a Bayesian label-aggregation model in which crowd workers belong to a few latent communities that share similar confusion matrices, and reports that it consistently beats prior aggregation methods (from the S2 TLDR; the abstract was not shown).
relation_to_specdx: Communities of raters with shared confusion matrices are the crowd analogue of SpecDx's model families. CBCC infers the communities, whereas SpecDx knows the families, and it uses them to model correlated errors, not to pool accuracy.

title: Fusing data with correlations
authors: Ravali Pochampally; Anish Das Sarma; Xin Luna Dong; Alexandra Meliou; Divesh Srivastava
venue: Proceedings of the 2014 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
subtopics: correlated sources; data fusion; copying beyond
summary: Generalises source dependence beyond copying to arbitrary positive and negative correlations among sources and extractors (e.g. complementary domains, shared extraction errors), and gives fusion algorithms that account for them, outperforming prior methods on real and synthetic data.
relation_to_specdx: Correlated LLM families (shared training data or architecture) are precisely the correlated sources studied here. SpecDx assumes cross-family independence. This paper is the template for modelling or testing that assumption.

title: Ranking and combining multiple predictors without labeled data
authors: Fabio Parisi; Francesco Strino; Boaz Nadler; Yuval Kluger
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
subtopics: spectral meta-learner; ranking advisers without ground truth; cartels
specdx_components: identifiability; family effects/correlated errors; baseline B2
summary: Shows that for conditionally independent binary advisers the off-diagonal covariance is rank-one, which lets one rank advisers and combine their predictions without ground truth (the spectral meta-learner). The method is robust to small cartels of malicious advisers.
relation_to_specdx: It is the founding spectral result on unsupervised rater ranking. 'Cartels' are correlated subgroups, similar to SpecDx's model families. It can rank interpreters for B2 without gold.
baseline_notes: Binarise readings against d_c and run SML (the leading eigenvector of the off-diagonal covariance) to rank models and get an unsupervised consensus. A few lines of numpy. It is a baseline for 'best single interpreter' selection and consensus without anchors.

title: Learning Whom to Trust with MACE
authors: Dirk Hovy; Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick; Ashish Vaswani; Eduard Hovy
venue: Proceedings of the 2013 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies
subtopics: MACE; annotator competence; spammer detection
summary: MACE (Multi-Annotator Competence Estimation) learns without supervision which annotators are trustworthy and predicts the underlying labels, improving both label accuracy and trustworthiness estimates over standard baselines (from the S2 TLDR and metadata; the abstract was not available).
relation_to_specdx: It is the closest classic analogue of SpecDx's competent-reading-or-noise mixture for each rater. SpecDx adds item difficulty, set-valued truth and an anchor, and restricts errors to values outside the entailment set.
baseline_notes: Two implementations are available: crowd-kit MACE (Python) and the original Java tool. Input is a CSV of item rows by annotator columns, so the matrix is cells by models with the spec as an extra column. Competence estimates per model plus the MAP label give a mis-key flag where the label differs from d_c. The entropy of the label posterior can serve as an ambiguity score, comparable to B4.

title: A Bayesian approach to discovering truth from conflicting sources for data integration
authors: Bo Zhao; Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein; Jim Gemmell; Jiawei Han
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment
subtopics: Latent Truth Model; multi-valued truth; false positive/negative source quality; truth discovery
summary: Proposes the Latent Truth Model, an unsupervised Bayesian graphical model that infers true records and source quality for data integration. It models two kinds of source error (false positives and false negatives), so it is the first truth-finding method able to merge multi-valued attributes, and it scales via sampling-based inference.
relation_to_specdx: LTM is the closest data-integration prior art for SpecDx's set-valued truth: each fact (value) is independently true or false, so an entity can have several true values. SpecDx restricts the entailment set to {x}, {x,y} or empty, and adds an anchor source plus item difficulty. LTM has no notion of the spec as a source whose disagreement is diagnostic.
baseline_notes: Treat each (cell, candidate value) as a fact and each model as a source. LTM's per-fact truth posterior yields a set-valued truth per cell: two true values mean ambiguity, no true value among the declared values means a contradiction or hidden-requirement signal. No official code was found; small re-implementations exist (not verified). Re-implementing the collapsed Gibbs sampler takes about 100 lines.

title: How To Grade a Test Without Knowing the Answers — A Bayesian Graphical Model for Adaptive Crowdsourcing and Aptitude Testing
authors: Yoram Bachrach; Thore Graepel; Tom Minka; John Guiver
venue: Proceedings of the 29th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2012)
subtopics: IRT without answer key; ability x difficulty; adaptive testing
specdx_components: item difficulty/IRT; anchored cell model; active synthesis
summary: Proposes a Bayesian graphical model that jointly infers question difficulties, participant abilities and the correct answers in aptitude tests and crowdsourcing, plus an adaptive testing scheme that picks the next question by greedy expected-entropy minimisation, which needs fewer questions.
relation_to_specdx: It is the closest classic model to SpecDx's anchored cell model: IRT-style ability-minus-difficulty with an unknown answer key, and active item selection like SpecDx's Thompson-sampling scenario synthesis. SpecDx adds the declared key as a fallible anchor and allows two-valued or empty keys.
baseline_notes: It is a near-direct ablation of SpecDx (no anchor, single-valued key). Implement in a few dozen lines (or via Infer.NET-style EP; no official code verified) on the cell x model matrix, then flag cells where the inferred key differs from d_c.

title: Semi-supervised truth discovery
authors: Xiaoxin Yin; Wenzhao Tan
venue: Proceedings of the 20th international conference on World wide web
subtopics: semi-supervised truth discovery; ground truth anchors
summary: Proposes semi-supervised truth discovery that uses a small amount of ground-truth data to guide the estimation of true values, with an optimal solution and a convergent iterative algorithm (from the S2 TLDR).
relation_to_specdx: It is the closest truth-discovery analogue of SpecDx's anchors. Here gold facts are trusted, whereas SpecDx's anchor (the declared spec value) is itself fallible and is what is being audited.

title: Identifiability of parameters in latent structure models with many observed variables
authors: Elizabeth S. Allman; Catherine Matias; John A. Rhodes
venue: The Annals of Statistics
subtopics: identifiability; latent class models; Kruskal; generic identifiability
summary: Develops an algebraic approach, built on Kruskal's theorem for three-way arrays, to prove generic identifiability of many latent-structure models (finite mixtures of product distributions, HMMs, random graph mixtures). It shows that classical identifiability is too strong and generic identifiability (non-identifiable set of measure zero) is the right notion.
relation_to_specdx: It is the standard identifiability reference for conditional-independence latent class models with three or more raters. SpecDx's identification arguments (two models with distinct accuracy, or one model plus a known error pool, plus the anchor) are an alternative route for a structured model with set-valued truth, and should be contrasted with the Kruskal/Allman conditions.

title: Integrating conflicting data: the role of source dependence
authors: Xin Luna Dong; Laure Berti-Equille; Divesh Srivastava
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment
subtopics: source dependence; copy detection; truth discovery; Bayesian analysis
summary: Shows that copying between sources spreads false values and defeats majority-based truth discovery. Proposes Bayesian detection of dependence, where sources sharing many rare (especially false) values likely copy, inside an iterative algorithm that jointly discovers truth and dependence, extended with source accuracy and value similarity.
relation_to_specdx: It is the canonical treatment of correlated raters in truth discovery. Shared rare errors between LLMs of one family are exactly 'copying' signals. SpecDx assumes independence across families and could borrow Dong et al.'s dependence test to validate that assumption on its reading matrix.

title: Whose Vote Should Count More: Optimal Integration of Labels from Labelers of Unknown Expertise
authors: Jacob Whitehill; Ting-fan Wu; Jacob Bergsma; Javier R. Movellan; Paul L. Ruvolo
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 22 (NIPS 2009)
subtopics: GLAD; ability x difficulty; item difficulty; adversarial labelers
specdx_components: anchored cell model; item difficulty/IRT; baseline B3
summary: Proposes GLAD, a probabilistic model that jointly infers each image's label, each labeler's expertise and each image's difficulty from multiple noisy binary labels, and shows it beats majority vote and is robust to adversarial and noisy labelers.
relation_to_specdx: GLAD's accuracy term (labeler ability times inverse item difficulty inside a logistic) is the direct ancestor of SpecDx's sigma(alpha_m - beta_g) faithful-reading probability. GLAD assumes one true label per item and has no anchor rater or empty or two-valued truth.
baseline_notes: crowd-kit GLAD on the cell x model reading table (multi-class labels allowed). Use the inferred label versus d_c to flag mis-keys, and use inferred difficulty to rank cells, where very hard cells are candidate ambiguities. It is a direct ablation of SpecDx without set-valued truth and without the anchor. Runs offline.

title: A Cautionary Note on the Robustness of Latent Class Models for Estimating Diagnostic Error without a Gold Standard
authors: Paul S. Albert; Lori E. Dodd
venue: Biometrics
subtopics: conditional dependence misspecification; latent class robustness; no gold standard
summary: Shows that misspecifying the conditional dependence between tests in latent class models biases estimates of sensitivity, specificity and prevalence. With few tests, likelihood comparisons cannot distinguish dependence structures. Gives asymptotics, simulations and practitioner guidelines.
relation_to_specdx: It is a direct warning for SpecDx: if same-family LLM errors are correlated and the model assumes independence, the inferred truth (and so the defect type) can be biased in ways fit statistics cannot detect. This motivates SpecDx's family-level design and its simulation stress tests.

title: Random Effects Models in Latent Class Analysis for Evaluating Accuracy of Diagnostic Tests
authors: Yinsheng Qu; Ming Tan; Michael H. Kutner
venue: Biometrics
subtopics: conditional dependence; random effects latent class; diagnostic tests
summary: Extends two-class latent class models for diagnostic accuracy without an error-free reference by adding random effects that capture conditional dependence among tests or readers, and gives a graphical check for when that dependence matters.
relation_to_specdx: It is the standard way to relax the conditional-independence assumption SpecDx makes across model families. A random family effect is a natural extension, or sensitivity analysis, for SpecDx's family-independence assumption.

title: Conceptual modeling of coincident failures in multiversion software
authors: B. Littlewood; D.R. Miller
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: forced diversity; coincident failures; methodological diversity; multiversion software
summary: Extends the Eckhardt-Lee model with forced (methodological) diversity: formalising methodology as a sequence of decisions, it shows that diverse decisions imply likely diverse behaviour of versions developed under forced diversity (from the S2 TLDR).
relation_to_specdx: It justifies SpecDx's use of diverse model families (different 'methodologies') to decorrelate interpreter errors. | Justifies SpecDx's use of several model families and Tell variants as forced diversity: diverse 'methodologies' reduce coincident errors, so a consensus deviation that survives diversification is more attributable to the specification.

title: Test Theory without an Answer Key
authors: William H. Batchelder; A. Kimball Romney
venue: Psychometrika
subtopics: cultural consensus theory; answer key unknown; test theory
summary: Presents a model for dichotomous items when the answer key is unknown, structurally a two-class latent model with the roles of respondents and items swapped. It develops estimation methods and shows by Monte Carlo that the key can be reconstructed accurately from small groups of respondents.
relation_to_specdx: Cultural consensus theory, i.e. recovering the answer key from competent respondents, is exactly SpecDx's setting with LLMs as respondents. SpecDx differs in starting from a declared key (the spec) that may be wrong, and in allowing set-valued keys.

title: An experimental evaluation of the assumption of independence in multiversion programming
authors: John C. Knight; Nancy G. Leveson
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: N-version programming; correlated failures; independence assumption; empirical study
summary: An experiment in which 27 programmers independently implemented one specification (the Launch Interceptor Program), evaluated on a million test inputs, rejected the hypothesis of independent failures: coincident failures were far more frequent than independence predicts (paraphrased from a search-result abstract summary).
relation_to_specdx: It is the classic evidence that independently built executors of the same spec fail together, often where the spec is hard. SpecDx's committee of LLM interpreters is an N-version system, and SpecDx exploits exactly such coincident deviations as evidence of spec defects while guarding against family-level correlation. | The classic evidence that independently produced interpreters of one specification fail together; SpecDx's assumption of independent errors across model families is exactly what this paper warns against, so SpecDx must model shared difficulty and family effects and test the assumption empirically (e.g. by within- vs across-family error correlation).

title: A Theoretical Basis for the Analysis of Multiversion Software Subject to Coincident Errors
authors: D.E. Eckhardt; L.D. Lee
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: coincident errors; intensity function; multiversion software theory; coincident failures; multiversion software; failure correlation model
specdx_components: family effects/correlated errors; item difficulty/IRT; identifiability
summary: Provides a probabilistic framework for multiversion software subject to coincident errors, centred on an 'intensity of coincident errors' function over the input space that describes the propensity of versions to fail together. It analyses how system failure probability depends on the number of versions N (paraphrased from a search-result abstract summary).
relation_to_specdx: The EL model is the software-engineering ancestor of SpecDx's cell difficulty: input-dependent difficulty induces correlated failures even among independent developers. SpecDx's beta_g plays the role of the intensity function, and a spec defect is the limiting case where every competent version fails at the same input. | The Eckhardt-Lee model explains correlated failures by input difficulty varying over the input space, which is precisely SpecDx's item-difficulty term beta_g: conditional on a cell's difficulty, interpreters can be independent while marginal errors are correlated. SpecDx must distinguish such difficulty-induced coincident errors from specification defects, which is what its accuracy-gradient identifiability argument addresses.

title: Estimating the Error Rates of Diagnostic Tests
authors: S. L. Hui; S. D. Walter
venue: Biometrics
subtopics: diagnostic tests without gold standard; identifiability; two populations
summary: Shows that when two tests are applied simultaneously to individuals from two populations with different disease prevalences, and assuming conditional independence of test errors, maximum likelihood estimates both tests' error rates and both prevalences. It generalises to several tests and populations.
relation_to_specdx: It is the classic proof that fallible raters can be calibrated without gold when an exogenous contrast (different prevalences) exists. SpecDx's 'identification from two models with distinct accuracy' uses a contrast across raters instead of across populations, and the spec anchor plays the role of the imperfect reference test.

title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation of Observer Error-Rates Using the EM Algorithm
authors: A. P. Dawid; A. M. Skene
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C (Applied Statistics)
subtopics: Dawid-Skene; latent class model; EM; confusion matrix
summary: Introduces the latent-class model in which each observer has an unknown class-confusion matrix and the true class of each item is latent, and shows that EM yields maximum-likelihood estimates of observer error rates and true classes without gold labels (motivated by compiling patient records from several clinicians).
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's anchored cell model is a Dawid-Skene descendant: models are observers, cells are items. SpecDx differs in three ways: the truth is a set (A_c in {{x},{x,y},empty}), the specification's declared value is treated as one more fallible rater (the anchor), and per-model accuracy is parameterised by ability minus cell difficulty instead of a free confusion matrix per rater.
baseline_notes: Run crowd-kit DawidSkene on a long table (task=cell id, worker=model id plus a pseudo-worker 'spec' carrying d_c, label=read value). Flag cells whose posterior truth differs from d_c as hidden-requirement or mis-key candidates. It cannot output a two-value truth or an empty truth, so ambiguity and contradiction are invisible to it, and it treats the specification as an ordinary worker. Offline, pip install crowd-kit.

title: Nonparametric Bayesian inference of item-level features in classifier combination
authors: Patrick Stinson; Nikolaus Kriegeskorte
venue: Proceedings of the Forty-first Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: item-level features; Indian Buffet Process; classifier combination; IRT comparison
summary: Develops a Bayesian classifier-combination model that infers latent item features via an Indian Buffet Process, capturing item heterogeneity that affects classifiers, and compares it with IRT and BCC on crowdsourcing and with instance-dependent neural models.
relation_to_specdx: It is a nonparametric generalisation of per-item difficulty. SpecDx's cell-group difficulty beta_g is a parametric special case.

title: A Comparative Study on Annotation Quality of Crowdsourcing and LLm Via Label Aggregation
authors: Jiyi Li
venue: ICASSP 2024 - 2024 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
subtopics: LLM vs crowd annotation; label aggregation; Crowd-LLM hybrid
summary: Builds a benchmark from existing crowdsourcing datasets, compares individual crowd and LLM labels and their aggregates, and proposes a Crowd-LLM hybrid aggregation. Adding labels from good LLMs to crowd data improves the aggregated labels beyond the LLM labels alone.
relation_to_specdx: It treats LLMs as workers inside classic truth-inference models, as SpecDx does. It assumes a correct gold standard for evaluation, whereas SpecDx audits the gold.

title: Bayesian Calibration of Win Rate Estimation with LLM Evaluators
authors: Yicheng Gao; Gonghan Xu; Zhe Wang; Arman Cohan
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
subtopics: Bayesian Dawid-Skene; LLM evaluators; win-rate calibration
summary: Proposes Bayesian Win-Rate Sampling and a Bayesian Dawid-Skene model to correct the inaccuracy and bias of LLM evaluators when estimating win rates between generative models, validated on six datasets covering story generation, summarisation and instruction following.
relation_to_specdx: It applies a Dawid-Skene latent-class model to LLM raters, the same move as SpecDx. Its target is the systems' win rate, not defects in the rubric or specification.

title: Replacing Judges with Juries: Evaluating LLM Generations with a Panel of Diverse Models
authors: Pat Verga; Sebastian Hofstatter; Sophia Althammer; Yixuan Su; Aleksandra Piktus; Arkady Arkhangorodsky; Minjie Xu; Naomi White; Patrick Lewis
venue: arXiv
subtopics: LLM jury; panel of LLM evaluators; intra-model bias
summary: Proposes evaluating LLM outputs with a Panel of LLM evaluators (PoLL) drawn from disjoint model families instead of a single large judge. Across three judge settings and six datasets the panel correlates better with humans, shows less intra-model bias and costs over seven times less.
relation_to_specdx: It motivates SpecDx's multi-family committee. PoLL aggregates by simple voting and assumes the rubric is correct, whereas SpecDx models raters and audits the rubric (spec).

title: Wisdom of the silicon crowd: LLM ensemble prediction capabilities rival human crowd accuracy
authors: Philipp Schoenegger; Indre Tuminauskaite; Peter S. Park; Rafael Valdece Sousa Bastos; Philip E. Tetlock
venue: Science Advances
subtopics: LLM ensemble; wisdom of the silicon crowd; forecasting; LLM ensembles; wisdom of crowds; aggregation
summary: Aggregates probabilistic forecasts from 12 LLMs on 31 binary questions and finds that the LLM crowd beats a no-information benchmark and is statistically indistinguishable from a 925-person human crowd. LLMs show human-like biases, and they improve when shown the human median.
relation_to_specdx: It is empirical support that a diverse population of LLMs behaves like a crowd of fallible raters, the premise of SpecDx's committee. | Evidence that aggregating heterogeneous LLMs yields crowd-like accuracy, supporting SpecDx's population view, while shared biases illustrate correlated errors across families.

title: Identifiability of Label Noise Transition Matrix
authors: Yang Liu; Hao Cheng; Kun Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: identifiability; noise transition matrix; Kruskal; multiple noisy labels
summary: Characterises when the instance-level label-noise transition matrix is identifiable, using Kruskal's theorem to show that multiple noisy labels are necessary, explains existing methods' assumptions, and shows that disentangled features aid identification.
relation_to_specdx: It is a modern Kruskal-based identifiability analysis for fallible labels. SpecDx needs a parallel statement for its anchored, set-valued model.

title: Picking on the Same Person: Does Algorithmic Monoculture Lead to Outcome Homogenization?
authors: Rishi Bommasani; Kathleen A. Creel; Ananya Kumar; Dan Jurafsky; Percy Liang
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35
subtopics: algorithmic monoculture; outcome homogenization; component sharing; correlated errors
summary: Formalises outcome homogenization under algorithmic monoculture and proposes the component-sharing hypothesis: systems sharing training data or models produce more homogeneous outcomes. Shared training data reliably increases homogenization, with mixed results for shared foundation models.
relation_to_specdx: It provides the theory for why LLMs sharing data or architecture (same family) have correlated errors, the risk SpecDx's family-level independence assumption must address. | The ML version of the N-version independence problem: models that share pretraining data or bases fail on the same items, which threatens SpecDx's cross-family independence assumption and motivates measuring family effects.

title: A Permutation-Based Model for Crowd Labeling: Optimal Estimation and Robustness
authors: Nihar B. Shah; Sivaraman Balakrishnan; Martin J. Wainwright
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
subtopics: permutation-based model; minimax rates; generalised Dawid-Skene
summary: Proposes a permutation-based crowd-labelling model that generalises Dawid-Skene (workers and questions ordered by ability and difficulty without parametric form), derives sharp global minimax rates, and gives efficient WAN and OBI-WAN estimators with non-asymptotic guarantees.
relation_to_specdx: It is a nonparametric relaxation of the ability-difficulty structure that SpecDx's sigma(alpha_m - beta_g) imposes parametrically. It is useful for robustness of the identifiability claims.

title: Crowdsourcing via Annotator Co-occurrence Imputation and Provable Symmetric Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
authors: Shahana Ibrahim; Xiao Fu
venue: Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: identifiability; symmetric NMF; co-occurrence; Dawid-Skene
summary: Recasts Dawid-Skene learning from pairwise annotator co-occurrences as symmetric NMF, which has stronger identifiability than coupled NMF. It adds co-occurrence imputation for sparse co-labelling and gives a provable low-complexity algorithm.
relation_to_specdx: It offers a second-order-moment identifiability route for DS, relevant to SpecDx's claim that two models of distinct accuracy suffice under its structured model.

title: Learning from Disagreement: A Survey
authors: Alexandra N. Uma; Tommaso Fornaciari; Dirk Hovy; Silviu Paun; Barbara Plank; Massimo Poesio
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research
subtopics: learning from disagreement; survey; soft labels
summary: Surveys evidence of human disagreement across NLP and vision tasks and the methods for training from multiple, possibly conflicting judgments, comparing them systematically under a common evaluation.
relation_to_specdx: It is the survey anchor for 'disagreement is not noise'. SpecDx uses disagreement diagnostically, to type defects in the spec, rather than as a training signal.

title: Semi-Supervised Aggregation of Dependent Weak Supervision Sources With Performance Guarantees
authors: Alessio Mazzetto; Dylan Sam; Andrew Park; Eli Upfal; Stephen Bach
venue: Proceedings of The 24th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
subtopics: dependent weak labelers; semi-supervised; performance guarantees
specdx_components: family effects/correlated errors; anchored cell model
summary: Gives performance-guaranteed aggregation of weak labelers without assuming independent errors: a small labelled set is used to select subsets of labelers whose majority vote has provably low error, beating semi-supervised Dawid-Skene by about 15 points on hard tasks.
relation_to_specdx: It shows how a few trusted labels (anchors) buy robustness to correlated raters. SpecDx's anchor is untrusted, so its robustness comes from median-breakdown contrasts instead.

title: Inherent Disagreements in Human Textual Inferences
authors: Ellie Pavlick; Tom Kwiatkowski
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
subtopics: inherent disagreement; NLI; plausible readings
summary: Shows that human disagreement about natural language inferences persists with more raters and more context, so it is not just noise, and that current NLI models' uncertainty does not reflect it. Argues for evaluating against the full distribution of plausible judgments.
relation_to_specdx: It supports SpecDx's position that some cells are genuinely two-valued (ambiguity) and should not be forced to a single truth.

title: Learning Dependency Structures for Weak Supervision Models
authors: Paroma Varma; Frederic Sala; Ann He; Alexander Ratner; Christopher Re
venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: dependency structure; robust PCA; weak supervision; sample complexity
summary: Learns weak-supervision source dependencies with a robust-PCA method, with improved recovery rates (sample complexity can be sublinear or logarithmic in the number of sources) and an information-theoretic lower bound, beating independence-assuming label models.
relation_to_specdx: It is an alternative tool for discovering latent family structure among LLM interpreters from the reading matrix.

title: Training Complex Models with Multi-Task Weak Supervision
authors: Alexander Ratner; Braden Hancock; Jared Dunnmon; Frederic Sala; Shreyash Pandey; Christopher Ré
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: MeTaL; multi-task weak supervision; matrix completion; dependency structure
summary: Models weak-supervision sources that have unknown accuracies, correlated outputs and different task granularities as labelling related sub-tasks, and recovers their accuracies via a matrix-completion problem given the dependency structure, without labelled data.
relation_to_specdx: Its identifiability via the inverse covariance with known dependency structure is the analogue of SpecDx's known family structure. Multi-task granularity is like clause-level vs cell-level readings.

title: Truth Inference at Scale: A Bayesian Model for Adjudicating Highly Redundant Crowd Annotations
authors: Yuan Li; Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein; Trevor Cohn
venue: The World Wide Web Conference
subtopics: highly redundant annotation; majority vote competitiveness; Bayesian truth inference
summary: Shows that in highly redundant crowdsourcing (five or more labels per item, mostly good workers) majority vote beats most truth-inference models, and proposes a conjugate Bayesian model with simple EM that is competitive across redundancy regimes.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's committee is highly redundant (many runs per cell), the regime where this paper finds majority vote hard to beat. This motivates SpecDx's majority-vote simulation baseline and its focus on structured truth rather than just reweighting raters.

title: Analysis of Minimax Error Rate for Crowdsourcing and Its Application to Worker Clustering Model
authors: Hideaki Imamura; Issei Sato; Masashi Sugiyama
venue: Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: minimax error rate; worker clustering model
summary: Derives a minimax error rate for a broad class of crowdsourcing models including DS under realistic settings, and proposes a worker clustering model (workers in a cluster share parameters) whose empirical error tracks the derived lower bound.
relation_to_specdx: Clustering workers into groups with shared confusion parameters resembles pooling by model family. SpecDx pools by family for error correlation rather than for accuracy.

title: Crowdsourcing Ground Truth for Medical Relation Extraction
authors: Anca Dumitrache; Lora Aroyo; Chris Welty
venue: ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems
subtopics: CrowdTruth; ambiguity-aware ground truth; medical relation extraction
summary: Applies the CrowdTruth method, which keeps annotator disagreement as a signal of textual ambiguity instead of minimising it, to build a medical relation-extraction dataset, and shows that ambiguity-aware crowd labels can match domain-expert quality for training.
relation_to_specdx: CrowdTruth scores sentence ambiguity from worker disagreement, an early operational analogue of SpecDx's ambiguity detection. SpecDx separates ambiguity from interpreter error using accuracy-dependent signatures, not raw disagreement.
baseline_notes: The CrowdTruth-core metrics (unit quality score, worker quality, annotation quality) on cells as units and models as workers. A low unit-quality cell is an 'ambiguous' candidate and gives a disagreement baseline like B4 but with worker weighting. pip-installable and offline. It does not distinguish ambiguity from hidden requirements and ignores the anchor.

title: Quality Control in Crowdsourcing: A Survey of Quality Attributes, Assessment Techniques, and Assurance Actions
authors: Florian Daniel; Pavel Kucherbaev; Cinzia Cappiello; Boualem Benatallah; Mohammad Allahbakhsh
venue: ACM Computing Surveys
subtopics: crowdsourcing quality control; gold questions; assurance actions; survey
summary: Surveys quality in crowdsourcing: it derives a quality model of task quality attributes, catalogues assessment techniques (including gold or control questions and agreement) and assurance actions, and identifies open challenges.
relation_to_specdx: It is the reference for the gold-item and quality-control practices that SpecDx's anchors generalise. In SpecDx the 'gold' is the spec, which is itself under test.

title: A solution to the single-question crowd wisdom problem
authors: Dražen Prelec; H. Sebastian Seung; John McCoy
venue: Nature
subtopics: surprisingly popular; crowd wisdom; majority can be wrong
summary: Shows that democratic voting is biased toward shallow, widely shared information. It proposes selecting the answer that is more popular than people predict (the 'surprisingly popular' principle), which recovers the best answer under reasonable assumptions where majority or confidence rules fail, even for a single question.
relation_to_specdx: It is a reminder that majority agreement need not be truth. SpecDx uses accuracy-gradient signatures (how answers shift with interpreter competence), a related signal for when the majority reading differs from the competent reading.

title: A Survey on Truth Discovery
authors: Yaliang Li; Jing Gao; Chuishi Meng; Qi Li; Lu Su; Bo Zhao; Wei Fan; Jiawei Han
venue: ACM SIGKDD Explorations Newsletter
subtopics: truth discovery survey
summary: Surveys truth discovery methods, which integrate conflicting multi-source data by jointly estimating source reliability and truths. It organises them along several dimensions and discusses future directions.
relation_to_specdx: It is a survey anchor for the truth-discovery side of SpecDx's anchored cell model.

title: Empowering Truth Discovery with Multi-Truth Prediction
authors: Xianzhi Wang; Quan Z. Sheng; Lina Yao; Xue Li; Xiu Susie Fang; Xiaofei Xu; Boualem Benatallah
venue: Proceedings of the 25th ACM International on Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
subtopics: multi-truth discovery; number of truths
summary: Notes that most truth discovery assumes exactly one true value per item. It proposes a generic framework that augments existing truth discovery methods to predict a varying number of true values per item (multi-truth), using the number of truths as a key clue.
relation_to_specdx: Predicting the cardinality of the truth set is SpecDx's {x} vs {x,y} vs empty decision. SpecDx does it with an explicit generative model and anchor, not a wrapper.

title: Estimating Accuracy from Unlabeled Data: A Bayesian Approach
authors: Emmanouil Antonios Platanios; Avinava Dubey; Tom Mitchell
venue: Proceedings of The 33rd International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: accuracy estimation from unlabeled data; Bayesian; nonparametric
summary: Estimates classifiers' true accuracies from unlabelled data with a simple graphical model and two nonparametric extensions, giving estimates within a few percent of truth and better combined predictions.
relation_to_specdx: It shares the goal of estimating interpreter accuracy without labels. SpecDx adds the spec anchor and set-valued truth, and its object of interest is the spec, not the classifiers.

title: Exact Exponent in Optimal Rates for Crowdsourcing
authors: Chao Gao; Yu Lu; Dengyong Zhou
venue: Proceedings of The 33rd International Conference on Machine Learning
subtopics: minimax error rate; Chernoff information; Dawid-Skene
summary: Under Dawid-Skene, establishes matching upper and lower bounds on the optimal crowdsourcing error rate with exact exponent m times the workers' average Chernoff information, which yields a precise sample-size requirement and optimality of EM given good initialisation.
relation_to_specdx: It gives the information-theoretic limit for how many models are needed per cell. SpecDx's committee size and escalation thresholds can be justified against this exponent.

title: Knowledge-based trust: estimating the trustworthiness of web sources
authors: Xin Luna Dong; Evgeniy Gabrilovich; Kevin Murphy; Van Dang; Wilko Horn; Camillo Lugaresi; Shaohua Sun; Wei Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment
subtopics: knowledge-based trust; extraction vs source errors; multi-layer model
summary: Proposes Knowledge-Based Trust: estimate web-source trustworthiness from the correctness of facts it provides, using a multi-layer probabilistic model that separates errors made by the extractors from factual errors in the sources, applied to 2.8B extracted facts.
relation_to_specdx: Its two-layer separation (extractor error vs source error) is analogous to SpecDx's separation of interpreter error from specification defect.

title: Budget-Optimal Task Allocation for Reliable Crowdsourcing Systems
authors: David R. Karger; Sewoong Oh; Devavrat Shah
venue: Operations Research
subtopics: budget-optimal task allocation; crowdsourcing theory; budget allocation; crowdsourcing; task assignment; iterative inference
specdx_components: active synthesis; identifiability; anchored cell model
summary: Journal version of the KOS work: it poses the problem of minimising total task assignments for a target reliability and gives assignment and inference algorithms proven asymptotically optimal, outperforming majority voting.
relation_to_specdx: It provides theory for how many fallible raters per item are needed, comparable to SpecDx's Hoeffding sample-size reasoning per cell. | Budget-optimal allocation of noisy raters to items; SpecDx's committee size per cell and the pilot-then-escalate rule are an adaptive answer to the same question, with LLM families as workers and specification cells as tasks.

title: Resolving conflicts in heterogeneous data by truth discovery and source reliability estimation
authors: Qi Li; Yaliang Li; Jing Gao; Bo Zhao; Wei Fan; Jiawei Han
venue: Proceedings of the 2014 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
subtopics: CRH; heterogeneous truth discovery; optimisation framework
summary: Proposes CRH, an optimisation framework that treats truths and source reliabilities as unknowns and minimises the reliability-weighted deviation between truths and multi-source observations, handling heterogeneous data types (categorical and continuous) jointly.
relation_to_specdx: Database cells are heterogeneous (categorical, numeric), like CRH's objects. CRH gives a loss-based alternative to SpecDx's likelihood model but has single-valued truth and no anchor.

title: Tensor Decompositions for Learning Latent Variable Models
authors: Animashree Anandkumar; Rong Ge; Daniel Hsu; Sham M. Kakade; Matus Telgarsky
venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research
subtopics: tensor decomposition; method of moments; latent variable models
summary: Gives a computationally and statistically efficient moment-based estimator for latent variable models (GMMs, HMMs, LDA) by reducing estimation to an orthogonal decomposition of a symmetric tensor built from low-order moments, with a robust tensor power method and perturbation analysis.
relation_to_specdx: It is the general method-of-moments machinery behind spectral Dawid-Skene. SpecDx's identification arguments sit beside this third-order-moment route.

title: The Benefits of a Model of Annotation
authors: Rebecca J. Passonneau; Bob Carpenter
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
subtopics: models of annotation; agreement coefficients vs probabilistic models; word sense
summary: Argues that inter-annotator agreement coefficients are neither necessary nor sufficient for corpus quality. A probabilistic annotation model applied to crowdsourced word-sense labels gives a certainty for each gold label at less than half the cost of trained annotators.
relation_to_specdx: It supports SpecDx's choice of a generative rater model over agreement statistics, e.g. B4 entropy. SpecDx extends such a model with an anchor and a set-valued truth.

title: Scoring Workers in Crowdsourcing: How Many Control Questions are Enough?
authors: Qiang Liu; Alex Ihler; Mark Steyvers
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
subtopics: control questions; gold items; worker scoring
summary: Analyses how many control items with known answers to give each crowd worker when budgets are limited. More control items score workers better but leave fewer target items, and the paper derives the optimal number for consensus estimation of continuous quantities.
relation_to_specdx: It is the gold-item theory behind anchors. In SpecDx the anchor (d_c) is not known to be correct, so anchor-based contrasts use a robust median (breakdown 1/2) rather than trusted control items.

title: Bayesian Classifier Combination
authors: Hyun-Chul Kim; Zoubin Ghahramani
venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2012), PMLR 22
subtopics: IBCC; Bayesian classifier combination; Dawid-Skene; MCMC
summary: Develops Bayesian classifier combination: a framework that models each base classifier's or human assessor's output given the unknown true label, starting from Dawid-Skene and adding richer structure via MCMC. It needs neither probabilistic nor independent base models, nor a correct one, and gives interpretable diagnostics.
relation_to_specdx: It is the Bayesian Dawid-Skene (IBCC) that SpecDx's MAP/EM fit with Dirichlet priors resembles. IBCC has no anchor rater, no item difficulty and no set-valued truth.

title: Learning from the Wisdom of Crowds by Minimax Entropy
authors: Dengyong Zhou; Sumit Basu; Yi Mao; John C. Platt
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
subtopics: minimax entropy; item confusability; worker expertise
summary: Proposes a minimax entropy principle: maximise entropy over a worker-item-label distribution to infer item confusability and worker expertise, then minimise it to infer ground truth (equivalently minimising KL to the unknown truth), optimised by coordinate descent.
relation_to_specdx: Item confusability is a richer version of SpecDx's cell difficulty, and item-specific confusion is how ambiguity looks under single-truth models. SpecDx instead makes ambiguity an explicit two-valued truth.

title: Truth finding on the deep web: is the problem solved?
authors: Xian Li; Xin Luna Dong; Kenneth Lyons; Weiyi Meng; Divesh Srivastava
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment
subtopics: data fusion evaluation; deep web; conflicting data
summary: Measures the truthfulness of Deep Web data in the Stock and Flight domains, finds large inconsistency and some low-accuracy sources, and evaluates state-of-the-art fusion methods, analysing their strengths and limitations.
relation_to_specdx: It provides empirical evidence that 'trusted' sources are often inconsistent, and an evaluation template (fusion methods on real conflicting data) that SpecDx mirrors with LLM interpreters on specifications.

title: Iterative Learning for Reliable Crowdsourcing Systems
authors: David R. Karger; Sewoong Oh; Devavrat Shah
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
subtopics: KOS; budget-optimal crowdsourcing; message passing
summary: Studies minimising the number of task assignments needed for a target reliability, and gives a task-assignment scheme and an iterative inference algorithm that beat majority voting and are asymptotically optimal against an oracle that knows worker reliabilities.
relation_to_specdx: The KOS algorithm is a standard simulation baseline (it is in crowd-kit). Budget-optimal assignment parallels SpecDx's pilot-then-committee escalation.

title: Learning From Crowds
authors: Vikas C. Raykar; Shipeng Yu; Linda H. Zhao; Gerardo Hermosillo Valadez; Charles Florin; Luca Bogoni; Linda Moy
venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research
subtopics: learning from crowds; annotator sensitivity/specificity; EM
summary: Gives a probabilistic EM approach for supervised learning from several annotators' noisy labels without a gold standard, jointly estimating annotator quality, the hidden true labels and a classifier, and outperforming majority voting.
relation_to_specdx: It is the canonical learning-from-crowds model. SpecDx shares the joint estimation of rater quality and latent truth, but it has no features or classifier, because the items are specification cells and the truth may be a set.

title: Quality management on Amazon Mechanical Turk
authors: Panagiotis G. Ipeirotis; Foster Provost; Jing Wang
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGKDD Workshop on Human Computation
subtopics: worker quality; bias vs error; gold data integration
summary: Improves Dawid-Skene-style worker quality estimation by separating systematic bias (recoverable by relabelling) from error, incorporating cost-sensitive errors, and integrating unsupervised estimation with supervised gold data (from the S2 TLDR).
relation_to_specdx: Separating correctable bias from noise parallels SpecDx's distinction between consistent deviation (spec defect) and scattered error (interpreter error). It also mixes gold and unsupervised data like SpecDx's anchors.

title: The Multidimensional Wisdom of Crowds
authors: Peter Welinder; Steve Branson; Pietro Perona; Serge J. Belongie
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
subtopics: multidimensional annotator model; schools of thought; item embedding
summary: Models images in an abstract Euclidean space and annotators as multidimensional entities with competence, expertise and bias, recovering groups of annotators with different skills ('schools of thought') and groups of images that differ qualitatively.
relation_to_specdx: 'Schools of thought' among annotators is the crowd analogue of several reasonable readings of a requirement (ambiguity) and of family-specific reading styles. SpecDx encodes ambiguity explicitly as A_c = {x, y}.

title: A review of solutions for diagnostic accuracy studies with an imperfect or missing reference standard
authors: Johannes B. Reitsma; Anne W.S. Rutjes; Khalid S. Khan; Arri Coomarasamy; Patrick M. Bossuyt
venue: Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
subtopics: imperfect reference standard; diagnostic accuracy; review
summary: Systematically reviews solutions for diagnostic-accuracy studies whose reference standard is imperfect or missing, grouped into imputation or adjustment for missing references, correction for an imperfect reference, constructing a reference from multiple tests (rule, consensus or latent class), and validation against clinical outcomes.
relation_to_specdx: The specification is an imperfect reference standard. This review maps the classical options and shows that SpecDx belongs to the 'construct the reference by statistical modelling' group, with the imperfect reference kept as an anchor.

title: Get another label? improving data quality and data mining using multiple, noisy labelers
authors: Victor S. Sheng; Foster Provost; Panagiotis G. Ipeirotis
venue: Proceedings of the 14th ACM SIGKDD international conference on Knowledge discovery and data mining

SpecDx's sequential escalation (pilot, then full committee) is a targeted version of 'get another label'. | Justifies SpecDx's sequential escalation: run one model per family as a pilot and spend the full committee only on cells whose pilot readings are uncertain. SpecDx adds an anchor (the declared value) and seeks specification defects rather than training labels.

title: Truth Discovery with Multiple Conflicting Information Providers on the Web
authors: Xiaoxin Yin; Jiawei Han; P.S. Yu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
subtopics: truth discovery; TruthFinder; source trustworthiness
summary: Defines the Veracity problem, finding true facts among conflicting information that many websites provide, and proposes TruthFinder, which exploits mutual reinforcement: a site is trustworthy if it provides many true facts, and a fact is likely true if many trustworthy sites provide it. It finds true facts and trustworthy sites better than popular search engines (journal version of the KDD 2007 paper, DOI 10.1145/1281192.1281309).
relation_to_specdx: It is the founding paper of truth discovery in data integration: sources are like LLM interpreters and facts are like cell values. SpecDx adds an anchor source (the spec) whose disagreements are themselves the diagnostic target.

venue: Linear Algebra and its Applications

summary: Defines rank for three-way arrays and proves lower bounds on it and conditions under which a trilinear (triad) decomposition is unique, with applications to arithmetic complexity and statistics.
