baseline_notes: Structural analogue rather than runnable baseline: its CCG lexicon is specific to networking RFCs and English. | Domain-specific CCG parser for RFC text; not reusable on business specifications.

title: Rapid quality assurance with Requirements Smells
authors: Henning Femmer; Daniel Méndez Fernández; Stefan Wagner; Sebastian Eder
venue: Journal of Systems and Software
subtopics: requirements smells; defect detection; static analysis
summary: Transfers code smells to requirements as Requirements Smells and implements a lightweight static detector (Smella); in three industrial cases and one academic case it reaches on average 59% precision and 82% recall, as a supplement to reviews.
relation_to_specdx: The canonical static, rule-based reading of T for quality defects. SpecDx differs by detecting defects relative to C and to behaviour (e.g. a vague phrase matters only if executors diverge on a checked cell), and by distinguishing spec defects from reader error.

title: Identifying Nocuous Ambiguities in Natural Language Requirements
authors: Francis Chantree; Bashar Nuseibeh; Anne de Roeck; Alistair Willis
venue: 14th IEEE International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE'06)
subtopics: ambiguity; nocuous ambiguity; human judgements
summary: Introduces nocuous versus innocuous ambiguity: an ambiguity is nocuous when human readers disagree on its reading, judged from the distribution of multiple human interpretations, and heuristics are trained to predict this for coordination ambiguities in requirements.
relation_to_specdx: The closest conceptual ancestor of SpecDx's ambiguity signal: ambiguity is defined by disagreement in a population of readers. SpecDx replaces human judgements with a population of LLM executors and models reading accuracy, so that disagreement due to reader error is separated from genuine multiple entailment.

title: Reasoning about inconsistencies in natural language requirements
authors: Vincenzo Gervasi; Didar Zowghi
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
subtopics: inconsistency; default reasoning; NL parsing; theorem proving; model checking
summary: Integrates NL parsing with nonmonotonic default reasoning to discover inconsistencies among requirements from multiple stakeholders, using theorem proving and model checking, implemented in the CARL prototype.
relation_to_specdx: The classic pipeline NL requirements -> logic -> automatic inconsistency discovery. SpecDx does not translate T into logic; it uses C as the logic and treats T only through the behaviour of interpreters.

title: From Contract Drafting to Software Specification: Linguistic Sources of Ambiguity
authors: Daniel M. Berry; Erik Kamsties; Michael M. Krieger
venue: Self-published handbook, University of Waterloo (Version 1.0, November 2003)
subtopics: ambiguity; linguistic ambiguity; foundations
summary: A handbook on unintended ambiguity in software requirements specifications and legal contracts, cataloguing linguistic sources (quantifiers such as all/each/every, only/also/even placement, and/or precedence, that/which, plurals, pronouns) with strategies for avoiding and detecting them. It frames ambiguity as text that admits several interpretations, so that different implementers build interfacing code under different assumptions.
relation_to_specdx: Supplies SpecDx's definition of Ambiguity (T admits two or more readings) and the motivating mechanism (different implementers diverge). SpecDx operationalises it empirically: divergent readings are observed in executions by a population of interpreters rather than detected by a human inspector using linguistic patterns.

title: Clarity Is Not Assumed: Understanding LLM-Based Code Generation under Ambiguous Requirements
authors: Di Yang; Xinou Xie; Xiuwen Yang; Ming Hu; Yihao Huang; Yueling Zhang; Weikai Miao; Ting Su; Chengcheng Wan; Geguang Pu
venue: Proceedings of the 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: ambiguity; benchmark; LLM code generation; divergent implementations
summary: Orchid is a benchmark of 1,304 function-level tasks with lexical, syntactic, semantic and vagueness ambiguity; ambiguity degrades all evaluated LLMs, most strongly the advanced ones, which frequently produce functionally divergent implementations and do not detect or resolve the ambiguity themselves.
relation_to_specdx: Empirical support for SpecDx's premise that ambiguous text produces divergent executions; it measures the effect on interpreters rather than diagnosing the specification.

title: Human-AI Collaboration in Requirements Engineering: Evidence of the Negative Effect of LLMs on Requirements Inspection
authors: Giovanna Broccia; Julian Frattini; Chetan Arora; Maurice H. ter Beek; Alessandro Fantechi; Andreas Vogelsang; Alessio Ferrari
venue: arXiv
subtopics: requirements inspection; LLM assistance; controlled experiment; smells
summary: Controlled experiment with 34 participants inspecting specifications with and without LLM support: LLM support lowers smell-detection accuracy, does not change classification or duration, and may impede learning of inspection skills.
relation_to_specdx: Evidence that static LLM review of requirements (B1-style) is unreliable even with a human in the loop, supporting SpecDx's choice of behaviour-grounded, check-arbitrated diagnosis.

title: When Prompts Go Wrong: Evaluating Code Model Robustness to Ambiguous, Contradictory, and Incomplete Task Descriptions
authors: Maya Larbi; Amal Akli; Mike Papadakis; Rihab Bouyousfi; Maxime Cordy; Federica Sarro; Yves Le Traon
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering
subtopics: robustness; ambiguity; contradiction; incompleteness; mutation of task descriptions
summary: Extends code-generation benchmarks by systematically mutating task descriptions to be ambiguous, contradictory or incomplete, and finds that even minor flaws cause notable performance drops, contradictions most of all, with larger models more resilient but still vulnerable.
relation_to_specdx: Uses specification mutation operators for ambiguity, contradiction and incompleteness, as SpecDx's evaluation does, but to stress interpreters instead of to evaluate a defect detector.

title: Detecting Defects in Natural Language Requirements Specifications
authors: Daniel M. Berry; Erik Kamsties; Cristina Ribeiro; Sri Fatimah Tjong
venue: Handbook on Natural Language Processing for Requirements Engineering
subtopics: defect detection; ambiguity; requirements specifications; handbook
summary: Handbook chapter on detecting defects (notably ambiguity) in natural-language requirements specifications.
relation_to_specdx: Up-to-date overview of static defect detection in NL specifications, the family SpecDx's B1 belongs to.

title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Requirements Engineering (RE): A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Mohammad Amin Zadenoori; Jacek Dąbrowski; Waad Alhoshan; Liping Zhao; Alessio Ferrari
venue: arXiv
subtopics: survey; LLM4RE; systematic literature review
summary: Systematic literature review of 74 LLM4RE studies (2023-2024): most target elicitation and validation, use GPT models with zero/few-shot prompting, and are evaluated in controlled rather than industrial settings.
relation_to_specdx: Maps LLM4RE validation work, all of which reviews requirement text statically; none executes a specification with a population of agents.

title: On the Impact of Requirements Smells in Prompts: The Case of Automated Traceability
authors: Andreas Vogelsang; Alexander Korn; Giovanna Broccia; Alessio Ferrari; Jannik Fischbach; Chetan Arora
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM 47th International Conference on Software Engineering: New Ideas and Emerging Results (ICSE-NIER)
subtopics: requirements smells; LLM prompts; traceability; effect of defects on LLMs
summary: Tests whether requirements smells in prompts affect LLM-based trace-link generation with two LLMs: smells have a small significant effect on predicting whether a requirement is implemented but none on line-level tracing.
relation_to_specdx: Evidence that textual smells do not uniformly change LLM behaviour, supporting SpecDx's choice to define defects by behavioural impact rather than by smell presence.

title: Requirements Ambiguity Detection and Explanation with LLMS: An Industrial Study
authors: Sarmad Bashir; Alessio Ferrari; Abbas Khan; Per Erik Strandberg; Zulqarnain Haider; Mehrdad Saadatmand; Markus Bohlin
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance and Evolution (ICSME)
subtopics: ambiguity; LLM; in-context learning; explanation; industrial
summary: Evaluates LLMs with in-context learning for detecting and explaining ambiguity in three industrial requirement datasets; 10-shot prompting improves classification by about 20% over zero-shot, and experts rate the generated explanations.
relation_to_specdx: A modern instance of B1 (static LLM review for ambiguity). SpecDx reports ambiguity only where readings change checked behaviour and gives the competing readings as executed alternatives.

title: Using Large Language Models for Natural Language Processing Tasks in Requirements Engineering: A Systematic Guideline
authors: Andreas Vogelsang; Jannik Fischbach
venue: Handbook on Natural Language Processing for Requirements Engineering
subtopics: LLM4RE; guidelines; model selection
summary: Chapter introducing how LLMs work and giving a systematic guideline for selecting and adapting LLMs (prompting, fine-tuning, architectures) to NLP4RE tasks.
relation_to_specdx: Methodological reference for designing the B1 static LLM-review baseline fairly.

title: Validating Network Protocol Parsers with Traceable RFC Document Interpretation
authors: Mingwei Zheng; Danning Xie; Qingkai Shi; Chengpeng Wang; Xiangyu Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering
subtopics: protocol specifications; RFC; LLM quasi-oracle; traceability; parser validation
summary: Translates RFC documents into formal message specifications with LLMs and uses them as a quasi-oracle to validate protocol parsers; validation results refine the oracle, and every discrepancy is traced back to the RFC to decide whether it is LLM hallucination or an implementation bug; 69 bugs found (36 confirmed) in nine protocols.
relation_to_specdx: Faces SpecDx's attribution problem in the other direction: a discrepancy may come from the LLM reader or from the artefact. It resolves it by tracing and refinement for one LLM; SpecDx resolves it statistically over a multi-family population with the spec as an anchor.

title: Automated Smell Detection and Recommendation in Natural Language Requirements
authors: Alvaro Veizaga; Seung Yeob Shin; Lionel C. Briand
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: requirements smells; controlled natural language; recommendation; financial domain
summary: Paska detects quality smells in arbitrary NL requirements and recommends rewrites using patterns of the controlled natural language Rimay; on 2,725 annotated requirements from 13 financial systems it reaches 89% precision and recall for smells.
relation_to_specdx: State-of-the-art static smell detection; it does not consult checks C and cannot tell whether a smell causes divergent behaviour.

title: Hermes: Unlocking Security Analysis of Cellular Network Protocols by Synthesizing Finite State Machines from Natural Language Specifications
authors: Abdullah Al Ishtiaq; Sarkar Snigdha Sarathi Das; Syed Md Mukit Rashid; Ali Ranjbar; Kai Tu; Tianwei Wu; Zhezheng Song; Weixuan Wang; Mujtahid Akon; Rui Zhang; Syed Rafiul Hussain
venue: 33rd USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 24)
subtopics: protocol specifications; 3GPP; FSM synthesis; formal analysis
summary: Hermes extracts transition components from cellular specifications with a neural constituency parser (NEUTREX), translates them to logical formulas through a DSL, and compiles FSMs for formal security analysis; 81-87% accuracy on 4G NAS, 5G NAS and 5G RRC, uncovering 3 new vulnerabilities and 7 baseband deviations.
relation_to_specdx: NL specification to formal model to analysis; SpecDx skips the single extracted model and treats each LLM executor as a sampled interpretation of T.

title: Improving requirements completeness: automated assistance through large language models
authors: Dipeeka Luitel; Shabnam Hassani; Mehrdad Sabetzadeh
venue: Requirements Engineering
subtopics: incompleteness; BERT; masked language model
summary: Uses BERT's masked language model as an external knowledge source to predict terminology missing from requirements; withholding content simulates incompleteness, and an ML filter removes noisy predictions.
relation_to_specdx: Incompleteness of T relative to world knowledge; SpecDx's Hidden requirement type is incompleteness of T relative to C (C demands something T does not say), detected by consistent deviation of competent executors.

title: Lessons from the Use of Natural Language Inference (NLI) in Requirements Engineering Tasks
authors: Mohamad Fazelnia; Viktoria Koscinski; Spencer Herzog; Mehdi Mirakhorli
venue: 2024 IEEE 32nd International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
subtopics: natural language inference; conflict detection; specification defects; zero-shot
summary: Evaluates natural language inference (NLI) for requirements classification, specification-defect identification and detection of conflicts between stakeholders' requirements, and finds NLI beats classical NLP, prompt-based, transfer-learning and chatbot LLM baselines, including zero-shot.
relation_to_specdx: Pairwise entailment/contradiction between requirement sentences is the text-level version of SpecDx's entailment sets; SpecDx defines entailment of a cell value by T through executions and contradiction through C.
baseline_notes: Would label pairs of requirement sentences as contradiction/entailment/neutral. Input: sentence pairs. Adaptation: run an off-the-shelf multilingual NLI model (e.g. an XNLI-trained model covering Vietnamese) over all sentence pairs of the BA documents and the τ² policy and report contradictions; cheap, offline, and language-capable. Code: none released with the paper; standard NLI models suffice.

title: Leveraging LLMs for the Quality Assurance of Software Requirements
authors: Sebastian Lubos; Alexander Felfernig; Thi Ngoc Trang Tran; Damian Garber; Merfat El Mansi; Seda Polat Erdeniz; Viet-Man Le
venue: 2024 IEEE 32nd International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
subtopics: LLM; ISO 29148; quality assessment; requirement improvement
summary: Uses an LLM to assess software requirements against the ISO 29148 quality characteristics, explain its judgements and propose improved requirements, validated in a study with software engineers.
relation_to_specdx: A direct, simple instance of B1 (static LLM review). SpecDx's contrast: judgements are grounded in executions and arbitrated by C, not in the reviewer's opinion.
baseline_notes: Would score each requirement sentence on ISO 29148 characteristics (unambiguous, consistent, complete, ...). Input: requirement sentences. Adaptation: prompt local models per sentence of the Vietnamese BA documents and the τ² policy (prompt in English, text in Vietnamese; LLMs handle Vietnamese), then map 'ambiguous'/'inconsistent'/'incomplete' to SpecDx types; this is the minimal published B1 and is easy to reimplement. Code: none.

title: Towards an automatic contradiction detection in requirements engineering
authors: Alexander Elenga Gärtner; Dietmar Göhlich
venue: Proceedings of the Design Society
subtopics: contradiction detection; formal logic + LLM; GPT-3
summary: Three-phase hybrid contradiction detection: identify conditionals and pseudo-grammatical elements in requirements, then use GPT-3 for nuanced contradiction detection; on an electric-bus project it reports 99% accuracy and 60% recall.
relation_to_specdx: Predecessor of ALICE; static text-level contradiction detection, versus SpecDx's behaviour-level contradictions among checks.

title: AI-based Question Answering Assistance for Analyzing Natural-language Requirements
authors: Saad Ezzini; Sallam Abualhaija; Chetan Arora; Mehrdad Sabetzadeh
venue: 2023 IEEE/ACM 45th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: question answering; incompleteness; inconsistency; LLM
summary: QAssist answers stakeholders' questions about an NL requirements specification by retrieving passages from the specification and from mined external domain knowledge, then extracting answers with language-model QA (answer localisation recall about 90-97%, extraction accuracy 84%).
relation_to_specdx: Interrogating T with a language model to expose incompleteness is close in spirit to running interpreters on T; SpecDx asks behavioural questions (scenarios) and compares the answers with C rather than relying on a human to judge them.

title: Leveraging Natural Language Processing for a Consistency Checking Toolchain of Automotive Requirements
authors: Vincent Bertram; Hendrik Kausch; Evgeny Kusmenko; Haron Nqiri; Bernhard Rumpe; Constantin Venhoff
venue: 2023 IEEE 31st International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
subtopics: consistency checking; LLM to structured English; SMT; scenario generation; automotive
summary: Translates automotive NL requirements into Structured English with few-shot LLMs (OptKATE for example selection), then into TCTL for Z3-based consistency analysis, and generates scenarios to check requirements whose preconditions conflict.
relation_to_specdx: Combines LLM translation, SMT consistency checking and scenario generation, a pipeline near SpecDx's components; SpecDx generates scenarios to maximise information about which clauses or sentences are defective and executes them with interpreters rather than a solver over a translated model.

title: Requirements quality research: a harmonized theory, evaluation, and roadmap
authors: Julian Frattini; Lloyd Montgomery; Jannik Fischbach; Daniel Mendez; Davide Fucci; Michael Unterkalmsteiner
venue: Requirements Engineering
subtopics: requirements quality theory; impact; roadmap
summary: Research commentary proposing a harmonised theory of requirements quality, evaluating the field and setting a roadmap; it finds that research focuses on normative rules and rarely connects quality defects to their impact on downstream activities.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx answers this critique directly: a defect is defined by its impact on the behaviour of executors that use the requirements (activity-based quality), not by a normative rule.

title: Automated Attack Synthesis by Extracting Finite State Machines from Protocol Specification Documents
authors: Maria Leonor Pacheco; Max von Hippel; Ben Weintraub; Dan Goldwasser; Cristina Nita-Rotaru
venue: 2022 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
subtopics: protocol specifications; RFC; FSM extraction; attacker synthesis
summary: RFCNLP extracts protocol finite-state machines from RFC prose with a data-driven pipeline (technical word representations, zero-shot mapping of text to a protocol-independent intermediate language, rule-based FSM extraction) and uses them for automated attacker synthesis.
relation_to_specdx: Turns NL specifications into an executable model to find problems; SpecDx keeps T in NL and executes it through interpreters instead of committing to one extracted model.

title: Automated handling of anaphoric ambiguity in requirements: a multi-solution study
authors: Saad Ezzini; Sallam Abualhaija; Chetan Arora; Mehrdad Sabetzadeh
venue: Proceedings of the 44th International Conference on Software Engineering
subtopics: ambiguity; anaphoric ambiguity; SpanBERT; ML
summary: Compares six NLP/ML solutions for anaphoric ambiguity detection and anaphora resolution on about 1,350 industrial requirements; supervised ML is best for detection (precision about 60%, recall 100%) and SpanBERT for resolution (about 98%).
relation_to_specdx: A static text detector for one ambiguity source; SpecDx detects ambiguity only when it changes executed behaviour, regardless of its linguistic source, and needs no labelled training data.

title: DocTer: documentation-guided fuzzing for testing deep learning API functions
authors: Danning Xie; Yitong Li; Mijung Kim; Hung Viet Pham; Lin Tan; Xiangyu Zhang; Michael W. Godfrey
venue: Proceedings of the 31st ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
subtopics: API documentation; constraint extraction; fuzzing; deep learning libraries
summary: DocTer automatically constructs dependency-parse rules to extract DL-specific input constraints from free-form API documentation and uses them to guide fuzzing of deep-learning library APIs, finding bugs including documentation-implementation mismatches.
relation_to_specdx: Uses constraints read from NL docs to synthesise valid and boundary inputs, much as SpecDx takes boundary values from the clauses of C to synthesise scenarios.

title: Empirical research on requirements quality: a systematic mapping study
authors: Lloyd Montgomery; Davide Fucci; Abir Bouraffa; Lisa Scholz; Walid Maalej
venue: Requirements Engineering
subtopics: survey; requirements quality; mapping study; quality attributes
summary: Systematic mapping of 105 empirical studies on requirements quality: 12 quality attributes and 111 sub-types are identified, the most studied being ambiguity, completeness, consistency and correctness, with few evidence-based definitions.
relation_to_specdx: Confirms that ambiguity, incompleteness and inconsistency are the dominant defect classes, matching SpecDx's types; SpecDx adds satisfaction-based definitions tied to executable checks.

title: TAPHSIR: towards AnaPHoric ambiguity detection and ReSolution in requirements
authors: Saad Ezzini; Sallam Abualhaija; Chetan Arora; Mehrdad Sabetzadeh
venue: Proceedings of the 30th ACM Joint European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering
subtopics: ambiguity; anaphoric ambiguity; tool
summary: Tool demo of TAPHSIR, which flags pronoun occurrences in requirements as ambiguous or not with ML and interprets them with a BERT variant; released on Zenodo.
relation_to_specdx: Runnable static anaphora-ambiguity detector; applicable only to English requirement statements and to pronoun ambiguity, while SpecDx localises behaviour-relevant ambiguity in any sentence of T by ddmin with an LLM-population oracle.
baseline_notes: Detects pronoun (anaphoric) ambiguity per requirement sentence. Input: English requirement sentences. Adaptation: run on the English τ² policy sentences (and machine-translated Vietnamese BA documents) and compare flagged sentences with SpecDx's ddmin-localised ambiguous sentences. Code: Zenodo artefact doi 10.5281/zenodo.5902117 (stated in the abstract; no GitHub repository found); English only; no Vietnamese model.

title: Bookworm Game: Automatic Discovery of LTE Vulnerabilities Through Documentation Analysis
authors: Yi Chen; Yepeng Yao; XiaoFeng Wang; Dandan Xu; Chang Yue; Xiaozhong Liu; Kai Chen; Haixu Tang; Baoxu Liu
venue: 2021 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
subtopics: protocol specifications; LTE; hazard indicators; test generation
summary: Bookworm Game analyses the LTE NAS specification with NLP to find hazard indicators (security-relevant, loosely specified statements) and automatically builds tests in an LTE simulation environment to confirm vulnerabilities; it reported 42 vulnerabilities, 10 new, from 192 hazard indicators.
relation_to_specdx: Couples static spec analysis with executed tests to confirm problems, as SpecDx couples interpretation with executions; its targets are implementation vulnerabilities caused by spec looseness, not typed specification defects.

title: Natural Language Processing for Requirements Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study
authors: Liping Zhao; Waad Alhoshan; Alessio Ferrari; Keletso J. Letsholo; Muideen A. Ajagbe; Erol-Valeriu Chioasca; Riza T. Batista-Navarro
venue: ACM Computing Surveys
subtopics: survey; NLP4RE; mapping study
summary: Systematic mapping study of 404 NLP4RE primary studies over 36 years; most are solution proposals evaluated in the lab, with little industrial evaluation and few released tools.
relation_to_specdx: Positions SpecDx relative to NLP4RE: all surveyed defect-detection work analyses the text statically; none executes the specification.

title: Using Domain-Specific Corpora for Improved Handling of Ambiguity in Requirements
authors: Saad Ezzini; Sallam Abualhaija; Chetan Arora; Mehrdad Sabetzadeh; Lionel C. Briand
venue: 2021 IEEE/ACM 43rd International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: ambiguity; coordination ambiguity; PP-attachment; domain corpora
summary: Detects and interprets coordination and prepositional-phrase attachment ambiguity in requirements using domain-specific corpora generated from Wikipedia; on 20 industrial documents (over 5,000 requirements) it reaches about 80% precision and 89% recall, including unacknowledged ambiguity.
relation_to_specdx: Targets 'unacknowledged ambiguity' (stakeholders each believe their reading is the only one), the same phenomenon SpecDx surfaces by observing divergent executions; SpecDx is language-agnostic and behaviour-grounded rather than syntax-specific.

title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Entity-Sensitive Privacy Policy and Data Flow Analysis with PoliCheck
authors: Benjamin Andow; Samin Yaseer Mahmud; Justin Whitaker; William Enck; Bradley Reaves; Kapil Singh; Serge Egelman
venue: 29th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 20)
subtopics: policy documents; policy-behaviour consistency; data flows
summary: PoliCheck checks consistency between apps' observed data flows and their privacy-policy disclosures, distinguishing first- and third-party recipients; up to 42.4% of 13,796 apps incorrectly disclose or omit sensitive transfers.
relation_to_specdx: Compares an NL policy with observed behaviour, as SpecDx does, but the behaviour is a single program's and deviations are blamed on the program; SpecDx observes many interpreters and blames the specification when all deviate together.

title: Generation of Formal Requirements from Structured Natural Language
authors: Dimitra Giannakopoulou; Thomas Pressburger; Anastasia Mavridou; Johann Schumann
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
subtopics: formalisation; structured natural language; FRET; temporal logic
summary: FRET lets users write requirements in FRETish, a restricted natural language with precise semantics, explains their meaning in text and diagrams, formalises them in future- and past-time metric temporal logic, and supports simulation of the formulas to check that they capture intent.
relation_to_specdx: Removes ambiguity by construction (restricted language plus simulation by a human); SpecDx keeps free-form T and discovers ambiguity by letting a population of interpreters execute it.

title: Detecting terminological ambiguity in user stories: Tool and experimentation
authors: Fabiano Dalpiaz; Ivor van der Schalk; Sjaak Brinkkemper; Fatma Başak Aydemir; Garm Lucassen
venue: Information and Software Technology
subtopics: ambiguity; terminological ambiguity; user stories; near-synonyms
summary: Tool-supported detection of near-synonyms (a source of terminological ambiguity) in user stories by combining conceptual-model extraction, semantic similarity and information visualisation; a quasi-experiment with 57 participants found manual inspection had higher recall.
relation_to_specdx: Terminological ambiguity is one source of SpecDx's Ambiguity type (two terms read as the same or different entity); SpecDx finds it when it changes behaviour on a cell, without a human-in-the-loop visualisation.

title: PolicyLint: Investigating Internal Privacy Policy Contradictions on Google Play
authors: Benjamin Andow; Samin Yaseer Mahmud; Wenyu Wang; Justin Whitaker; William Enck; Bradley Reaves; Kapil Singh; Tao Xie
venue: 28th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 19)
subtopics: policy documents; contradiction; privacy policies; ontology
summary: PolicyLint finds internal contradictions in privacy policies by extracting data-collection and sharing statements and reasoning over negation and the semantic generality of data objects and entities; 14.2% of 11,430 apps' policies contain contradictions, and 510 were manually verified.
relation_to_specdx: Contradiction detection inside an NL policy document, close to SpecDx's τ² policy setting; it is text-internal and ontology-based, whereas SpecDx's Contradiction is unsatisfiability of executable checks against any behaviour.

title: Scalable Analysis of Real-Time Requirements
authors: Annie-Isabell V. Langenfeld; Daniel Dietsch; Bernd Westphal; Jochen Hoenicke; Amalinda Post
venue: 2019 IEEE 27th International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
subtopics: real-time requirements; rt-inconsistency; vacuity; Hanfor
summary: Scales analysis of formalised real-time requirements (rt-inconsistency, vacuity) by reducing it to software model checking and theorem proving, enabling industrial-size requirement sets; implemented in the Hanfor/Ultimate toolchain.
relation_to_specdx: Vacuity (a requirement trivially satisfied) parallels SpecDx's Weak check; rt-inconsistency parallels Contradiction. Hanfor needs a manual formalisation, whereas SpecDx works on executable clauses already present and free-form T.

title: Detecting requirements defects with NLP patterns: an industrial experience in the railway domain
authors: Alessio Ferrari; Gloria Gori; Benedetta Rosadini; Iacopo Trotta; Stefano Bacherini; Alessandro Fantechi; Stefania Gnesi
venue: Empirical Software Engineering
subtopics: requirements defects; NLP patterns; railway; industrial
summary: Implements rule-based defect-detection patterns (GATE) for typical defect classes in a railway signalling manufacturer's requirements and applies them to 1,866 expert-annotated requirements, with expert inspection of false positives and a comparison against the company's manual practice.
relation_to_specdx: Large industrial evidence on pattern-based static defect detection; such patterns flag surface vagueness, whereas SpecDx's defects are defined by satisfaction against executable checks.

title: Towards Development of Complete and Conflict-Free Requirements
authors: Abha Moitra; Kit Siu; Andrew Crapo; Harsh Chamarthi; Michael Durling; Meng Li; Han Yu; Panagiotis Manolios; Michael Meiners
venue: 2018 IEEE 26th International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
subtopics: ASSERT; complete and conflict-free requirements; theorem proving; test generation
summary: ASSERT captures requirements in an unambiguous form backed by a formal analysis engine with an automated theorem prover, detecting conflicting, incomplete and type-inconsistent requirements early, and generates requirements-based tests.
relation_to_specdx: Targets the same defect classes (ambiguity, conflict, incompleteness) symbolically after controlled capture; SpecDx diagnoses existing NL documents against existing executable checks without re-authoring them.

title: Analyzing APIs Documentation and Code to Detect Directive Defects
authors: Yu Zhou; Ruihang Gu; Taolue Chen; Zhiqiu Huang; Sebastiano Panichella; Harald Gall
venue: 2017 IEEE/ACM 39th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: API documentation; directive defects; constraint solving; doc-code inconsistency
summary: Detects defective directives in API documentation (parameter constraints, exception declarations) by extracting constraints from code via program analysis and from documents via NLP and comparing them with a first-order-logic constraint solver; on JDK 1.8 it finds 1,158 defective directives at 81.6% precision and 82.0% recall.
relation_to_specdx: Formalises both the NL document and the executable artefact and compares them with a solver, a B5-style analogue of SpecDx's Hidden requirement and Weak check types (document stricter or looser than code).

title: Improving agile requirements: the Quality User Story framework and tool
authors: Garm Lucassen; Fabiano Dalpiaz; Jan Martijn E. M. van der Werf; Sjaak Brinkkemper
venue: Requirements Engineering
subtopics: user stories; quality defects; tool
summary: Proposes the Quality User Story framework (13 criteria) and the AQUSA tool, which uses NLP to detect user-story quality defects and suggest remedies; evaluated on 1,023 user stories from 18 companies.
relation_to_specdx: Released static quality checker for one requirement notation; its defects are syntactic/pragmatic and not tied to executable checks, unlike SpecDx's satisfaction-defined types.
baseline_notes: Detects user-story defects (atomicity, minimality, well-formedness, uniqueness, conflict-free). Input: user stories in 'As a ..., I want ..., so that ...' form, English only. Adaptation: only applicable to the parts of TonomyX BA documents that are user stories, after translation into English; serves as a weak static baseline next to B1. Code: GitHub gglucass/AQUSA (MIT, archived) and RELabUU/aqusa-core (CLI, MIT).

title: @tComment: Testing Javadoc Comments to Detect Comment-Code Inconsistencies
authors: Shin Hwei Tan; Darko Marinov; Lin Tan; Gary T. Leavens
venue: 2012 IEEE Fifth International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation
subtopics: doc-code inconsistency; Javadoc; random testing; null/exception properties
summary: @tComment infers null-value and exception properties from the English text of Javadoc comments and checks them with generated random tests, reporting comment-code inconsistencies that indicate faults in either the body or the comment.
relation_to_specdx: Executes tests to adjudicate between documentation and code, as SpecDx executes scenarios to adjudicate between T and C; @tComment trusts a single rule-based reading of the comment, while SpecDx samples many readings.

title: Analysing anaphoric ambiguity in natural language requirements
authors: Hui Yang; Anne de Roeck; Vincenzo Gervasi; Alistair Willis; Bashar Nuseibeh
venue: Requirements Engineering
subtopics: ambiguity; anaphoric ambiguity; nocuous ambiguity
summary: Identifies potentially nocuous anaphoric ambiguity in NL requirements with heuristics-based classifiers that predict how strongly readers prefer an interpretation, using the distribution of multiple human judgements to decide nocuousness.
relation_to_specdx: Again uses the spread of human readings to define ambiguity; SpecDx obtains the spread from executions and uses the specification's checks C as an arbiter of which readings are entailed.

title: Automatic detection of nocuous coordination ambiguities in natural language requirements
authors: Hui Yang; Alistair Willis; Anne De Roeck; Bashar Nuseibeh
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM international conference on Automated software engineering
subtopics: ambiguity; nocuous ambiguity; coordination ambiguity
summary: Automatically extracts sentences with coordination ambiguity from requirements and classifies them as nocuous or innocuous with a machine-learned model built on heuristics and human-judgement training data (tool NAI).
relation_to_specdx: Uses reader-disagreement as ground truth for nocuousness, as SpecDx does, but needs human judgements and is restricted to one syntactic ambiguity class; SpecDx needs no labels and covers ambiguity of any linguistic origin that changes behaviour.

title: Ambiguity in Requirements Specification
authors: Daniel M. Berry; Erik Kamsties
venue: Perspectives on Software Requirements
subtopics: ambiguity; foundations
summary: Book chapter surveying ambiguity in natural-language requirements specifications: its linguistic and software-engineering forms and the range of techniques for avoiding, detecting and resolving it.
relation_to_specdx: Standard citation for ambiguity as a requirements defect; SpecDx treats ambiguity as a set-valued entailment (A_c={x,y}) inferred from executions, rather than as a text property flagged by inspection.

title: Managing conflicts in goal-driven requirements engineering
authors: A. van Lamsweerde; R. Darimont; E. Letier
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: conflicts; divergences; goal-oriented RE; KAOS
summary: Formal techniques in the KAOS goal-oriented framework for detecting and resolving conflicts and divergences among goals, where a divergence is witnessed by a boundary condition under which the goals cannot be satisfied together.
relation_to_specdx: Boundary conditions are scenario witnesses of conflict, analogous to SpecDx's witness states; SpecDx finds them over executable database clauses instead of temporal-logic goals.

title: Managing inconsistent specifications: reasoning, analysis, and action
authors: Anthony Hunter; Bashar Nuseibeh
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
subtopics: inconsistency management; quasi-classical logic; multi-perspective specifications
summary: Presents quasi-classical (QC) logic and labelled QC logic, which allow non-trivial reasoning in the presence of inconsistency and track the assumptions behind each derivation, applied to multi-perspective specifications.
relation_to_specdx: Tracking which assumptions jointly yield an inconsistency is the logical ancestor of SpecDx's MUS-based localisation of contradictory clauses.

title: Automated analysis of requirement specifications
authors: William M. Wilson; Linda H. Rosenberg; Lawrence E. Hyatt
venue: Proceedings of the 19th international conference on Software engineering  - ICSE '97
subtopics: requirements quality; indicators; static analysis; NASA ARM
summary: Describes NASA's Automated Requirement Measurement (ARM) tool, which scans requirement specifications for quality indicators such as weak phrases, options, incomplete statements and imperatives.
relation_to_specdx: The first automated static requirements-quality checker, the root of the smell-detection line that B1 modernises with LLMs.

title: Automated consistency checking of requirements specifications
authors: Constance L. Heitmeyer; Ralph D. Jeffords; Bruce G. Labaw
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
subtopics: consistency checking; SCR; tabular requirements; formal analysis
summary: Consistency checking for SCR tabular requirements specifications: a formal finite-state requirements model enables automatic detection of type errors, nondeterminism, missing cases and circular definitions, evaluated on real avionics specifications.
relation_to_specdx: Classic symbolic consistency/completeness checking of a formal specification without interpreters (B5-style); SpecDx needs no formal model of T and adds interpreter-based typing of T-C defects.

title: Context-aware large language models for ambiguity detection in requirements
authors: Victor Vilhelm Poulsen; Matthias Guertler; Boris Eisenbart; Laura Tomidei; Nathalie Sick
venue: Proceedings of the Design Society
subtopics: ambiguity; LLM; domain context; defect injection
summary: Studies LLM ambiguity detection on NASA JWST requirements with systematically injected defects, showing that adding auto-extracted domain knowledge helps LLMs separate genuinely ambiguous requirements from acceptable ones.
relation_to_specdx: Uses injected (seeded) defects for evaluation, as SpecDx's mutation operators do, but for a static detector.

title: Leveraging Large Language Model for Ambiguity Detection and Resolution in Software Requirement Specifications
authors: Ankit Raj; Muhammad Abdul Basit Ur Rahim; Mayur Jain; Shahid Hussain
venue: Software: Practice and Experience
subtopics: ambiguity; fine-tuned LLM; LoRA; resolution
summary: Fine-tunes LLaMA 3/3.1 with LoRA adapters to detect and resolve seven categories of ambiguity (semantic, syntactic, functional, operational, scope, temporal, quality) in SRS documents and user stories.
relation_to_specdx: Supervised static detector; needs annotated data, which SpecDx avoids.

title: Software Requirements Ambiguity Resolution Using Large Language Models
authors: Abdullah Tahir; Nafiseh Kahani; Mohamed Nasr; Masoud Barati; Paniz Oghabi
venue: 2026 IEEE 34th International Requirements Engineering Conference Workshops (REW)
subtopics: ambiguity resolution; chain-of-thought; RAG; Llama
summary: Unified chain-of-thought prompting with Llama 3.1-8B (with and without RAG) for resolving anaphoric, structural, vagueness and scope ambiguities on 411 instances; few-shot CoT reaches 90% human-judged accuracy on anaphora and RAG effects are type-dependent.
relation_to_specdx: Resolution rather than detection; SpecDx's ambiguity output (the competing readings) could feed such a resolver.

title: SpecFSM: Extracting and Repairing Finite State Machines from Protocol Specification Documents
authors: Xiangdong Li; DaWei Huang; Jingjing Guan; Hui Li
venue: Proceedings of the 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: protocol specifications; FSM extraction; LLM; formal verification; repair
summary: SpecFSM extracts protocol FSMs from NL specifications with LLMs and repairs them through state completion, evidence tracing and formal verification, improving correctly extracted transitions by 54.7%.
relation_to_specdx: Uses formal verification to repair LLM misreadings of a spec (interpreter error); SpecDx asks the inverse question of whether consistent misreadings are spec defects.

title: Bridging Natural Language and Formal Specification–Automated Translation of Software Requirements to LTL via Hierarchical Semantics Decomposition Using LLMs
authors: Zhi Ma; Cheng Wen; Zhexin Su; Xiao Liang; Cong Tian; Shengchao Qin; Mengfei Yang
venue: 2025 40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
subtopics: NL to LTL; LLM; hierarchical decomposition; aerospace
summary: Req2LTL translates industrial NL requirements into LTL via a hierarchical intermediate representation (OnionL), using LLMs for semantic decomposition and rule-based synthesis for validity; 88.4% semantic accuracy on aerospace requirements.
relation_to_specdx: State of the art in LLM requirement formalisation, which a VERIMED- or SAT-LLM-style baseline would build on.

title: Code Comment Inconsistency Detection and Rectification Using a Large Language Model
authors: Guoping Rong; Yongda Yu; Song Liu; Xin Tan; Tianyi Zhang; Haifeng Shen; Jidong Hu
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM 47th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: doc-code inconsistency; LLM; fine-tuning; rectification
summary: C4RLLaMA fine-tunes CodeLLaMA to both detect and rectify code-comment inconsistencies, outperforming prior detectors.
relation_to_specdx: LLM-era static doc-code inconsistency detection; SpecDx differs by executing the documentation through interpreters and using checks as the arbiter.

title: Multi-Label Ambiguity Detection in Software Requirements Using Language Models
authors: Paniz Oghabi; Nafiseh Kahani
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Collaborative Advances in Software and COmputiNg (CASCON)
subtopics: ambiguity; multi-label classification; RoBERTa; PURE
summary: Fine-tunes DistilBERT and RoBERTa to detect structural, scope, anaphoric ambiguity and vagueness on 1,266 labelled PURE requirements; RoBERTa reaches about 76% macro-F1.
relation_to_specdx: Supervised text classifier for ambiguity types; SpecDx is unsupervised and behaviour-grounded.

title: PSMBench: A Benchmark and Dataset for Evaluating LLMs Extraction of Protocol State Machines from RFC Specifications
authors: Zilin Shen; Xinyu Luo; Imtiaz Karim; Elisa Bertino
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025), Datasets and Benchmarks Track
subtopics: protocol specifications; RFC; benchmark; LLM reading accuracy
summary: RFC2PSM pairs 1,580 pages of RFC text with 108 validated states and 297 transitions over 14 protocols; PsmBench scores nine LLMs' extracted state machines and finds a state-transition gap (state F1 up to 0.82, transition F1 at most 0.38).
relation_to_specdx: Evidence that LLM readers of long specifications err systematically, which SpecDx must model (reader accuracy and item difficulty) before attributing deviations to the specification.

title: A Tool for Automatically Identifying Semantic Conflicts in User Stories by Combining NLP and BERT Model
authors: Zhen Xuan; Tianci Wang; Chunhui Wang; Tong Li
venue: 2024 IEEE 32nd International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
subtopics: semantic conflicts; user stories; BERT; tool
summary: Tool that checks each user story for syntax and ambiguity problems and detects semantic conflicts between user stories by combining NLP with a BERT model, reaching 92% F1 on 9,060 user stories.
relation_to_specdx: Static pairwise conflict detection in agile requirements; SpecDx's contradictions are found among executable checks.

title: Advancing Requirements Engineering Through Generative AI: Assessing the Role of LLMs
authors: Chetan Arora; John Grundy; Mohamed Abdelrazek
venue: Generative AI for Effective Software Development
subtopics: LLM4RE; SWOT; position
summary: Book chapter assessing LLMs across RE activities (elicitation, analysis, specification, validation) with a SWOT analysis, research directions and preliminary evaluations.
relation_to_specdx: Frames LLM-based requirements validation as text review; SpecDx proposes validation by execution.

title: Scalable Redundancy Detection for Real-Time Requirements
authors: Elisabeth Henkel; Nico Hauff; Lena Funk; Annie-Isabell V. Langenfeld; Andreas Podelski
venue: 2024 IEEE 32nd International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
subtopics: redundancy; real-time requirements; phase event automata
summary: Detects redundant requirements in formal real-time specifications by automata-theoretic model checking over Phase Event Automata, scaling to industrial requirement sets.
relation_to_specdx: A further symbolic quality check on formalised requirements (B5-style); redundancy is not in SpecDx's taxonomy but relates to weak or duplicated checks.

title: NL2TL: Transforming Natural Languages to Temporal Logics using Large Language Models
authors: Yongchao Chen; Rujul Gandhi; Yang Zhang; Chuchu Fan
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
subtopics: NL to temporal logic; LLM; dataset
summary: NL2TL builds a 28K NL-TL dataset with LLMs and human annotation and fine-tunes T5 on lifted NL/TL (atomic propositions hidden) for domain-general translation into temporal logic.
relation_to_specdx: Representative LLM autoformalisation of requirements; SpecDx avoids depending on a single formalisation of T.

title: Deep Just-In-Time Inconsistency Detection Between Comments and Source Code
authors: Sheena Panthaplackel; Junyi Jessy Li; Milos Gligoric; Raymond J. Mooney
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: doc-code inconsistency; just-in-time; deep learning
summary: A deep-learning model that correlates a comment with code changes to detect, before commit, comments made inconsistent by edits to the code; it outperforms baselines and is combined with a comment-update model.
relation_to_specdx: Learned, supervised static inconsistency detection between NL and code; SpecDx is unsupervised and execution-based.

title: A Large-Scale Empirical Study on Code-Comment Inconsistencies
authors: Fengcai Wen; Csaba Nagy; Gabriele Bavota; Michele Lanza
venue: 2019 IEEE/ACM 27th International Conference on Program Comprehension (ICPC)
subtopics: doc-code inconsistency; empirical study; taxonomy
summary: Mines 1.3 billion AST-level changes from 1,500 systems and manually analyses 500 commits to build a taxonomy of code-comment inconsistencies that developers fix.
relation_to_specdx: Shows how a defect taxonomy can be grounded in real fixes from project history, as SpecDx grounds real defects in TonomyX history and the τ²-Bench-Verified diff.

title: An NLP approach for cross-domain ambiguity detection in requirements engineering
authors: Alessio Ferrari; Andrea Esuli
venue: Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: ambiguity; cross-domain ambiguity; word embeddings
summary: Ranks terms by cross-domain ambiguity by comparing word embeddings from domain-specific language models, so that terms used differently by stakeholders of different domains are flagged; evaluated on seven elicitation scenarios against manual and crowd rankings (Kendall tau up to 0.88).
relation_to_specdx: Measures reading divergence across reader populations (domains) through embeddings; SpecDx measures divergence across executor families through behaviour.

title: Translating code comments to procedure specifications
authors: Arianna Blasi; Alberto Goffi; Konstantin Kuznetsov; Alessandra Gorla; Michael D. Ernst; Mauro Pezzè; Sergio Delgado Castellanos
venue: Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
subtopics: comments to specifications; Javadoc; test oracles; Randoop
summary: Jdoctor translates Javadoc comments into executable procedure specifications (Java expressions) by pattern, lexical and semantic matching (92% precision, 83% recall) and feeds them to Randoop as oracles.
relation_to_specdx: Turns NL documentation into executable checks, i.e. builds C from T; SpecDx assumes both exist and diagnoses their disagreement.

title: Requirements Capture and Analysis in ASSERT(TM)
authors: Andrew Crapo; Abha Moitra; Craig McMillan; Daniel Russell
venue: 2017 IEEE 25th International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
subtopics: ASSERT; requirements capture; semantic analysis
summary: Describes requirements capture and formal analysis in GE's ASSERT tool.
relation_to_specdx: Industrial formal requirements analysis tool; see the RE 2018 ASSERT paper for the defect classes it targets.

title: SpeAR v2.0: Formalized Past LTL Specification and Analysis of Requirements
authors: Aaron W. Fifarek; Lucas G. Wagner; Jonathan A. Hoffman; Benjamin D. Rodes; M. Anthony Aiello; Jennifer A. Davis
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
subtopics: formal requirements; Past LTL; consistency; realizability
summary: SpeAR v2.0 captures requirements in a formal language designed to read like natural language with Past LTL semantics, and proves properties of requirement sets (e.g. logical consistency) by model checking.
relation_to_specdx: Formal-by-construction requirement capture with consistency analysis; a B5-style symbolic baseline rather than an NL-interpretation method.

title: Automated Checking of Conformance to Requirements Templates Using Natural Language Processing
authors: Chetan Arora; Mehrdad Sabetzadeh; Lionel Briand; Frank Zimmer
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: template conformance; controlled natural language; NLP
summary: Casts requirements templates (Rupp's and EARS) into NLP pattern matchers to check conformance automatically, robustly and accurately even without a glossary, evaluated on four case studies.
relation_to_specdx: Prevents ambiguity by constraining the form of T; SpecDx instead accepts free-form T (Vietnamese BA documents, policies) and diagnoses it by execution.

title: Finding Contradictions in Text
authors: Marie-Catherine de Marneffe; Anna N. Rafferty; Christopher D. Manning
venue: Proceedings of ACL-08: HLT
subtopics: contradiction detection; NLP foundations; textual entailment
summary: Defines contradiction detection between text pairs as an NLP task, characterises types of contradiction, and builds a feature-based detector on top of textual-entailment alignment.
relation_to_specdx: NLP foundation of text-level contradiction detection used by requirements tools (ALICE, NLI-based RE); SpecDx's contradictions are among executable clauses, not sentences.

title: /*icomment: bugs or bad comments?*/
authors: Lin Tan; Ding Yuan; Gopal Krishna; Yuanyuan Zhou
venue: Proceedings of twenty-first ACM SIGOPS symposium on Operating systems principles
subtopics: doc-code inconsistency; comments; rule extraction; Linux
summary: iComment extracts programming rules from code comments (lock-related topics) with NLP and checks the code against them, reporting each mismatch as either a bug or a bad comment; applied to Linux and Mozilla.
relation_to_specdx: Origin of the 'bugs or bad comments?' attribution question: a doc-code mismatch may indict either side. SpecDx asks the analogous question for executions versus specifications and answers it statistically over a population of executors.

title: The linguistic approach to the natural language requirements quality: benefit of the use of an automatic tool
authors: F. Fabbrini; M. Fusani; S. Gnesi; G. Lami
venue: Proceedings 26th Annual NASA Goddard Software Engineering Workshop
subtopics: requirements quality; linguistic analysis; QuARS; ambiguity indicators
summary: Presents a linguistic quality model for NL requirements and the automatic tool QuARS that flags expressiveness defects (vagueness, optionality, subjectivity, implicitness, weakness) in requirement sentences.
relation_to_specdx: Lexical indicator-based ambiguity detection; SpecDx detects ambiguity only when it affects checked behaviour.

title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack
authors: Hao Wang; Hanchen Li; Qiuyang Mang; Alvin Cheung; Koushik Sen; Dawn Song
venue: arXiv
subtopics: benchmark auditing; reward hacking; weak checks; agentic benchmarks; benchmark red-teaming; exploit synthesis
specdx_components: defect taxonomy; refutation; baseline B1; mutation evaluation
summary: Derives an eight-class taxonomy of benchmark flaws from past reward hacks, proposes an Agent-Eval Checklist, and builds BenchJack, an automated red-teaming system in which coding agents audit benchmarks and synthesise reward-hacking exploits; finds 219 flaws across 10 agent benchmarks and iteratively patches several.
relation_to_specdx: Automatically audits agent-benchmark checkers with agents and produces exploit witnesses, overlapping SpecDx's weak-check detection with witnesses; it is adversarial (one agent seeks exploits) rather than a statistical diagnosis over a population of honest executors, and covers only checks that are too loose. | BenchJack's synthesised exploits are witnesses of weak checks (a wrong behaviour that passes every clause), the defect type SpecDx calls 'weak check'. SpecDx finds weak checks from the population plus symbolic search on the database; BenchJack finds them adversarially and does not address contradictions, hidden requirements or ambiguity.
baseline_notes: BenchJack drives coding agents to audit a benchmark's evaluation and synthesise reward-hacking exploits (witnesses that score without solving). On SpecDx: point it at a tau-style task's checker (SQL clauses, golden state) to find passing-but-wrong behaviours, i.e. weak checks with witnesses. It does not find hidden requirements, ambiguity or contradictions, nor separate agent error from spec defect. Python, Apache-2.0, released 2026. | For the weak-check class only: point BenchJack at a SpecDx task with its checks C and let it search for a passing behaviour that violates T; a found exploit is a weak-check witness. Code public; requires a capable coding agent.

title: MutDafny: A Mutation-Based Approach to Assess Dafny Specifications
authors: Isabel Amaral; Alexandra Mendes; José Campos
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering
subtopics: specification weakness; mutation testing; Dafny; verified programs
summary: MutDafny reveals weak Dafny specifications by mutating code: if a mutant still verifies, the specification may be too weak; 40 operators (from existing tools plus ones mined from Dafny bug fixes), evaluated on 794 real programs, revealing five weak real-world specifications.
relation_to_specdx: State of the art for detecting weak checks by mutation in verified code; SpecDx detects weak checks in executable business specifications and additionally types and localises hidden requirements, ambiguities and contradictions without a reference implementation.
baseline_notes: MutDafny mutates the implementation and flags weak specifications when a mutant still verifies. SpecDx analogue: mutate agent trajectories / end states (or golden state) with the analogous operators and report clauses under which mutated behaviours still pass as weak-check candidates. Code available (C#, Dafny-specific), so only the operator catalogue transfers; the SQL-side reimplementation is straightforward.

title: Spec-Harness: Assessing and Guiding LLM-Synthesized Formal Specifications Beyond Verifiability
authors: Md Rakib Hossain Misu; Cristina V. Lopes; Iris Ma; Yuangang Li; Shuvendu Lahiri
venue: arXiv
subtopics: LLM-generated specifications; specification adequacy; JML; mutation
summary: Shows that verifier acceptance of LLM-synthesised JML specifications says little about quality (22.7% of verified specs had no postcondition) and introduces Spec-Harness, which measures behavioural adequacy along precondition/postcondition correctness and completeness using symbolic verification and input/output mutation, revealing over- and under-constraining specs.
relation_to_specdx: Closest recent work on clause-level over/under-constraint diagnosis of specifications; it relies on generated test suites as ground truth and Java code, whereas SpecDx uses an LLM-executor population against NL requirements and also handles ambiguity and contradiction.
baseline_notes: Spec-Harness scores a specification on four dimensions (precondition/postcondition correctness and completeness) via Hoare-triple symbolic checks and input/output mutation on built test suites, per clause. Its per-dimension scores correspond to SpecDx's hidden requirement (over-constraining) and weak check (under-constraining). Adaptation requires labelled I/O tests; on SpecDx, use golden end states and one-cell output mutations. Code: Mondego/vACT (Java, GPL-3.0, active 2026) is described as using Spec-Harness feedback; the link to the paper is by group and description.

title: UTBoost: Rigorous Evaluation of Coding Agents on SWE-Bench
authors: Boxi Yu; Yuxuan Zhu; Pinjia He; Daniel Kang
venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
subtopics: weak test oracles; benchmark repair; SWE-bench; weak tests; LLM test generation; leaderboard correction; weak checks; insufficient tests; test augmentation
summary: Introduces UTGenerator, an LLM-driven test generator, and UTBoost for test augmentation of SWE-Bench; finds 36 tasks with insufficient tests and 345 wrongly passed patches, changing 40.9% of SWE-Bench Lite and 24.4% of Verified leaderboard entries.
relation_to_specdx: Automatic weak-check detection in an agent benchmark via LLM-generated extra oracles; SpecDx covers all four defect types and separates spec defects from agent errors statistically rather than by trusting generated tests. | Automated weak-check repair for code benchmarks by generating tests that refute wrong patches; SpecDx detects weak clauses in business specifications by executor-population statistics and confirms them with witness states. | Detects weak checks (C looser than T) and repairs them with generated tests, using agents' wrongly accepted patches as witnesses; SpecDx detects the same class from interpreter populations on business specifications and certifies by witness states.
baseline_notes: UTGenerator/UTBoost augments a benchmark's tests with LLM-generated tests and flags tasks whose original tests accept wrong patches (weak checks). Adaptation: have an LLM generate extra SQL expectations per tau-style task from T, and flag tasks where recorded agent runs pass the original C but fail generated checks. Detects weak checks only; Python, MIT, code released.

title: Can Large Language Models Transform Natural Language Intent into Formal Method Postconditions?
authors: Madeline Endres; Sarah Fakhoury; Saikat Chakraborty; Shuvendu K. Lahiri
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE 2024)
subtopics: nl2postcond; LLM-generated specifications; mutation-based specification evaluation
specdx_components: mutation evaluation; defect taxonomy; baseline B1
summary: Defines nl2postcond, using LLMs to turn natural-language intent into formal postconditions (assertions), and introduces metrics based on correctness on tests and discriminative power against buggy mutants; finds LLM postconditions are often correct and discriminating and can catch real historical bugs.
relation_to_specdx: Assesses executable checks derived from NL intent along the same two axes as SpecDx's Hidden requirement (rejects correct behaviour) and Weak check (accepts buggy behaviour), using tests and mutants as ground truth; SpecDx assumes no labelled tests and infers the intended behaviour from a fallible executor population.
baseline_notes: Its two metrics are directly reusable as evaluation baselines for clause quality: test-set correctness (a clause must accept all reference-correct behaviours; failing = hidden requirement) and bug-discriminating power (fraction of buggy behaviours/mutants a clause rejects; low = weak check). Inputs: clauses, a set of correct behaviours and a set of mutants; in SpecDx use golden-state runs as correct behaviours and seeded wrong behaviours as mutants. Needs labelled behaviours, which SpecDx avoids. Code: not verified.

title: Evaluating LLM-driven User-Intent Formalization for Verification-Aware Languages
authors: Shuvendu K. Lahiri
venue: Proceedings of the 24th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2024), TU Wien Academic Press
subtopics: user-intent formalization; specification soundness; specification completeness; symbolic testing of specifications; Dafny
summary: Argues that evaluating NL-to-specification formalisation in Dafny/F* cannot rely on dynamic execution, and proposes symbolically testing specifications against input-output examples, measuring soundness and completeness of a specification (including against mutated outputs); the metric agrees closely with human labels on Dafny specifications from MBPP-DFY.
relation_to_specdx: Formalises specification soundness/completeness checking, which maps to SpecDx's hidden-requirement and weak-check types; it presumes trusted tests, whereas SpecDx diagnoses clauses whose intended behaviour must itself be inferred from T via fallible interpreters.
baseline_notes: Symbolic testing of specifications: a spec is sound if it admits every (input, expected output) test and complete if it rejects every wrong output (mutated output). Adaptation: for each scenario, check SpecDx's clause set against the golden end state (soundness; a failure flags hidden requirement/contradiction) and against mutated end states that change one cell (completeness; acceptance flags weak check), using PostgreSQL to evaluate clauses. Requires a trusted golden state, which SpecDx itself treats as fallible. Implementation is simple to replicate; no released code verified.

title: IronSpec: Increasing the Reliability of Formal Specifications
authors: Eli Goldweber; Weixin Yu; Seyed Armin Vakil Ghahani; Manos Kapritsos
venue: 18th USENIX Symposium on Operating Systems Design and Implementation (OSDI 24)
subtopics: specification bugs; spec testing; spec mutation testing; verified systems
specdx_components: mutation evaluation; defect taxonomy; real-defect benchmark
summary: IronSpec is a framework of automatic and manual techniques to make formal specifications more reliable: automated sanity checking, a methodology for spec-testing proofs, and automated spec mutation testing; on 14 specs, including six from real verified systems, it found ten specification bugs.
relation_to_specdx: Directly targets bugs in trusted specifications with mutation and sanity checks, like SpecDx, but for Dafny specs with human-written spec tests; SpecDx is automatic, works on NL+SQL business specs, and uses executor-population statistics.
baseline_notes: IronSpec's automated sanity checks (e.g. vacuity/always-true or unsatisfiable predicates) and spec mutation testing are the formal-spec analogue of SpecDx's B5. Adaptation: run sanity checks per SQL clause (is it satisfiable on the schema? is it implied by other clauses or always true on reachable states?) and mutate clauses to see whether any recorded run distinguishes them. Code exists (Dafny/C#), not directly reusable on SQL.

title: FLACK: Counterexample-Guided Fault Localization for Alloy Models
authors: Guolong Zheng; ThanhVu Nguyen; Simon Gutierrez Brida; German Regis; Marcelo F. Frias; Nazareno Aguirre; Hamid Bagheri
venue: 2021 IEEE/ACM 43rd International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: Alloy; fault localization; counterexamples; fault localisation; declarative specifications; MaxSAT
summary: FLACK localises faults in Alloy models with a violated assertion by analysing differences between counterexamples and satisfying instances, returning a ranked list of suspicious expressions; it handles large real models within seconds and ranks buggy expressions in the top 1.9% on average.
relation_to_specdx: Contrasts violating and satisfying instances to localise a specification fault, which resembles SpecDx's use of passing vs violating behaviours; SpecDx's instances come from fallible LLM executors, so it must first separate interpreter error from specification defect. | Fault localisation inside a formal specification using counterexample/witness pairs, related to SpecDx's witness-based refutation; FLACK needs a formal model and an assertion, while SpecDx localises defects between natural-language T and executable C.
baseline_notes: FLACK takes a specification with a violated assertion and ranks suspicious expressions by contrasting counterexamples with satisfying instances; no tests needed. Adaptation: the satisfying instances are agent end states that pass the clause set and the counterexamples are end states that violate a clause; ranking clause sub-expressions by how they separate the two gives a solver-free localisation baseline on C. It assumes the assertion (intended property) is correct, which in SpecDx corresponds to trusting T's reading. Code: no link in the abstract; repository not verified.

title: Evolutionary improvement of assertion oracles
authors: Valerio Terragni; Gunel Jahangirova; Paolo Tonella; Mauro Pezzè
venue: Proceedings of the 28th ACM Joint Meeting on European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering
subtopics: oracle improvement; assertion oracles; evolutionary search; false positives; false negatives
summary: GAssert: a co-evolutionary algorithm that repairs assertion oracles so they have no false positives on correct executions and fewer false negatives on mutant executions, outperforming oracles inferred by Daikon-like tools.
relation_to_specdx: Repairs oracle deficiencies of both kinds using correct executions and mutants as evidence; SpecDx diagnoses (and localises) the analogous clause defects without a trusted program, using LLM-executor runs as noisy evidence of the intended behaviour.

title: Fault Localization for Declarative Models in Alloy
authors: Kaiyuan Wang; Allison Sullivan; Darko Marinov; Sarfraz Khurshid
venue: 2020 IEEE 31st International Symposium on Software Reliability Engineering (ISSRE)
subtopics: Alloy; fault localization; spectrum-based; mutation-based
summary: AlloyFL, a fault-localisation technique for Alloy models that brings spectrum-based and mutation-based fault localisation to declarative models using multiple test formulas; on 90 real faulty models it is much more effective than Alloy's built-in unsat core.
relation_to_specdx: Localises faults inside a specification from test outcomes, as SpecDx localises defects to clauses and cells; AlloyFL trusts its tests, whereas SpecDx's 'tests' are fallible executor runs whose reliability it estimates.
baseline_notes: AlloyFL ranks suspicious Alloy expressions using spectrum-based and mutation-based fault localisation over test formulas. Adaptation: treat each SpecDx run as a test (pass/fail per clause), each clause or clause-conjunct as a 'statement', and compute spectrum suspiciousness (e.g. Ochiai) of clauses over runs judged correct vs incorrect; this gives a localisation baseline that ignores interpreter accuracy. Needs labelled runs, which SpecDx does not have, so labels must come from majority vote. Code: Java; a candidate repository was found by search but not yet linked to the paper.

title: MuAlloy: a mutation testing framework for alloy
authors: Kaiyuan Wang; Allison Sullivan; Sarfraz Khurshid
venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Software Engineering: Companion Proceeedings
subtopics: Alloy; specification mutation; equivalent mutants; tool
summary: Tool paper for MuAlloy, an open-source Java command-line tool defining mutation testing for Alloy: mutation operators, mutant generation, and equivalent-mutant checking with the Alloy Analyzer, used to assess AUnit test suites.
relation_to_specdx: Mutation operators and solver-based equivalent-mutant checking for a specification language, close to SpecDx's specification mutation operators with kill witnesses; MuAlloy evaluates tests of a spec, SpecDx evaluates a diagnoser of specs.

title: OASIs: oracle assessment and improvement tool
authors: Gunel Jahangirova; David Clark; Mark Harman; Paolo Tonella
venue: Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
subtopics: oracle assessment; tool; false positives; false negatives
summary: Tool demo of OASIs, a search-based Java tool that assists oracle assessment and improvement by combining test generation to reveal false positives and mutation testing to reveal false negatives of assertions.
relation_to_specdx: Directly operationalises the two oracle deficiencies SpecDx types as Hidden requirement and Weak check, but assumes the implementation is the reference; SpecDx has no reference implementation and uses a fallible executor population plus anchored truth inference.
baseline_notes: OASIs (Java) reports false positives (generated tests where an assertion fails though the program is deemed correct) and false negatives (mutants an assertion does not catch). Adaptation to SpecDx: treat each SQL clause in C as an assertion over the end state; FP search = find agent end states that satisfy T (population majority) but violate a clause (hidden requirement); FN search = mutate the golden state or an accepted trajectory and check whether any clause fails (weak check). Code: Java/EvoSuite-based; repository not yet verified, so the idea, not the tool, is the baseline.

title: An Empirical Study on the Correctness of Formally Verified Distributed Systems
authors: Pedro Fonseca; Kaiyuan Zhang; Xi Wang; Arvind Krishnamurthy
venue: Proceedings of the Twelfth European Conference on Computer Systems
subtopics: specification bugs; verified systems; empirical study
summary: First empirical study of correctness of formally verified distributed systems (IronFleet, Verdi, Chapar): 16 bugs found, many serious, caused by violated assumptions in the trusted base, including specification and shim-layer issues, showing verification guarantees rest on unverified specifications.
relation_to_specdx: Evidence that 'the specification is the bug' even in verified systems; motivates SpecDx's premise that executable specifications treated as ground truth are themselves defective.

title: Test oracle assessment and improvement
authors: Gunel Jahangirova; David Clark; Mark Harman; Paolo Tonella
venue: Proceedings of the 25th International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
subtopics: oracle assessment; false positives; false negatives; mutation
summary: Proposes assessing assertion oracles by finding false positives (assertion fails on a correct execution, found by test generation) and false negatives (assertion passes on an incorrect execution, found by mutation), and iteratively improving them with human feedback; fault detection rose 48.6% on five subjects.
relation_to_specdx: The closest SE analogue of SpecDx's Hidden requirement (false positive) and Weak check (false negative) types, each backed by a concrete witness execution. It assumes the program is correct and a human adjudicates; SpecDx has no trusted implementation and replaces the human with a population of LLM executors.

title: The Effectiveness of Test Coverage Criteria for Relational Database Schema Integrity Constraints
authors: Phil Mcminn; Chris J. Wright; Gregory M. Kapfhammer
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
subtopics: SQL integrity constraints; schema mutation; coverage criteria
summary: Proposes logic-coverage-derived criteria for testing integrity constraints of relational schemas (from accepted/rejected INSERTs to multi-column keys and arbitrary CHECK constraints), accounting for DBMS-specific semantics, with search-based data generation and mutation analysis to evaluate them.
relation_to_specdx: Mutation analysis of SQL constraints is the nearest prior art for SpecDx's SQL clause mutation operators and for searching witness rows on PostgreSQL; it tests a schema against intent given by a tester, while SpecDx infers intent from NL requirements via executors.
baseline_notes: SchemaAnalyst generates INSERT data and runs mutation analysis on schema integrity constraints (PK, FK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK) for PostgreSQL among others. For SpecDx: express the declarative part of C as CHECK/constraint DDL, reuse its mutation operators as seeded weak-check/hidden-requirement mutants, and its data generator as a solver-free witness search for clause satisfiability. Code: Java, GPL-3.0, last push 2021.

title: The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey
authors: Earl T. Barr; Mark Harman; Phil McMinn; Muzammil Shahbaz; Shin Yoo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: test oracle problem; survey
summary: Surveys the test oracle problem, classifying oracles as specified, derived, implicit, or human, and reviewing techniques and open challenges for deciding whether observed behaviour is correct.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's clause set C is a specified oracle and its Weak check / Hidden requirement types are oracle deficiencies (too loose / too strict); SpecDx adds a derived oracle from a population of LLM executors to diagnose the specified oracle itself.

title: Improving oracle quality by detecting brittle assertions and unused inputs in tests
authors: Chen Huo; James Clause
venue: Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Foundations of Software Engineering
subtopics: oracle quality; brittle assertions; over-checking; under-checking
summary: Dynamic-tainting technique (OraclePolish) that detects brittle assertions, which depend on uncontrolled inputs, and unused inputs, which no assertion checks; finds 164 brittle and 1,618 unused-input tests among 4,000+ real JUnit tests.
relation_to_specdx: Names both oracle failure directions (checks too much vs too little) that SpecDx types as Hidden requirement and Weak check; it is purely structural and per test, while SpecDx decides from behaviour across a population whether the extra or missing check contradicts T.
baseline_notes: OraclePolish uses dynamic taint tracking to find brittle assertions (checking values derived from uncontrolled inputs: over-strict, a hidden-requirement analogue) and unused inputs (inputs never checked: a weak-check analogue). Adaptation: taint the scenario inputs and agent-written cells through the PostgreSQL end state; a clause reading cells not determined by the scenario/T is brittle; scenario-controlled cells read by no clause are unchecked. Static/dataflow baseline with no interpreters (fits B5 family). Code: Java/JUnit tool; repository not verified.

title: Assessing Oracle Quality with Checked Coverage
authors: David Schuler; Andreas Zeller
venue: 2011 Fourth IEEE International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation
subtopics: oracle quality; checked coverage; dynamic slicing
summary: Introduces checked coverage: the dynamic slice of executed statements that actually influence an oracle check; shows on seven open-source projects that it indicates oracle quality better than statement coverage.
relation_to_specdx: A weak-check detector by construction: computations not reaching any check are unchecked. The SpecDx analogue is cells (table, row, column) that agents write but no clause reads; SpecDx instead detects weak checks behaviourally, via passing runs that the population deems wrong.

title: Programs, tests, and oracles: the foundations of testing revisited
authors: Matt Staats; Michael W. Whalen; Mats P.E. Heimdahl
venue: Proceedings of the 33rd International Conference on Software Engineering
subtopics: test oracle theory; oracle adequacy
summary: Extends Gourlay's functional framework of testing with an explicit test oracle, uses it to clarify earlier concepts and define new oracle-related ones, and argues that oracle selection must be considered when judging the efficacy of a testing process.
relation_to_specdx: Gives the formal vocabulary for oracles that are wrong in either direction, which matches SpecDx's satisfaction-based taxonomy (weak check = oracle accepts incorrect behaviour; hidden requirement = oracle rejects behaviour allowed by T); SpecDx adds automatic detection of such oracle defects.

title: Finding Minimal Unsatisfiable Cores of Declarative Specifications
authors: Emina Torlak; Felix Sheng-Ho Chang; Daniel Jackson
venue: FM 2008: Formal Methods, LNCS 5014
subtopics: unsat cores; declarative specifications; Alloy; overconstraint; over-constrained axioms
summary: Presents recycling core extraction, a coverage analysis that pinpoints an irreducible (minimal) unsatisfiable core of a declarative specification to expose overconstrained axioms or underconstrained conjectures; based on resolution refutation proofs, proved correct for a general language and implemented and evaluated for Alloy.
relation_to_specdx: The direct logic-only analogue of SpecDx's contradiction detection (MUS of the clause set); SpecDx obtains candidate MUSes as hitting sets of correction sets sampled from executor behaviours, which also works when clauses are not translatable to a solver, and then refutes candidates with witness states. | Minimal unsat cores as a diagnostic for defects of declarative specifications (over-constraint ~ contradiction / hidden requirement) is the symbolic counterpart of SpecDx's contradiction step; it needs a formal specification, whereas SpecDx diagnoses NL text against executable checks via interpreters.
baseline_notes: Recycling core extraction (implemented in Alloy/Kodkod) returns an irreducible unsatisfiable core of an over-constrained specification. As a B5-style baseline: encode C (SQL invariants + expectations + golden state, per scenario) as Kodkod/Alloy relational constraints or as SMT, ask for a minimal core when the conjunction is unsatisfiable, and report core clauses as contradiction candidates. It finds contradictions only (no hidden requirement, ambiguity or weak check) and needs a faithful translation of SQL to relational logic. Code: Kodkod/Alloy Analyzer are open source (repository not yet verified here).

title: Vacuity in Testing
authors: Thomas Ball; Orna Kupferman
venue: Tests and Proofs (TAP 2008), LNCS 4966
subtopics: vacuity detection; testing; specification quality
