summary: Transfers vacuity from model checking to testing: defines vacuous satisfaction of a specification by a test suite (a mutated specification is still satisfied, so some specification elements play no role) and shows how vacuity analysis improves specifications and test suites.
relation_to_specdx: The closest formal definition of a weak check in a testing setting: a clause that can be mutated without any test noticing. SpecDx detects weak checks without mutating clauses, via runs that pass every clause yet contradict T according to the interpreter population; the mutation view is used in SpecDx's evaluation.

title: Debugging overconstrained declarative models using unsatisfiable cores
authors: I. Shlyakhter; R. Seater; D. Jackson; M. Sridharan; M. Taghdiri
venue: 18th IEEE International Conference on Automated Software Engineering, 2003. Proceedings.
subtopics: unsat cores; overconstraint; Alloy; declarative models
summary: Introduces core extraction for declarative models: the SAT solver's unsatisfiable core is mapped back to the model's syntax to show fragments irrelevant to the result, helping to discover and localise unintended overconstraint, with a soundness argument and case studies.
relation_to_specdx: First use of unsat cores to localise overconstraint (contradictions and hidden requirements) in a specification; SpecDx's MUS/MCS step addresses the same defect from behavioural correction sets, and adds statistical typing of non-contradiction defects. | The original "unsat cores for specification debugging" idea; it targets overconstrained (vacuous) formal models, a defect class related to SpecDx's contradictions and hidden requirements, but it needs a formal model and cannot see NL ambiguity or weak checks.

title: Vacuity detection in temporal model checking
authors: Orna Kupferman; Moshe Y. Vardi
venue: International Journal on Software Tools for Technology Transfer (STTT)
subtopics: vacuity detection; model checking; weak specifications
summary: Gives a general method to detect vacuity and generate interesting witnesses for CTL* specifications, defining vacuity as some subformula not affecting the specification's truth in the system; also studies alternative definitions, linear witnesses for branching logic and complexity.
relation_to_specdx: Vacuity is the model-checking form of a weak check: the specification passes for an uninteresting reason. SpecDx's weak-check type likewise asks whether a clause constrains anything, but decides it from a population of executions of a natural-language spec rather than by mutating temporal subformulas against a fixed model.

title: Mutation operators for specifications
authors: P.E. Black; V. Okun; Y. Yesha
venue: Proceedings ASE 2000. Fifteenth IEEE International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: specification mutation; mutation operators; model checking
summary: Defines an extensive set of syntactic mutation operators for formal (model-checker) specifications, used to generate test suites via mutation analysis, studies theoretically and experimentally which fault classes each operator detects, and recommends reduced operator sets.
relation_to_specdx: Canonical source for mutating the specification itself rather than the program; SpecDx's evaluation seeds defects with specification mutation operators, but its operators target typed business-spec defects (contradiction, hidden requirement, ambiguity, weak check) and each mutant carries a kill witness against a population of LLM executors rather than a model-checker counterexample.

title: TOGLL: Correct and Strong Test Oracle Generation with LLMS
authors: Soneya Binta Hossain; Matthew B. Dwyer
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM 47th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: LLM oracle generation; false positives; oracle strength
summary: Large study of LLMs for test oracle generation (seven fine-tuned code LLMs, six prompts) yielding TOGLL, which produces correct, diverse and strong oracles with far fewer false positives than TOGA, assessed on 25 Java projects including mutation-based strength.
relation_to_specdx: Shows LLM-written checks suffer both false positives (too strict) and weak oracles (too loose), the deficiencies SpecDx diagnoses in benchmark clauses.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Pre-trained Large Language Models for Repairing Declarative Formal Specifications
authors: Mohannad Alhanahnah; Md Rashedul Hasan; Lisong Xu; Hamid Bagheri
venue: arXiv
subtopics: LLM; Alloy; specification repair; agents
summary: Systematically evaluates LLMs for repairing Alloy declarative specifications in six settings (single/dual agent, feedback levels, auto-prompting) on 1,974 faulty specifications from ARepair and Alloy4Fun; a dual-agent auto-prompting setup beats state-of-the-art Alloy repair tools.
relation_to_specdx: LLMs reasoning over a faulty specification with solver feedback is close to SpecDx's static LLM review baseline (B1) plus refutation; it assumes the defect exists and a reference oracle, whereas SpecDx must first detect and type defects without one.

title: Large Language Models for Equivalent Mutant Detection: How Far Are We?
authors: Zhao Tian; Honglin Shu; Dong Wang; Xuejie Cao; Yasutaka Kamei; Junjie Chen
venue: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
subtopics: equivalent mutant problem; LLM
summary: Empirical study of LLMs for equivalent mutant detection on a large benchmark, comparing prompting and fine-tuning strategies with prior detection techniques.
relation_to_specdx: Shows LLMs can judge semantic equivalence of mutants; SpecDx could use a similar LLM check as a pre-filter for seeded specification mutants, but relies on executable kill witnesses rather than LLM judgement for soundness.

title: Right or Wrong – Understanding How Users Write Software Models in Alloy
authors: Ana Jovanovic; Allison Sullivan
venue: Software Engineering and Formal Methods (SEFM 2024), LNCS
subtopics: Alloy4Fun; specification errors; underconstraint; overconstraint; benchmark
summary: Empirical study of over 97,000 Alloy models written by novices (Alloy4Fun) analysing how correct and incorrect models are written, separating underconstrained errors (model allows scenarios it should prevent) from overconstrained ones (prevents scenarios it should allow), and releasing benchmarks of faulty models.
relation_to_specdx: Its under/over-constraint split maps onto SpecDx's weak check vs hidden requirement/contradiction types, giving external evidence that the taxonomy reflects real specification errors.

title: ATR: template-based repair for Alloy specifications
authors: Guolong Zheng; ThanhVu Nguyen; Simón Gutiérrez Brida; Germán Regis; Nazareno Aguirre; Marcelo F. Frias; Hamid Bagheri
venue: Proceedings of the 31st ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
subtopics: Alloy; specification repair; counterexamples
summary: ATR repairs Alloy specifications with a violated assertion by contrasting counterexamples with satisfying instances to guide template-based repair candidates and prune them; repairs 66.3% of 1,974 faulty specifications, with code and benchmarks released.
relation_to_specdx: Uses instance contrasts to repair a specification; its 1,974-specification benchmark (ARepair + Alloy4Fun) is the standard real-defect benchmark for declarative specifications that SpecDx could cite for the logic component.

title: Fuzzing class specifications
authors: Facundo Molina; Marcelo d'Amorim; Nazareno Aguirre
venue: Proceedings of the 44th International Conference on Software Engineering
subtopics: specification inference; mutation filtering
summary: SpecFuzzer infers class specifications by combining grammar-based fuzzing of candidate assertions, Daikon-based filtering of assertions falsified by a test suite, and a mutation-based mechanism that clusters assertions and ranks the stronger ones first; evaluated on 43 Java methods against GAssert and EvoSpex.
relation_to_specdx: Uses mutants to measure whether inferred specifications are strong enough, the same strength criterion SpecDx applies to seeded weak-check mutants; SpecDx does not synthesise clauses.

title: ICEBAR: Feedback-Driven Iterative Repair of Alloy Specifications
authors: Simón Gutiérrez Brida; Germán Regis; Guolong Zheng; Hamid Bagheri; Thanhvu Nguyen; Nazareno Aguirre; Marcelo Frias
venue: Proceedings of the 37th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: Alloy; specification repair; property-based oracles; overfitting
summary: ICEBAR repairs Alloy specifications using property-based oracles (predicates and assertions) for patch assessment instead of tests, iterating with counterexample feedback to reduce the overfitting typical of test-based repair.
relation_to_specdx: Shows that weak (test-based) oracles cause overfit specification repairs, i.e. weak checks; SpecDx diagnoses such weak checks directly in the oracle.

title: An Empirical Validation of Oracle Improvement
authors: Gunel Jahangirova; David Clark; Mark Harman; Paolo Tonella
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: oracle improvement; human study
summary: Human studies (68 participants) of oracle assessment and improvement; developers judge assertion correctness poorly (29% accuracy) unaided, and the proposed false-positive/false-negative guided process helps them produce better oracles.
relation_to_specdx: Evidence that humans are unreliable at judging oracle (clause) correctness, which supports SpecDx's choice of fully automatic, statistically aggregated diagnosis.

title: Bounded Exhaustive Search of Alloy Specification Repairs
authors: Simon Gutierrez Brida; German Regis; Guolong Zheng; Hamid Bagheri; ThanhVu Nguyen; Nazareno Aguirre; Marcelo Frias
venue: 2021 IEEE/ACM 43rd International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: Alloy; specification repair; bounded exhaustive search
summary: BeAFix repairs faulty Alloy models by bounded-exhaustive yet scalable exploration of fix candidates (mutations of suspicious expressions) with sound pruning, using the model's own assertions instead of unit tests; repairs thousands of real faulty models better than prior work.
relation_to_specdx: Uses mutation operators over a specification to search for fixes; SpecDx uses specification mutation for evaluation (seeding defects) and does not repair, but the repair space hints at which mutation operators produce realistic defects.

title: Experiences on teaching alloy with an automated assessment platform
authors: Nuno Macedo; Alcino Cunha; José Pereira; Renato Carvalho; Ricardo Silva; Ana C.R. Paiva; Miguel Sozinho Ramalho; Daniel Silva
venue: Science of Computer Programming
subtopics: Alloy4Fun; dataset; specification errors
summary: Presents Alloy4Fun, a web platform for editing, sharing and automatically assessing Alloy specification challenges via secret paragraphs and commands; it stores all model versions and derivation trees, a dataset that can be mined for typical specification mistakes.
relation_to_specdx: Source of the Alloy4Fun dataset of real faulty specifications with ground-truth oracles used by ATR, ICEBAR and LLM repair studies; useful as an external real-defect set for SpecDx's logic components.

title: GAssert: A Fully Automated Tool to Improve Assertion Oracles
authors: Valerio Terragni; Gunel Jahangirova; Paolo Tonella; Mauro Pezzè
venue: 2021 IEEE/ACM 43rd International Conference on Software Engineering: Companion Proceedings (ICSE-Companion)
subtopics: oracle improvement; tool
summary: Tool paper for GAssert, which automatically improves assertion oracles (executable boolean expressions) by evolving them to reduce false positives and false negatives.
relation_to_specdx: Same relation as the FSE 2020 paper; the tool's input/output shape (assertion plus labelled executions) is close to a clause plus labelled runs in SpecDx.
baseline_notes: GAssert takes a Java method, an assertion oracle, correct executions and mutant executions, and evolves the assertion to remove false positives/negatives. Adaptation: encode each SQL invariant/expectation as a boolean expression over end-state variables; use runs judged correct by the population as 'correct executions' and seeded spec mutants or wrong runs as 'mutant executions'; clauses GAssert must weaken are hidden-requirement candidates, clauses it must strengthen are weak-check candidates. Requires re-implementing the search over SQL predicates; code: github.com/valerio-terragni/gassert (repo exists, no licence, last push 2020).

title: A comprehensive study of pseudo-tested methods
authors: Oscar Luis Vera-Pérez; Benjamin Danglot; Martin Monperrus; Benoit Baudry
venue: Empirical Software Engineering
subtopics: pseudo-tested methods; extreme mutation; weak oracles
summary: Replicates the pseudo-tested-method study on 28K+ methods (methods covered by tests yet no test fails when the body is removed) and characterises 101 of them manually, finding they are less tested than other methods but often not worth fixing to developers.
relation_to_specdx: Pseudo-tested code is the program-side symptom of weak oracles; SpecDx's weak-check operator (deleting or loosening a clause so a wrong behaviour passes) is the specification-side analogue.

title: Automated model repair for Alloy
authors: Kaiyuan Wang; Allison Sullivan; Sarfraz Khurshid
venue: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM/IEEE International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: Alloy; specification repair; mutation
summary: ARepair, the first repair technique for Alloy models: given a faulty model and a test suite with failing tests, it combines mutation testing and program synthesis to output a model passing the tests; fixes 28 of 38 real faulty models.
relation_to_specdx: Repairs specification defects but assumes trusted tests as the oracle; SpecDx has no trusted oracle and stops at typed, localised diagnosis. Its benchmark of real faulty Alloy models is a candidate external benchmark for the logic half of SpecDx.

title: Are mutants a valid substitute for real faults in software testing?
authors: René Just; Darioush Jalali; Laura Inozemtseva; Michael D. Ernst; Reid Holmes; Gordon Fraser
venue: Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Foundations of Software Engineering
subtopics: mutant validity; real faults
summary: Empirically tests whether mutant detection correlates with real-fault detection, using real faults from open-source projects and generated test suites; finds a significant correlation that coverage alone does not explain, while some real-fault types are not coupled to common mutants.
relation_to_specdx: Motivates SpecDx's two-pronged evaluation: seeded specification mutants plus real defects (TonomyX history, tau2-Bench-Verified diff), since mutant results alone may not transfer to real specification defects.

title: Overcoming the Equivalent Mutant Problem: A Systematic Literature Review and a Comparative Experiment of Second Order Mutation
authors: Lech Madeyski; Wojciech Orzeszyna; Richard Torkar; Mariusz Jozala
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: equivalent mutant problem; second-order mutation
summary: Systematic literature review of techniques that detect, suggest or avoid equivalent mutants (17 techniques in 22 articles), plus an experiment comparing second-order mutation strategies against first-order mutation for reducing equivalent mutants.
relation_to_specdx: A seeded specification mutant that changes no admissible behaviour is an equivalent mutant and would be scored as a missed defect; SpecDx requires a kill witness (a behaviour or state separating mutant from original) for each seeded mutant, which is its answer to this problem.

title: Checked coverage: an indicator for oracle quality
authors: David Schuler; Andreas Zeller
venue: Software Testing, Verification and Reliability
subtopics: oracle quality; checked coverage
summary: Journal version of checked coverage: the dynamic slice of covered statements that influence an oracle, evaluated as an indicator of oracle quality that also reveals parts of the computation left unchecked.
relation_to_specdx: Same relation as the ICST paper: structural detection of unchecked state, versus SpecDx's statistical detection of weak checks over agent runs.

title: What good are strong specifications?
authors: Nadia Polikarpova; Carlo A. Furia; Yu Pei; Yi Wei; Bertrand Meyer
venue: 2013 35th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: specification strength; contracts; weak specifications
summary: Studies the cost and benefit of writing strong (complete functional) contracts in Eiffel compared with typical weak contracts, showing stronger specifications reveal more faults with tools such as automated testing and verification.
relation_to_specdx: Empirical evidence that weak specifications let faults pass, the program-level counterpart of SpecDx's Weak check type.

title: Automated oracle creation support, or: How I learned to stop worrying about fault propagation and love mutation testing
authors: Matt Staats; Gregory Gay; Mats P. E. Heimdahl
venue: 2012 34th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: oracle creation; mutation testing
summary: Supports oracle creation by using mutation analysis to rank which program variables an oracle should check, so that a small expected-value oracle detects most faults.
relation_to_specdx: Chooses which state to check by mutant sensitivity; in SpecDx terms it proposes where clauses should exist, whereas SpecDx flags where existing clauses are too loose (weak check) using behavioural evidence.

title: An Analysis and Survey of the Development of Mutation Testing
authors: Yue Jia; Mark Harman
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: mutation testing survey
summary: Comprehensive survey of three decades of mutation testing: approaches, tools, empirical results, and trend analyses showing the technique maturing toward practical applicability.
relation_to_specdx: Standard reference for the mutation-analysis methodology that SpecDx's seeded-defect evaluation borrows; SpecDx mutates specifications (T and C) and measures diagnosis (typed, localised) rather than test-suite adequacy.

title: A Theory of Mutations with Applications to Vacuity, Coverage, and Fault Tolerance
authors: Orna Kupferman; Wenchao Li; Sanjit A. Seshia
venue: 2008 Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design
subtopics: vacuity; coverage; mutation theory
summary: Develops a theory of mutations of finite-state systems and specifications, unifying vacuity and coverage checks (both evaluate specification quality through mutations) and showing how orders among mutations improve specifications and reason about fault-tolerance coverage.
relation_to_specdx: Theoretical grounding for using specification and system mutations to evaluate specification quality; relevant to designing SpecDx's mutation operators and their subsumption, though SpecDx's mutants are on SQL clauses and NL requirements.

title: Mutating database queries
authors: Javier Tuya; Ma José Suárez-Cabal; Claudio de la Riva
venue: Information and Software Technology
subtopics: SQL mutation; mutation operators
summary: Defines mutation operators for SQL SELECT queries covering many SQL features including NULL handling, evaluated on NIST SQL conformance queries, with selective mutation and mutant ordering to cut cost; usable to assess database test adequacy or to inject faults.
relation_to_specdx: Operator catalogue directly applicable to mutating SpecDx's SQL invariants and policy functions when seeding weak-check and hidden-requirement defects.

title: The Daikon system for dynamic detection of likely invariants
authors: Michael D. Ernst; Jeff H. Perkins; Philip J. Guo; Stephen McCamant; Carlos Pacheco; Matthew S. Tschantz; Chen Xiao
venue: Science of Computer Programming
subtopics: specification inference; likely invariants
summary: Describes Daikon, which runs a program (or reads record-structured data), observes computed values and reports properties true over the observed executions as likely invariants (constants, ranges, linear relations, orderings, containment, sortedness, etc.); outputs have been used for test generation, data-stream validity checking and more.
relation_to_specdx: Inferring invariants from runs and comparing them with declared clauses is a natural non-statistical baseline for weak checks and hidden requirements; SpecDx instead models fallible readings with an anchored, set-valued truth model and interpreter accuracy, and also types contradictions and ambiguities.
baseline_notes: Daikon accepts record-structured data, so it can run on SpecDx runs directly: dump the end-state rows (and per-step cell reads) of runs that the population or golden state deems correct as Daikon traces, infer likely invariants, then diff against C. Inferred invariants that no clause implies are weak-check candidates; declared clauses falsified by many correct runs are hidden-requirement candidates. No interpreter statistics, no typing of ambiguity/contradiction. Code: codespecs/daikon (Java, actively maintained); 267 stars, last push 2026-10.

title: Sanity Checks in Formal Verification
authors: Orna Kupferman
venue: CONCUR 2006 - Concurrency Theory, LNCS 4137
subtopics: vacuity detection; coverage; sanity checks; survey
summary: Surveys sanity checks for passed verification: vacuity (the specification is satisfied trivially) and coverage (parts of the system unused by the specification), arguing both amount to re-verifying with mutated specifications or mutated systems.
relation_to_specdx: Frames specification-quality checks as mutation-based re-verification, the same framing SpecDx's evaluation uses; SpecDx applies it to executable business specifications with an LLM-population oracle rather than a model checker.

title: Coverage Metrics for Temporal Logic Model Checking
authors: Hana Chockler; Orna Kupferman; Moshe Y. Vardi
venue: Tools and Algorithms for the Construction and Analysis of Systems (TACAS 2001), LNCS 2031
subtopics: specification coverage; model checking; weak specifications
summary: Proposes coverage metrics for model checking that ask how complete a specification is, by modifying (mutating) the system and checking which parts were relevant for verification to succeed; distinguishes state-based vs logic-based coverage and system vs environment, with algorithms to find uncovered parts.
relation_to_specdx: Specification incompleteness measured by system mutations is the formal-methods analogue of SpecDx's weak-check detection (behaviour that differs yet still passes all clauses); SpecDx obtains such behaviour from fallible LLM executors instead of syntactic system mutations.

title: Dynamically discovering likely program invariants to support program evolution
authors: Michael D. Ernst; Jake Cockrell; William G. Griswold; David Notkin
venue: Proceedings of the 21st international conference on Software engineering
subtopics: specification inference; likely invariants
summary: Original Daikon paper: dynamically discovers likely program invariants from execution traces to support program evolution.
relation_to_specdx: Foundation for inferring specifications from behaviour; SpecDx infers an entailment set per cell from fallible LLM behaviours instead of trusted program traces.

title: Using model checking to generate tests from specifications
authors: Paul E Ammann; Paul E Black; William Majurski
venue: NIST Interagency/Internal Report (NISTIR) 6166, National Institute of Standards and Technology
subtopics: specification mutation; model checking; test generation
summary: Applies syntactic mutation operators to a model-checker specification; the model checker produces counterexamples distinguishing each mutant from the original, which become complete test cases with inputs and expected results, in two classes (tests a correct implementation must fail or must pass).
relation_to_specdx: Origin of the kill-witness idea for specification mutants: a counterexample separating mutant and original. SpecDx's kill witnesses play the same role for seeded business-spec defects, but are found by symbolic search on PostgreSQL or directed LLM probes.

title: Efficient detection of vacuity in ACTL formulas
authors: Ilan Beer; Shoham Ben-David; Cindy Eisner; Yoav Rodeh
venue: Computer Aided Verification (CAV 1997), LNCS 1254
subtopics: vacuity detection; model checking; witnesses
summary: Formalises vacuity and interesting witnesses (e.g. antecedent failure making an implication trivially true) and gives an efficient detection and witness-generation procedure for a useful subset of ACTL.
relation_to_specdx: Introduces the idea that a passing check needs a witness of non-trivial satisfaction; SpecDx's sound refutation similarly attaches witness states to candidate defects.

title: Alloy Repair Hint Generation Based on Historical Data
authors: Ana Barros; Henrique Neto; Alcino Cunha; Nuno Macedo; Ana C. R. Paiva
venue: Formal Methods (FM 2024), LNCS
subtopics: Alloy4Fun; hints; specification repair
summary: Data-driven next-step hint generation for novices writing Alloy specifications, built from historical Alloy4Fun submissions.
relation_to_specdx: Uses historical faulty-to-correct specification edits; analogous to SpecDx mining TonomyX history for real defects, but for education rather than diagnosis.

title: EvoSpex: An Evolutionary Algorithm for Learning Postconditions
authors: Facundo Molina; Pablo Ponzio; Nazareno Aguirre; Marcelo Frias
venue: 2021 IEEE/ACM 43rd International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: specification inference; postconditions; mutation
summary: EvoSpex learns method postconditions with an evolutionary algorithm that uses valid executions and mutation-generated invalid executions as positive and negative evidence.
relation_to_specdx: Learns specifications from executions labelled valid/invalid; SpecDx instead takes the specification as given and asks which clauses disagree with the behaviour of competent interpreters.

title: AUnit: A Test Automation Tool for Alloy
authors: Allison Sullivan; Kaiyuan Wang; Sarfraz Khurshid
venue: 2018 IEEE 11th International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation (ICST)
subtopics: Alloy; specification testing; coverage
summary: AUnit extension of the Alloy Analyzer: grammar for test cases (valuations) of Alloy models, test execution, test-suite coverage and automatic test generation.
relation_to_specdx: Unit tests for specifications, i.e. checking a specification against expected instances; SpecDx uses agent behaviours as unlabelled 'tests' of the specification instead of hand-written expected instances.

title: Will my tests tell me if I break this code?
authors: Rainer Niedermayr; Elmar Juergens; Stefan Wagner
venue: Proceedings of the International Workshop on Continuous Software Evolution and Delivery
subtopics: pseudo-tested methods; extreme mutation
summary: Introduces pseudo-tested methods, detected by removing a method's body and checking whether any covering test fails, as a sign of inadequate test oracles.
relation_to_specdx: Extreme mutation to expose missing checks; SpecDx's weak-check detection does not need a mutated implementation, only agent runs that pass all clauses yet deviate from T.

title: Assertions are strongly correlated with test suite effectiveness
authors: Yucheng Zhang; Ali Mesbah
venue: Proceedings of the 2015 10th Joint Meeting on Foundations of Software Engineering
subtopics: assertions; test effectiveness
summary: Shows that the number and kind of assertions in tests correlate strongly with mutation-based test-suite effectiveness, more than test-suite size.
relation_to_specdx: Context: oracle strength, not coverage, determines fault detection; SpecDx's clauses are the oracle of the benchmark, so their strength determines what wrong agent behaviour is caught.

title: Trivial Compiler Equivalence: A Large Scale Empirical Study of a Simple, Fast and Effective Equivalent Mutant Detection Technique
authors: Mike Papadakis; Yue Jia; Mark Harman; Yves Le Traon
venue: 2015 IEEE/ACM 37th IEEE International Conference on Software Engineering
subtopics: equivalent mutant problem; duplicate mutants
summary: Proposes Trivial Compiler Equivalence (TCE), which flags equivalent and duplicated mutants by comparing compiled binaries, and evaluates it on large open-source and benchmark programs.
relation_to_specdx: Cheap equivalence filter for program mutants; the analogue for SQL clause mutants would be checking semantic equivalence of mutated clauses (e.g. by query-equivalence or SMT) before requiring a kill witness, which SpecDx does by search rather than by compilation.

title: Mutation-driven generation of unit tests and oracles
authors: Gordon Fraser; Andreas Zeller
venue: Proceedings of the 19th international symposium on Software testing and analysis
subtopics: mutation testing; oracle generation
summary: Generates unit tests and minimal assertion oracles that kill mutants of object-oriented classes, so test suites target defects rather than coverage.
relation_to_specdx: Kill-driven oracle synthesis; SpecDx uses mutant killing only for evaluation (each seeded spec defect needs a kill witness), not for generating clauses.

title: Testing with model checkers: a survey
authors: Gordon Fraser; Franz Wotawa; Paul E. Ammann
venue: Software Testing, Verification and Reliability
subtopics: model checking; test generation; specification mutation
summary: Surveys a decade of work that uses model-checker counterexamples as test cases, including coverage- and mutation-based test generation from specifications, and lists open problems.
relation_to_specdx: Background for witness generation from specifications; SpecDx's refutation step similarly searches for witness states, but on SQL clauses over a live database.

title: A specification-based coverage metric to evaluate test sets
authors: Paul E Ammann; Paul E Black
venue: NIST Interagency/Internal Report (NISTIR) 6403, National Institute of Standards and Technology
subtopics: specification mutation; specification coverage; model checking
summary: Defines a specification-based coverage metric for test sets, computed with a model checker over mutants of the specification, to assure that a test set is sensitive to the structure of the specification.
relation_to_specdx: Measures test-set adequacy against a trusted specification; SpecDx inverts the trust direction and uses behaviours to assess whether the specification is adequate.

title: Delta Debugging for Cyber-Physical Systems with Flaky Test Executions
authors: Pablo Valle; Shaukat Ali; Aitor Arrieta
venue: arXiv
subtopics: delta debugging; flaky tests; stochastic oracle
summary: Presents three delta debugging algorithms for stochastic cyber-physical systems that combine statistical failure analysis, repeated executions and environment-aware reduction to isolate minimal failure-inducing inputs despite flaky executions.
relation_to_specdx: One of few works on ddmin with a non-deterministic oracle, which is SpecDx's situation (an LLM population). SpecDx's oracle is a statistical test over interpreters rather than repeated simulator runs.

title: Delta Debugging for LLM-integrated Systems
authors: Hao-Nan Zhu; Muhammad Numair Mansur; Martin Schäf; Zeya Chen; Tancrède Lepoint; Willem Visser
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering: Software Engineering in Practice
subtopics: delta debugging; LLM prompts; semantic markers
summary: Investigates delta debugging of natural-language instruction prompts in LLM-integrated systems: semantic markers embedded in the input and traced through chain-of-thought identify causal fragments, letting delta debugging isolate minimal prompt subsets responsible for incorrect outputs in development and production benchmarks.
relation_to_specdx: Closest prior art for SpecDx step 5: ddmin over the natural-language text that instructs an LLM, with LLM behaviour as the oracle. It debugs one system's prompt for a known wrong output; SpecDx reduces a specification T to localise ambiguity, defined by disagreement across a population of interpreters.

title: Probabilistic Delta debugging
authors: Guancheng Wang; Ruobing Shen; Junjie Chen; Yingfei Xiong; Lu Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the 29th ACM Joint Meeting on European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering
subtopics: probabilistic delta debugging; ProbDD; Bayesian optimisation
summary: ProbDD replaces ddmin's fixed partitioning with a probabilistic model of how likely each element is to be kept, selecting deletions that maximise expected gain and updating the model from test outcomes; it reduces programs faster and to smaller results than ddmin and CHISEL.
relation_to_specdx: A query-efficient minimiser that suits SpecDx's expensive population oracle; neither ProbDD nor its follow-ups model an oracle that is itself noisy, which SpecDx's LLM committee is.
baseline_notes: Drop-in alternative to ddmin for SpecDx step 5. Input: the list of sentences of T and a property test psi(T') = "the LLM population still splits into two readings on the ambiguous cell when given T'". ProbDD keeps a per-sentence probability of being essential and chooses which subset to delete to maximise expected gain, typically needing fewer oracle calls (each call = a population run, so cost matters). Caveat: ProbDD assumes a deterministic oracle; with a noisy population oracle, repeat or threshold the test. Code: Amocy-Wang/ProbDD (replication, C/Python, GPL-3.0, last push 2021); ProbDD/CDD are also simple to reimplement.

title: Model-Based Diagnosis with Uncertain Observations
authors: Dean Cazes; Meir Kalech
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: model-based diagnosis; uncertain observations; noisy sensors
summary: Formalises model-based diagnosis when observations come from noisy sensors that return incorrect values with known probability, for both consistency-based and abductive models; gives two complete algorithms that find and rank all diagnoses and a third that returns the most probable diagnosis directly.
relation_to_specdx: The closest MBD prior art to SpecDx's noisy setting: SpecDx's "sensors" are LLM interpreters whose readings are wrong with model-dependent probability. Cazes and Kalech assume known sensor error rates; SpecDx estimates interpreter accuracy and item difficulty jointly (IRT-style) and uses the specification as an anchor. | See the AAAI 2020 version: the nearest MBD formulation of SpecDx's noisy-reader setting, with known rather than estimated error rates.

title: Model-Based Diagnosis with Multiple Observations
authors: Alexey Ignatiev; Antonio Morgado; Georg Weissenbacher; Joao Marques-Silva
venue: Proceedings of the Twenty-Eighth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: model-based diagnosis; multiple observations; MaxSAT
summary: Shows that existing approaches for jointly diagnosing multiple observations (e.g. many failing tests in continuous integration) fail to compute the set of minimal diagnoses, corrects them, and proposes a new algorithm with large performance gains.
relation_to_specdx: Closest formal analogue of SpecDx's setting, where many runs (observations) must be jointly diagnosed over a common clause set. Ignatiev et al. treat every observation as correct; SpecDx must tolerate observations corrupted by interpreter errors and separate them statistically before hitting.

title: PySAT: A Python Toolkit for Prototyping with SAT Oracles
authors: Alexey Ignatiev; Antonio Morgado; Joao Marques-Silva
venue: Theory and Applications of Satisfiability Testing – SAT 2018 (LNCS)
subtopics: SAT toolkit; MUS/MCS; hitting sets
summary: Presents PySAT, a Python toolkit giving a simple API to several state-of-the-art SAT oracles plus cardinality encodings, aimed at fast prototyping of SAT-based problem-solving methods (MUS/MCS extraction, MaxSAT, hitting sets).
relation_to_specdx: Likely implementation substrate for SpecDx's hitting-set step and for symbolic baselines; it supplies algorithms, not the statistical treatment of noisy correction sets.
baseline_notes: Practical engine for both SpecDx step 3 and a B5 baseline. pysat.examples provides MUSX, LBX/MCSls (MCS enumeration), OptUx/RC2 (MaxSAT) and a Hitman minimal-hitting-set enumerator. (a) Baseline: run LBX/MCSls + Hitman on a CNF/MaxSAT encoding of C to enumerate MUSes symbolically. (b) Ablation: feed the observed violated-clause sets to Hitman as sets to hit (hard) versus SpecDx's soft hitting. MIT licence, pip-installable, offline.

title: Fast, flexible MUS enumeration
authors: Mark H. Liffiton; Alessandro Previti; Ammar Malik; Joao Marques-Silva
venue: Constraints
subtopics: MUS enumeration; MARCO; anytime enumeration
summary: Presents MARCO, an anytime algorithm that enumerates MUSes and MCSes of any constraint system by exploring the power set with a map formula, producing MUSes steadily with per-MUS cost close to a single MUS extraction.
relation_to_specdx: Ready-made symbolic contradiction finder that SpecDx can be compared with on the same clause set: MARCO needs a formal encoding of C and finds only logical contradictions, whereas SpecDx works from executed behaviours and also types hidden requirements, ambiguity and weak checks.
baseline_notes: B5 analogue. Input: the clause set C encoded as constraints (SAT/SMT, e.g. via z3 over the PostgreSQL schema domain). Output: MUSes = contradiction sets and MCSes, with no interpreters. Adaptation: encode each clause of C as a soft group over the finite domain of the scenario state; MARCO enumerates MUSes/MCSes anytime. It finds only contradictions that are expressible symbolically (no hidden requirements, ambiguity or weak checks). Code: liffiton/MARCO (Python driver, MiniSat/MUSer2 back-ends), maintained, runs offline.

title: Minimal Sets over Monotone Predicates in Boolean Formulae
authors: Joao Marques-Silva; Mikoláš Janota; Anton Belov
venue: Computer Aided Verification: CAV 2013 (LNCS 8044)
subtopics: minimal sets over monotone predicates; MUS; MCS; unification
summary: Shows that computing MUSes, MCSes, prime implicates and minimal models are all instances of finding a minimal set subject to a monotone predicate (MSMP), solvable by the same algorithms, and gives an asymptotically optimal MSMP algorithm that beats state-of-the-art MUS extractors.
relation_to_specdx: MSMP unifies SpecDx's two minimisation steps: MUS candidates over clauses (step 3) and ddmin over sentences of T (step 5) are both minimal sets for a monotone predicate; SpecDx's predicates are statistical and only approximately monotone.

title: On Computing Minimal Correction Subsets
authors: Joao Marques-Silva; Federico Heras; Mikolas Janota; Alessandro Previti; Anton Belov
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2013)
subtopics: MCS computation; CLD; MaxSAT
summary: Shows that existing MCS algorithms (MaxSAT-based or iterative SAT) can be inefficient, develops techniques to speed them up and proposes a new algorithm (clause D, CLD) for computing minimal correction subsets, evaluated as the most efficient and robust.
relation_to_specdx: Defines the MCS object that SpecDx samples from behaviour; in a B5 baseline the MCSes of C would be computed with these algorithms instead of being observed.

title: Exploring the Duality in Conflict-Directed Model-Based Diagnosis
authors: Roni Stern; Meir Kalech; Alexander Feldman; Gregory Provan
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-12)
subtopics: model-based diagnosis; conflict-diagnosis duality; hitting sets
summary: Exploits the duality that a diagnosis is a hitting set of conflicts and a conflict is a hitting set of diagnoses, interleaving the search for both; the resulting algorithm finds minimal-cardinality diagnoses faster than Conflict-Directed A*.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx uses exactly this duality in reverse: sampled correction sets (diagnosis-like objects) are hit to obtain conflict (MUS) candidates. SpecDx adds soft (noise-tolerant) hitting and sound refutation, which the deterministic setting does not need.

title: Cause clue clauses: error localization using maximum satisfiability
authors: Manu Jose; Rupak Majumdar
venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGPLAN Conference on Programming Language Design and Implementation
subtopics: error localisation; MaxSAT; MCS; BugAssist
summary: BugAssist encodes a bounded unrolling of a C program plus a failing test and the assertion as an unsatisfiable formula, uses MAX-SAT to find a maximal satisfiable set of clauses, and reports the complement (a minimal correction set) as the likely cause of the error.
relation_to_specdx: Error localisation as MCS computation over a formula that a failing execution makes unsatisfiable is the logical core SpecDx reuses at the specification level; BugAssist trusts its test oracle, while SpecDx's "tests" are behaviours of fallible interpreters.

title: Diagnosing multiple intermittent failures using maximum likelihood estimation
authors: Rui Abreu; Arjan J.C. van Gemund
venue: Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: intermittent failures; maximum likelihood; Bayesian diagnosis; Barinel
summary: Intermittent-failure models give each faulty component a probability of behaving correctly; Barinel estimates these unknown parameters by maximum likelihood within the Bayesian computation of posterior candidate probabilities, outperforming persistent and earlier intermittent models on synthetic systems, Siemens and real programs.
relation_to_specdx: Jointly estimating per-component goodness and candidate posteriors from noisy pass/fail spectra parallels SpecDx's joint estimation of interpreter accuracy and cell entailment sets. Barinel has no notion of interpreter ability or item difficulty and no anchor, so it cannot separate "the specification is wrong" from "the executor is weak".

title: Spectrum-Based Multiple Fault Localization
authors: Rui Abreu; Peter Zoeteweij; Arjan J.C. van Gemund
venue: 2009 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: spectrum-based fault localisation; Bayesian diagnosis; intermittent faults; Barinel
summary: Proposes Barinel, which models a program by abstractions of execution traces (as in SFL) and uses Bayesian reasoning to compute multiple-fault candidates and their probabilities (as in MBD), with a probabilistic component model in which faulty components may fail intermittently.
relation_to_specdx: Barinel is the most direct "statistics + hitting sets" precedent: candidates are minimal hitting sets of failing spectra, ranked by a noise-aware likelihood. SpecDx differs by diagnosing a specification rather than code, by modelling interpreter accuracy and item difficulty, by using the specification as an anchor, and by typing defects and refuting candidates with witnesses.
baseline_notes: Spectrum mapping: one component = one clause c in C (or one cell), one test = one interpreter run r (model m, scenario s); A[r,c]=1 if clause c was evaluated/active in run r, and the error vector e[r]=1 if run r violated at least one clause (or, finer, one spectrum per clause with e = violation of that clause). Barinel computes minimal hitting sets of failing runs (Staccato) and ranks multi-clause candidates by a Bayesian posterior with per-component goodness h_c (probability a faulty component still passes), which absorbs intermittent agent errors. Output: ranked clause sets; it does not type defects or use anchors. Code: original Zoltar toolset is archived (ncfxy/zoltar, C++); the algorithm (Staccato + gradient ascent on h) is short to reimplement in Python offline.

title: Algorithms for Computing Minimal Unsatisfiable Subsets of Constraints
authors: Mark H. Liffiton; Karem A. Sakallah
venue: Journal of Automated Reasoning
subtopics: MUS enumeration; MCS; hitting-set duality; CAMUS
summary: Gives a sound and complete algorithm (CAMUS) for all MUSes of an unsatisfiable constraint system, based on the relationship between satisfiable and unsatisfiable subsets: all MCSes are computed first, and the MUSes are their minimal hitting sets.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's step 3 is CAMUS's second phase applied to sampled, noisy correction sets instead of exactly computed MCSes. Running CAMUS on the SQL/clause encoding of C would give the exact symbolic answer (a B5-style baseline) when the clauses can be encoded.

title: Conflict-based Diagnosis: Adding Uncertainty to Model-based Diagnosis
authors: Ildikó Flesch; Peter Lucas; Theo van der Weide
venue: Proceedings of the 20th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2007)
subtopics: consistency-based diagnosis; uncertainty; Bayesian networks; conflict measure
summary: Represents logical diagnostic systems in a probabilistic (Bayesian-network) theory and shows that consistent and inconsistent states can still be determined as in consistency-based diagnosis, while a Bayesian conflict measure ranks diagnoses, adding uncertainty reasoning to consistency-based diagnosis.
relation_to_specdx: A "soft conflict" view of consistency-based diagnosis, close to SpecDx's soft hitting sets over noisy correction sets; SpecDx's uncertainty comes from fallible interpreters rather than component behaviour, and it adds witness refutation.

title: Discovery of Minimal Unsatisfiable Subsets of Constraints Using Hitting Set Dualization
authors: James Bailey; Peter J. Stuckey
venue: Practical Aspects of Declarative Languages (LNCS)
subtopics: MUS enumeration; hitting set dualization; type-error diagnosis
summary: Discovers all minimal unsatisfiable subsets of a constraint set by hitting set dualization, alternating between maximal satisfiable subsets (whose complements are correction sets) and their minimal hitting sets (abstract not read; summary from title and citing literature).
relation_to_specdx: The dualization that SpecDx step 3 relies on (MUS = minimal hitting set of the MCS family) was introduced here for exact, solver-computed sets; SpecDx observes the MCS family noisily and so needs soft hitting.

title: Consistency-based diagnosis of configuration knowledge bases
authors: Alexander Felfernig; Gerhard Friedrich; Dietmar Jannach; Markus Stumptner
venue: Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: configuration knowledge bases; consistency-based diagnosis; test cases
summary: Shows that debugging configuration knowledge bases can be done by consistency-based diagnosis: valid (positive) and invalid (negative) examples serve as test cases, and diagnoses are minimal sets of knowledge-base constraints whose removal makes the knowledge base consistent with the examples; a conflict-based algorithm is given.
relation_to_specdx: Very close in spirit: a declarative specification (the knowledge base) is diagnosed with example behaviours, much as SpecDx diagnoses C with interpreter behaviours. Felfernig et al. need correctly labelled examples; SpecDx's behaviours come from fallible LLM interpreters and must be separated into specification defects and agent errors.

title: QUICKXPLAIN: Preferred Explanations and Relaxations for Over-Constrained Problems
authors: Ulrich Junker
venue: Proceedings of the 19th National Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI 2004)
subtopics: QuickXplain; preferred explanations; conflict extraction
summary: Defines preferred explanations (conflicts) and relaxations of over-constrained problems from user preferences between constraints and computes them with a generic divide-and-conquer method that works with any CP, SAT or description-logic solver.
relation_to_specdx: QuickXplain is the divide-and-conquer MUS extractor that is structurally the same as ddmin; SpecDx uses ddmin over sentences with an LLM-population oracle where QuickXplain uses a consistency checker.

title: Simplifying and isolating failure-inducing input
authors: A. Zeller; R. Hildebrandt
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: delta debugging; ddmin; input simplification
summary: Presents the ddmin algorithm, which simplifies a failing test case to a 1-minimal one that still fails, and dd, which isolates the minimal difference between a passing and a failing input; e.g. a Mozilla crash after 95 user actions is reduced to 3.
relation_to_specdx: The algorithm SpecDx applies to the sentences of T, with "the interpreter population still splits into two readings" as the test; ddmin assumes a deterministic, monotone oracle, which a population oracle only approximates.

title: A theory of diagnosis from first principles
authors: Raymond Reiter
venue: Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: model-based diagnosis; hitting sets; HS-tree
summary: Defines consistency-based diagnosis from first principles: given a logical system description and an observation that conflicts with intended behaviour, a diagnosis is a minimal set of components whose abnormality restores consistency; diagnoses are the minimal hitting sets of the conflict sets, computed with the HS-tree.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx step 3 rests on this duality: each LLM behaviour's violated-clause set plays the role of a conflict/correction set and minimal hitting sets give candidate MUSes. Reiter assumes noise-free observations and a known system description; SpecDx samples noisy correction sets from fallible interpreters and must refute candidates with witnesses.

title: Diagnosing multiple faults
authors: Johan de Kleer; Brian C. Williams
venue: Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: model-based diagnosis; GDE; measurement selection
summary: Introduces the General Diagnostic Engine (GDE), which diagnoses multiple faults by representing candidates through minimal sets of violated assumptions (minimal conflicts) and combines model-based prediction with probabilistic, entropy-based measurement selection to localise faults sequentially.
relation_to_specdx: Provides both the conflict/candidate machinery and the information-theoretic choice of the next measurement, which parallels SpecDx's hitting-set candidates and its Thompson-sampling scenario synthesis; GDE measures a physical device, whereas SpecDx "measures" by running LLM interpreters on synthesised scenarios.

title: DDOR: Delta Debugging for Explainable Overrefusal Testing and Repair
authors: Qinyan Zhou; Peixin Zhang; Jun Sun; Haonan Zhang; Dongxia Wang
venue: arXiv
subtopics: delta debugging; LLM prompts; overrefusal
summary: DDOR applies delta debugging to prompts in a black-box setting to localise minimal refusal-triggering fragments that explain why an LLM over-refuses a benign query, then uses them to generate overrefusal test suites and repair prompts.
relation_to_specdx: ddmin over natural-language text with an LLM as oracle, as in SpecDx step 5. DDOR localises fragments that trigger one model's refusal; SpecDx localises sentences of a specification that make a population of models split into two readings.

title: Accelerating Delta Debugging through Probabilistic Monotonicity Assessment
authors: Yonggang Tao; Jingling Xue
venue: Proceedings of the 29th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering
subtopics: delta debugging; monotonicity; probabilistic assessment
summary: Probabilistic Monotonicity Assessment (PMA) models whether the search space is monotone from prior tests and uses a confidence function to skip subsets probabilistically, cutting redundant tests of ddmin-style tools without hurting reduction quality.
relation_to_specdx: Monotonicity is doubtful for SpecDx's ambiguity predicate (removing a sentence can create or remove a reading); PMA is one of the few works that relaxes it.

title: LLM-based Satisfiability Checking of String Requirements by Consistent Data and Checker Generation
authors: Boqi Chen; Aren A. Babikian; Shuzhao Feng; Dániel Varró; Gunter Mussbacher
venue: 2025 IEEE 33rd International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
subtopics: satisfiability of NL requirements; LLM; checker generation; witnesses
summary: Hybrid approach that checks satisfiability of natural-language requirements over strings by having LLMs derive a verdict, generate consistent data (witnesses) and generate declarative (SMT) and imperative (Python) checkers that validate the outcome; this doubles generation success and F1 in some settings.
relation_to_specdx: Uses LLM-generated witness data validated by executable checkers to decide satisfiability of requirements, the same idea as SpecDx's refutation by witness states; it works on string requirements with one LLM, without population statistics or defect typing.

title: Toward a Better Understanding of Probabilistic Delta Debugging
authors: Mengxiao Zhang; Zhenyang Xu; Yongqiang Tian; Xinru Cheng; Chengnian Sun
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM 47th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: probabilistic delta debugging; CDD; theory
summary: First in-depth theoretical analysis of ProbDD, showing that its probabilities essentially act as monotonically increasing counters; proposes CDD, a much simpler counter-based variant that matches ProbDD on 76 minimisation and debloating benchmarks.
relation_to_specdx: CDD is the simplest query-efficient replacement for ddmin in SpecDx's ambiguity localisation.

title: WDD: Weighted Delta Debugging
authors: Xintong Zhou; Zhenyang Xu; Mengxiao Zhang; Yongqiang Tian; Chengnian Sun
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM 47th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: delta debugging; weighted partitioning; WDD
summary: WDD makes ddmin and ProbDD weight-aware: elements of a test input differ in size, so partitioning by weight rather than count improves efficiency and effectiveness of delta debugging.
relation_to_specdx: Relevant if SpecDx's units of T (sentences, paragraphs, tool descriptions) differ greatly in length.

title: Critical observations in model-based diagnosis
authors: Cody James Christopher; Alban Grastien
venue: Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: model-based diagnosis; critical observations; abstraction
summary: Defines a sub-observation as an abstraction of the observations and calls it sufficient if it yields the same minimal diagnosis; a critical observation is a maximally abstracted sufficient sub-observation, and the paper shows how to compute one for state-based and event-based observations.
relation_to_specdx: Minimising the observations needed to support a diagnosis mirrors SpecDx's ddmin over the sentences of T needed to sustain an ambiguity.

title: LPR: Large Language Models-Aided Program Reduction
authors: Mengxiao Zhang; Yongqiang Tian; Zhenyang Xu; Yiwen Dong; Shin Hwei Tan; Chengnian Sun
venue: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
subtopics: LLM-aided program reduction; LPR
summary: LPR alternates a language-generic reducer (Perses/Vulcan) with LLM-driven, language-specific program transformations, producing smaller programs than Vulcan on C, Rust and JavaScript benchmarks.
relation_to_specdx: LLMs used inside a reduction loop as transformers; SpecDx uses LLMs as the oracle of the reduction (does the ambiguity persist?), not as transformers.

title: DynamicHS: Streamlining Reiter’s Hitting-Set Tree for Sequential Diagnosis
authors: Patrick Rodler
venue: Information Sciences
subtopics: HS-tree; sequential diagnosis; stateful hitting-set search
summary: DynamicHS is a stateful variant of Reiter's HS-tree for sequential diagnosis that keeps the search tree between measurement iterations and minimises costly reasoner calls; it beats HS-tree in 96% of sessions while keeping its guarantees.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx also alternates hitting-set computation with new observations (new scenarios); incremental hitting-set maintenance like DynamicHS avoids recomputation as correction sets arrive.

title: Enhancing Self-Consistency and Performance of Pre-Trained Language Models through Natural Language Inference
authors: Eric Mitchell; Joseph Noh; Siyan Li; Will Armstrong; Ananth Agarwal; Patrick Liu; Chelsea Finn; Christopher Manning
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
subtopics: LLM self-consistency; MaxSAT; NLI; factor graph
summary: ConCoRD boosts the consistency and accuracy of pre-trained QA/VQA models by using an NLI model to detect relations between candidate answers to related questions and choosing a globally consistent set of answers with a MaxSAT solver over a factor graph, without fine-tuning.
relation_to_specdx: Combines statistics over many model outputs with weighted MaxSAT, as SpecDx combines population statistics with logic; ConCoRD repairs a model's beliefs assuming the questions are well posed, whereas SpecDx diagnoses the specification.

title: Fault localization via efficient probabilistic modeling of program semantics
authors: Muhan Zeng; Yiqian Wu; Zhentao Ye; Yingfei Xiong; Xin Zhang; Lu Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the 44th International Conference on Software Engineering
subtopics: probabilistic fault localisation; SmartFL; program semantics
summary: SmartFL models only the correctness of program values (not full semantics) with a probabilistic graphical model built from static analysis and execution traces, balancing the precision of semantic approaches and the scalability of SBFL; best top-1 accuracy on Defects4J.
relation_to_specdx: Probabilistic inference over the correctness of values (cells) from passing and failing runs is close to SpecDx's cell-level latent model; SmartFL localises code faults and trusts the test oracle, whereas SpecDx's observations come from fallible readers.

title: Random vs. Best-First: Impact of Sampling Strategies on Decision Making in Model-Based Diagnosis
authors: Patrick Rodler
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: model-based diagnosis; sampling diagnoses; information gain
summary: Empirically examines whether biased best-first samples of fault explanations, commonly used to estimate diagnosis probabilities and choose the most informative measurement, are representative, comparing random and best-first sampling methods and sample sizes.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx also estimates over sampled correction sets and chooses informative scenarios; this work questions the statistical validity of such samples in MBD.

title: MUST: Minimal Unsatisfiable Subsets Enumeration Tool
authors: Jaroslav Bendík; Ivana Černá
venue: Tools and Algorithms for the Construction and Analysis of Systems (LNCS)
subtopics: MUS enumeration; tool
summary: MUST is a tool that implements several domain-agnostic online MUS enumeration algorithms (MARCO, ReMUS, TOME) for SAT, SMT and LTL constraints in one framework.
relation_to_specdx: A runnable alternative to MARCO for a B5-style symbolic baseline on an SMT encoding of the clauses.

title: Simulating the Effect of Test Flakiness on Fault Localization Effectiveness
authors: Béla Vancsics; Tamás Gergely; Árpád Beszédes
venue: 2020 IEEE Workshop on Validation, Analysis and Evolution of Software Tests (VST)
subtopics: flaky tests; spectrum-based fault localisation; noisy outcomes
summary: Simulation study of how increasing levels of test flakiness (non-deterministic outcomes) degrade the effectiveness of spectrum-based fault localisation.
relation_to_specdx: Quantifies SFL under noisy test outcomes, the regime of SpecDx's interpreter x clause matrix; it motivates SpecDx's explicit noise model over plain suspiciousness ranking.

title: Binary reduction of dependency graphs
authors: Christian Gram Kalhauge; Jens Palsberg
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 27th ACM Joint Meeting on European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering
subtopics: binary reduction; dependency graphs; J-Reduce
summary: Recasts input reduction for inputs with internal dependencies as reduction of a dependency graph and introduces Binary Reduction (tool J-Reduce for Java bytecode), 12x faster than delta debugging with more reduction.
relation_to_specdx: If sentences of T depend on each other (definitions, cross-references), SpecDx's ddmin could reduce closures in a dependency graph as Binary Reduction does.

title: An Artificial Intelligence paradigm for troubleshooting software bugs
authors: Amir Elmishali; Roni Stern; Meir Kalech
venue: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: learn-diagnose-plan; software diagnosis; test planning
summary: LDP integrates machine-learned fault predictions (from code structure, history and past failures) as priors for automated software diagnosis, and automated planning of additional tests to improve diagnostic accuracy, demonstrated on real faults in four open-source projects.
relation_to_specdx: Same pipeline shape as SpecDx (priors -> diagnosis -> active test planning); LDP diagnoses code with Barinel-style reasoning, SpecDx diagnoses specifications with an IRT-style population model.

title: Core-Guided Minimal Correction Set and Core Enumeration
authors: Nina Narodytska; Nikolaj Bjørner; Maria-Cristina Marinescu; Mooly Sagiv
venue: Proceedings of the Twenty-Seventh International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: MCS enumeration; MUS enumeration; core-guided
summary: Proposes an algorithm that extracts minimal unsatisfiable cores and correction sets simultaneously within the relaxation-and-strengthening framework; the solver outperforms state-of-the-art MCS extractors and compares favourably on cores.
relation_to_specdx: Simultaneous MUS/MCS enumeration, a stronger symbolic engine for a B5-style baseline.

title: Recursive Online Enumeration of All Minimal Unsatisfiable Subsets
authors: Jaroslav Bendík; Ivana Černá; Nikola Beneš
venue: Automated Technology for Verification and Analysis (LNCS)
subtopics: MUS enumeration; online enumeration; domain-agnostic
summary: Recursive online algorithm (ReMUS) that enumerates MUSes one by one in any constraint domain, reducing the number of expensive satisfiability tests compared with earlier domain-agnostic enumerators.
relation_to_specdx: Domain-agnostic MUS enumeration only needs a satisfiability oracle, so in principle the oracle could be a witness search on PostgreSQL as in SpecDx's refutation step.

title: Spectrum-Based Fault Localization in Model Transformations
authors: Javier Troya; Sergio Segura; Jose Antonio Parejo; Antonio Ruiz-Cortés
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
subtopics: spectrum-based fault localisation; model transformations; rule localisation
summary: Applies SBFL to locate faulty rules in model transformations, using test cases and rule coverage, and compares 18 SBFL techniques; Kulczynski2, Mountford, Ochiai and Zoltar perform best.
relation_to_specdx: Shows SFL working on declarative rule sets rather than statements, close to SpecDx's clause-level spectra; tests are assumed to have correct oracles.

title: A Test-Suite Diagnosability Metric for Spectrum-Based Fault Localization Approaches
authors: Alexandre Perez; Rui Abreu; Arie van Deursen
venue: 2017 IEEE/ACM 39th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: diagnosability; test-suite adequacy; DDU
summary: Proposes DDU (density, diversity, uniqueness), a test-suite diagnosability metric that measures how well tests support spectrum-based fault localisation; optimising suites for DDU gives a 34% gain in SFL accuracy over branch coverage.
relation_to_specdx: Diagnosability of a spectrum matrix is what SpecDx's active scenario synthesis tries to maximise; DDU could serve as a cheap scenario-selection criterion or a diagnostic of the interpreter x clause matrix.

title: Evaluating and Improving Fault Localization
authors: Spencer Pearson; Jose Campos; Rene Just; Gordon Fraser; Rui Abreu; Michael D. Ernst; Deric Pang; Benjamin Keller
venue: 2017 IEEE/ACM 39th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: fault localisation evaluation; real faults; artificial faults
summary: Re-evaluates seven fault localisation techniques on both artificial (mutant) and real faults from Defects4J and finds that results on artificial faults do not carry over to real faults; proposes improved techniques.
relation_to_specdx: Directly informs SpecDx's evaluation design, which uses both seeded specification mutations and real defects; it warns that mutation-only results may not predict real-defect performance.

title: The Minimal Hitting Set Generation Problem: Algorithms and Computation
authors: Andrew Gainer-Dewar; Paola Vera-Licona
venue: SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics
subtopics: minimal hitting sets; enumeration algorithms; benchmark
summary: Surveys and benchmarks algorithms that generate all inclusion-minimal hitting sets (hypergraph transversals), comparing many implementations on diverse instances and giving guidance on which to use.
relation_to_specdx: Reference for choosing the hitting-set enumerator in SpecDx step 3 and for its complexity.

title: A Survey on Software Fault Localization
authors: W. Eric Wong; Ruizhi Gao; Yihao Li; Rui Abreu; Franz Wotawa
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: fault localisation; survey
summary: Comprehensive survey of software fault localisation techniques (spectrum-based, slicing, statistical, program-state, machine-learning and model-based), with key issues, concerns and evaluation practices.
relation_to_specdx: Reference survey for positioning SpecDx's clause-level localisation against code-level fault localisation.

title: Practical Improvements to the Minimizing Delta Debugging Algorithm
authors: Renáta Hodován; Ákos Kiss
venue: Proceedings of the 11th International Joint Conference on Software Technologies
subtopics: ddmin; parallel delta debugging; picire
summary: Revisits the minimizing delta debugging algorithm and proposes practical improvements, especially parallel testing of subsets and complements, with formal variants and pseudo-code; on more than 1000 real minimisation sessions, ddmin reaches 1-minimal results in a quarter to a fifth of the original time.
relation_to_specdx: Makes ddmin cheaper in oracle wall-clock time, the bottleneck when each test is a population of LLM runs.
baseline_notes: Implementation substrate (and ddmin reference) for SpecDx step 5. picire exposes ddmin with configurable splitting, caching and parallel subset testing; the test function can be any Python callable, so it can wrap SpecDx's population oracle ("does the two-reading split on cell c survive with sentences T'?"). Parallel testing matters because each oracle call runs a committee of local LLMs. Comparing picire ddmin against ProbDD/CDD on the same oracle gives the ambiguity-localisation ablation. Code: renatahodovan/picire, maintained (2026), Python, offline.

title: Cause reduction: delta debugging, even without bugs
authors: Alex Groce; Mohammad Amin Alipour; Chaoqiang Zhang; Yang Chen; John Regehr
venue: Software Testing, Verification and Reliability
subtopics: cause reduction; delta debugging generalisation
summary: Generalises delta debugging to cause reduction: tests are reduced while preserving an arbitrary effect (coverage, behaviour) rather than a failure, yielding effective quick test suites and better seeded symbolic execution.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's ddmin also preserves a non-failure property (the persistence of a two-reading split among interpreters), which is cause reduction in Groce et al.'s sense.

title: Efficient Model Based Diagnosis with Maximum Satisfiability
authors: Joao Marques-Silva; Mikoláš Janota; Alexey Ignatiev; Antonio Morgado
venue: Proceedings of the 24th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2015)
subtopics: model-based diagnosis; MaxSAT encoding
summary: Proposes an optimised MaxSAT encoding of model-based diagnosis, building on SAT-based MBD, plus a set of harder MBD benchmarks, with clear performance gains over the state of the art.
relation_to_specdx: MaxSAT is the natural engine for SpecDx's soft hitting sets (weighted, violable sets to hit); this paper shows MBD at scale through MaxSAT but with hard observations.

title: Literal-Based MCS Extraction
authors: Carlos Mencía; Alessandro Previti; Joao Marques-Silva
venue: Proceedings of the 24th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2015)
subtopics: MCS extraction; LBX; backbones; MaxSAT approximation
summary: Proposes LBX, a literal-based view of MCS extraction inspired by the link between MCSes and backbones, and techniques to approximate weighted partial MaxSAT by selective MCS enumeration.
relation_to_specdx: LBX is implemented in PySAT (pysat.examples.lbx) and is the MCS enumerator a symbolic B5 baseline would use on SpecDx's clause set.

title: On the empirical evaluation of similarity coefficients for spreadsheets fault localization
authors: Birgit Hofer; Alexandre Perez; Rui Abreu; Franz Wotawa
venue: Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: spreadsheets; spectrum-based fault localisation; similarity coefficients
summary: Studies 42 similarity coefficients for SFL applied to spreadsheets (cells as components, correct/incorrect output cells as observations); Ochiai, Jaccard and Sorensen-Dice need the least inspection effort and are interchangeable.
relation_to_specdx: SFL on a declarative, cell-based artefact is a close analogue of SpecDx's cells; the observations here are user-judged output cells, assumed correct.

title: Smallest MUS Extraction with Minimal Hitting Set Dualization
authors: Alexey Ignatiev; Alessandro Previti; Mark Liffiton; Joao Marques-Silva
venue: Principles and Practice of Constraint Programming: CP 2015 (LNCS 9255)
subtopics: smallest MUS; hitting set dualization
summary: Computes a smallest MUS of an inconsistent constraint set by minimal hitting set dualization, exploiting the MUS/MCS duality (abstract not available to us; summary from title and citing descriptions).
relation_to_specdx: The implicit-hitting-set route from correction sets to a minimum MUS is the exact analogue of SpecDx's soft hitting over sampled correction sets.

title: Using Minimal Correction Sets to More Efficiently Compute Minimal Unsatisfiable Sets
authors: Fahiem Bacchus; George Katsirelos
venue: Computer Aided Verification (LNCS)
subtopics: MUS extraction; MCS duality
summary: Develops MUS algorithms that exploit the duality between correction subsets and unsatisfiable subsets, using MCS computation to compute MUSes more efficiently than previous methods.
relation_to_specdx: Same MCS-to-MUS direction as SpecDx step 3; SpecDx's MCSes are not computed by a solver but observed (noisily) as violated-clause sets of interpreter behaviours.

title: Using the wisdom of the crowds to find critical errors in biomedical ontologies: a study of SNOMED CT
authors: Jonathan M Mortensen; Evan P Minty; Michael Januszyk; Timothy E Sweeney; Alan L Rector; Natalya F Noy; Mark A Musen
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
subtopics: crowdsourced verification; ontology errors; Bayesian aggregation
summary: Crowdsources verification of SNOMED CT taxonomic relationships with micro-tasks and a Bayesian classifier; the crowd finds errors as well as a single expert at a quarter of the cost (kappa 0.58 vs 0.59 between experts) and reveals 39 previously unknown critical errors.
relation_to_specdx: A population of fallible raters, aggregated statistically, detects defects in a knowledge base, which is SpecDx's core statistical idea with humans instead of LLMs; it has no logical localisation, typing or witnesses.

title: Enumerating Infeasibility: Finding Multiple MUSes Quickly
authors: Mark H. Liffiton; Ammar Malik
venue: Integration of AI and OR Techniques in Constraint Programming for Combinatorial Optimization Problems (LNCS)
subtopics: MUS enumeration; MARCO
summary: Conference version of MARCO: enumerates multiple MUSes quickly by exploring the power set of constraints with a map formula, giving MUSes and MCSes incrementally.
relation_to_specdx: Earlier form of the MARCO baseline; see the Constraints 2016 journal version.

title: Metamorphic slice: An application in spectrum-based fault localization
authors: Xiaoyuan Xie; W. Eric Wong; Tsong Yueh Chen; Baowen Xu
venue: Information and Software Technology
subtopics: spectrum-based fault localisation; oracle problem; metamorphic testing
summary: Alleviates the test-oracle problem of SBFL with metamorphic slices, so that spectrum-based formulas can be applied when per-test pass/fail verdicts are unavailable (abstract not read; summary from descriptions of the work).
relation_to_specdx: SBFL without ground-truth verdicts is SpecDx's situation (no human labels); SpecDx replaces the oracle with agreement structure across interpreters and the specification anchor instead of metamorphic relations.

title: RIO: Minimizing User Interaction in Ontology Debugging
authors: Patrick Rodler; Kostyantyn Shchekotykhin; Philipp Fleiss; Gerhard Friedrich
venue: Web Reasoning and Rule Systems (LNCS)
subtopics: interactive ontology debugging; risk-aware query selection
summary: RIO adapts interactive ontology debugging to unreliable fault-probability meta-information by learning a risk-optimised query-selection strategy, balancing entropy-based and no-risk (split-in-half) strategies.
relation_to_specdx: Addresses the reliability of probabilistic guidance in sequential diagnosis, a concern SpecDx shares when its interpreter accuracies are estimated rather than known.

title: An efficient diagnosis algorithm for inconsistent constraint sets
authors: A. Felfernig; M. Schubert; C. Zehentner
venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing
subtopics: FastDiag; constraint diagnosis; preferred diagnoses
summary: Introduces FastDiag, a divide-and-conquer algorithm that directly computes preferred minimal diagnoses (sets of faulty constraints to delete) of an inconsistent constraint set or knowledge base without computing conflicts first, and compares it to conflict-directed hitting-set computation.
relation_to_specdx: FastDiag is the MCS-side counterpart of QuickXplain and, like ddmin, a divide-and-conquer minimiser over a monotone predicate; SpecDx could use it to compute a single preferred correction set, but its oracle is a consistency check, not a noisy LLM population.

title: Interactive ontology debugging: Two query strategies for efficient fault localization
authors: Kostyantyn Shchekotykhin; Gerhard Friedrich; Philipp Fleiss; Patrick Rodler
venue: Journal of Web Semantics
subtopics: interactive ontology debugging; query selection; entropy
summary: Interactive ontology debugging that identifies the target diagnosis by asking an oracle (the user) about entailments of the intended ontology, with split-in-half and entropy-based query selection that exploits fault probabilities of typical user errors.
relation_to_specdx: Sequential, information-gain-driven discrimination among diagnoses, as in SpecDx's active scenario synthesis; the oracle here is a human assumed to answer correctly, whereas SpecDx's oracle is a noisy LLM committee.

title: A model for spectra-based software diagnosis
authors: Lee Naish; Hua Jie Lee; Kotagiri Ramamohanarao
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
subtopics: spectrum-based fault localisation; ranking metrics; theory
summary: Builds a simple single-bug model program to analyse spectral ranking metrics in idealised conditions, identifies groups of equivalent metrics and derives an optimal ranking metric that also performs best on Siemens and Space benchmarks.
relation_to_specdx: Spectral suspiciousness metrics (Ochiai, Naish, etc.) are trivial baselines on SpecDx's interpreter x clause matrix; they rank clauses but cannot distinguish specification defects from agent errors.

title: Solving MAXSAT by Solving a Sequence of Simpler SAT Instances
authors: Jessica Davies; Fahiem Bacchus
venue: Principles and Practice of Constraint Programming: CP 2011 (LNCS 6876)
subtopics: MaxSAT; implicit hitting sets; MaxHS
summary: New MaxSAT algorithm that solves a sequence of simpler SAT instances: it collects cores (conflicting soft clauses) and computes minimum-cost hitting sets of them, avoiding the growing difficulty and weighting problems of earlier SAT-sequence approaches; the basis of MaxHS.
relation_to_specdx: Implicit hitting sets with weights is the algorithmic template for SpecDx's soft (weighted) minimal hitting sets over observed correction sets.

title: A Model-Based Active Testing Approach to Sequential Diagnosis
authors: A. Feldman; G. Provan; A. Van Gemund
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research
subtopics: active testing; sequential diagnosis; MBD
summary: FRACTAL combines MBD with automated test pattern generation to choose control inputs (test vectors) that most reduce the number of remaining minimal-cardinality diagnoses, with a greedy approximation FRACTAL-G.
relation_to_specdx: Active test selection to discriminate diagnoses, the MBD counterpart of SpecDx's scenario synthesis; SpecDx chooses business scenarios by Thompson sampling over a statistical model.

title: Approximate Model-Based Diagnosis Using Greedy Stochastic Search
authors: A. Feldman; G. Provan; A. Van Gemund
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research
subtopics: model-based diagnosis; stochastic search; approximate diagnosis
summary: Proposes SAFARI, a stochastic greedy fault diagnosis algorithm that trades guarantees of minimality for speed, achieving orders-of-magnitude speedups on ISCAS-85 and 74XXX circuits and proving optimality for some fault models.
relation_to_specdx: An approximate route to diagnoses when exact hitting-set enumeration is too costly, relevant if SpecDx's clause sets grow large; SpecDx's approximation is statistical (soft hitting under noise), not search-based.

title: Automated analysis of feature models 20 years later: A literature review
authors: David Benavides; Sergio Segura; Antonio Ruiz-Cortés
venue: Information Systems
subtopics: feature models; automated analysis; anomaly detection; survey
summary: Literature review of 20 years of automated analysis of feature models, cataloguing analysis operations (including detection and explanation of anomalies such as void models, dead and false-optional features), techniques (SAT, CSP, BDD) and tools.
relation_to_specdx: Feature-model anomalies (void model = contradiction, dead feature, false-optional) form a defect taxonomy for a declarative variability specification and are found symbolically; SpecDx targets executable business specifications and finds defects from executed LLM behaviour.

title: Minimal Unsatisfiability: Models, Algorithms and Applications (Invited Paper)
authors: Joao Marques-Silva
venue: 2010 40th IEEE International Symposium on Multiple-Valued Logic
subtopics: minimal unsatisfiability; survey; MUS algorithms
summary: Invited survey paper on minimal unsatisfiability: models (MUS, MCS, MSS), algorithms for their extraction and enumeration, and applications (abstract not read; summary from title and venue record).
relation_to_specdx: Survey entry point for MUS/MCS concepts used in SpecDx's contradiction step.

title: A Low-Cost Approximate Minimal Hitting Set Algorithm and its Application to Model-Based Diagnosis
authors: Rui Abreu; Arjan J. C. van Gemund
venue: Proceedings of the Eighth Symposium on Abstraction, Reformulation, and Approximation (SARA 2009), AAAI Press
subtopics: approximate minimal hitting sets; Staccato; SFL heuristic
