Inputs: the scenario generator and committee executions. Code: testingautomated-usi/deepjanus (MIT, Python; tied to its BeamNG/MNIST models, so only the search loop is reusable).

title: Simple Bayesian Algorithms for Best-Arm Identification
authors: Daniel Russo
venue: Operations Research
subtopics: best-arm identification; top-two Thompson sampling; pure exploration
summary: Studies adaptive allocation of measurement effort to identify the best of a finite set of designs from noisy signals (pure exploration), proposes several simple Bayesian allocation algorithms (top-two sampling rules built on Thompson sampling), and characterises asymptotic limits showing these algorithms are in a formal sense the best possible.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's objective is identification (which cells are defective, and of what type), not regret, so plain Thompson sampling over-exploits; top-two Thompson sampling is the principled pure-exploration fix and a cheap ablation of the selector.

title: Variational Bayesian Optimal Experimental Design
authors: Adam Foster; Martin Jankowiak; Elias Bingham; Paul Horsfall; Yee Whye Teh; Thomas Rainforth; Noah Goodman
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (NeurIPS 2019)
subtopics: BOED; EIG estimation; variational inference
summary: Introduces several classes of fast estimators of the expected information gain (EIG) of an experiment, built on amortised variational inference, and shows theoretically and empirically that they are faster and more accurate than previous approaches, including in end-to-end adaptive experiments.
relation_to_specdx: Provides principled EIG estimators that could replace SpecDx's realised-information-gain reward; SpecDx's design space is discrete and small, so exact or nested-MC EIG under the EM posterior is feasible, which makes VBOED mainly a positioning reference.
baseline_notes: Alternative to Thompson-EIG: at each round estimate the EIG of each scenario cell under the current cell-model posterior (draw A_c, alpha, beta from a Laplace/bootstrap posterior; simulate committee readings; average entropy reduction of the defect label) and pick the argmax. EIG estimators are available in Pyro's pyro.contrib.oed module (eig.py; Apache-2.0, offline); for SpecDx's small discrete design space plain nested Monte Carlo suffices. Compare with A4 (random) and Thompson-EIG at an equal LLM-run budget.

title: A Tutorial on Thompson Sampling
authors: Daniel J. Russo; Benjamin Van Roy; Abbas Kazerouni; Ian Osband; Zheng Wen
venue: Foundations and Trends® in Machine Learning
subtopics: Thompson sampling; bandits; tutorial; active learning
summary: Tutorial on Thompson sampling for online decision problems that balance exploitation and information gathering, covering Bernoulli bandits, shortest paths, recommendation, active learning with neural networks and RL, and discussing when Thompson sampling works and when alternatives are needed.
relation_to_specdx: Standard reference for posterior sampling over correlated arms; SpecDx's cells are arms whose outcomes inform beliefs about other cells (shared clause/defect hypotheses), a case the tutorial discusses. SpecDx replaces the regret objective with information gain on defect diagnosis.

title: Adaptive generation of challenging scenarios for testing and evaluation of autonomous vehicles
authors: Galen E. Mullins; Paul G. Stankiewicz; R. Chad Hawthorne; Satyandra K. Gupta
venue: Journal of Systems and Software
subtopics: adaptive sampling; performance boundaries; scenario generation; autonomous vehicles
summary: Generates test scenarios for black-box autonomous systems by adaptive, simulation-based sampling that concentrates on the boundaries between performance modes, then clusters scenarios by mode and ranks boundary scenarios by how well they diagnose behaviour changes (summary from the publisher/APL description of the abstract).
relation_to_specdx: Closest SE analogue of SpecDx's boundary-oriented active scenario synthesis: adaptive sampling at mode boundaries with few expensive runs. SpecDx's boundaries come symbolically from clause literals and its 'modes' are reading patterns of an interpreter population.

title: Learning to Optimize via Information-Directed Sampling
authors: Daniel Russo; Benjamin Van Roy
venue: Operations Research
subtopics: information-directed sampling; bandits; information gain
summary: Introduces information-directed sampling (IDS), which samples actions to minimise the ratio of squared expected one-step regret to the mutual information between the optimal action and the next observation, with an entropy-scaled regret bound and gains over Thompson sampling and UCB in structured problems. Conference version at NeurIPS 2014.
relation_to_specdx: IDS is the principled alternative to SpecDx's 'Thompson sampling rewarded by realised information gain'; SpecDx has no regret term (pure exploration for diagnosis), so its objective sits closer to the information-gain denominator of IDS. Worth citing to justify or contrast the heuristic.

title: Active sequential hypothesis testing
authors: Mohammad Naghshvar; Tara Javidi
venue: The Annals of Statistics
subtopics: active hypothesis testing; information acquisition; sequential design
summary: Studies a decision maker who adaptively selects the most informative sensing action to identify a hypothesis quickly, penalising wrong declarations; derives dynamic-programming lower bounds on optimal cost and upper bounds for two heuristic action-selection policies that are asymptotically optimal.
relation_to_specdx: Theory for exactly SpecDx's problem shape: choose actions (scenarios) to identify which hypothesis (contradiction, hidden requirement, ambiguity, weak check, agent error) holds. Could supply optimality language for Thompson-EIG; SpecDx's observation model is the learned anchored cell model.

title: Optimistic Knowledge Gradient Policy for Optimal Budget Allocation in Crowdsourcing
authors: Xi Chen; Qihang Lin; Dengyong Zhou
venue: Proceedings of the 30th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 28(3)
subtopics: budget allocation; crowdsourcing; knowledge gradient; Bayesian MDP
summary: Formulates allocating a fixed labeling budget across instance-worker pairs as a Bayesian MDP and proposes the optimistic knowledge gradient policy, a tractable consistent approximation to the DP optimum, extended to heterogeneous workers and contextual tasks with differing ambiguity. A journal version appeared later (Chen, Lin, Zhou, 'Statistical decision making for optimal budget allocation in crowd labeling').
relation_to_specdx: Nearest prior art for SpecDx's allocation of LLM runs to cells under item difficulty and rater reliability: both allocate noisy ratings where posterior uncertainty is largest. SpecDx's raters are LLM interpreters with family effects, the specification itself is an anchor rater, and the truth is set-valued.
baseline_notes: Adapt: each scenario cell = instance with Beta/Dirichlet posterior on its deviation pattern; each LLM-family run = one label; opt-KG picks the cell whose optimistic one-step improvement in expected accuracy of the defect/no-defect decision is largest. Inputs: the reading matrix so far. No official code found; the policy is short (closed-form Beta updates) and easy to re-implement offline.

title: Bayesian Active Learning for Classification and Preference Learning
authors: Neil Houlsby; Ferenc Huszár; Zoubin Ghahramani; Máté Lengyel
venue: arXiv
subtopics: BALD; mutual information; active learning; Gaussian process classification
summary: Proposes Bayesian Active Learning by Disagreement (BALD): express information gain about model parameters in terms of predictive entropies (entropy of the marginal prediction minus expected conditional entropy), applied to Gaussian process classification and preference learning.
relation_to_specdx: BALD's 'disagreement' form of mutual information matches SpecDx's committee setting: a scenario is informative when interpreters disagree yet each is confident. SpecDx targets information about specification defects (A_c, anchors), not model parameters. Seminal 2011 preprint, kept despite the recency rule because the caller named it and it is the canonical BALD source.
baseline_notes: BALD acquisition over scenario cells: treat the posterior over (A_c, defect type) as the 'parameter' and the next committee reading as the label; score = H[E_theta p(reading|cell)] - E_theta H[p(reading|cell, theta)] using posterior samples from the fitted cell model; pick the top cell. Code: BALD is a few lines given posterior samples; BatchBALD reference implementation (BlackHC/BatchBALD, GPL-3.0) for batch selection.

title: Bayesian Experimental Design: A Review
authors: Kathryn Chaloner; Isabella Verdinelli
venue: Statistical Science
subtopics: Bayesian experimental design; review; expected utility
summary: Reviews Bayesian experimental design under a single decision-theoretic framework that covers linear and nonlinear design problems, casts the Bayesian design criteria as choices of utility function, and justifies choosing an optimality criterion on decision-theoretic grounds.
relation_to_specdx: Foundation for treating scenario choice as an experiment whose utility is expected information about the latent entailment sets and defect labels. SpecDx applies this sequentially and with a bandit approximation instead of solving the design problem exactly.

title: Query by committee
authors: H. S. Seung; M. Opper; H. Sompolinsky
venue: Proceedings of the fifth annual workshop on Computational learning theory
subtopics: query by committee; disagreement; information gain; active learning
summary: Proposes query by committee: a committee of learners trained on the same data picks the next query by maximal disagreement; on toy models this yields asymptotically finite information gain per query and exponentially decreasing generalisation error, unlike random queries.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's committee of LLM interpreters and disagreement-driven scenario choice descend from QBC. The twist: SpecDx treats consensus deviation from the specification (not disagreement alone) as defect evidence, and disagreement among families as evidence of ambiguity.
baseline_notes: Vote-entropy / disagreement QBC selection: run the cheap pilot committee (one model per family) on candidate scenario cells and pick the cell with the highest reading entropy (equivalent to B4's statistic used as an acquisition rule). Inputs: pilot reading matrix. No code needed (a few lines).

title: A Domain Strategy for Computer Program Testing
authors: L.J. White; E.I. Cohen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: domain testing; boundary values; predicate errors
summary: Domain testing: program predicates partition the input space into path domains, and test points placed on and just off each domain boundary detect domain errors, i.e., a shifted boundary or a changed relational operator, with conditions under which the strategy is reliable.
relation_to_specdx: The theoretical root of SpecDx's boundary values from clause literals: an on/off pair around a clause threshold separates a mis-keyed check (shifted constant, > vs >=) from the NL requirement. SpecDx applies it to specification clauses and judges the boundary by an interpreter population rather than a known-correct program.

title: On the Likelihood that One Unknown Probability Exceeds Another in View of the Evidence of Two Samples
authors: William R. Thompson
venue: Biometrika
subtopics: Thompson sampling; bandits; foundation
summary: The original paper behind Thompson sampling: it asks how likely it is that one unknown success probability exceeds another given two samples, and proposes allocating trials according to that posterior probability (as later summarised by Agrawal & Goyal and the Russo et al. tutorial).
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's scenario-cell selector is a Thompson sampler; this is the citation for the rule. SpecDx differs in that the reward is realised information gain about defect hypotheses, not a success probability.

title: Survey of Computerized Adaptive Testing: A Machine Learning Perspective
authors: Yan Zhuang; Qi Liu; Haoyang Bi; Zhenya Huang; Weizhe Huang; Jiatong Li; Junhao Yu; Zirui Liu; Zirui Hu; Yuting Hong; Zachary A. Pardos; Haiping Ma; Mengxiao Zhu; Shijin Wang; Enhong Chen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
subtopics: computerized adaptive testing; survey; question selection; AI model evaluation
summary: Machine-learning-focused survey of computerised adaptive testing covering measurement models, question-selection algorithms, item-bank construction and test control, including CAT for evaluating AI models.
relation_to_specdx: Survey to cite for selection rules (Fisher, KL, MI, learned policies) that SpecDx's Thompson-EIG competes with; SpecDx's 'bank' is synthesised from the specification rather than pre-calibrated.

title: Active Evaluation Acquisition for Efficient LLM Benchmarking
authors: Yang Li; Jie Ma; Miguel Ballesteros; Yassine Benajiba; Graham Horwood
venue: arXiv
subtopics: efficient evaluation; subset selection; RL acquisition policy; LLM benchmarking
summary: Selects a subset of prompts from each benchmark with a learned acquisition policy that models dependencies between test examples, so the outcomes of unselected examples can be predicted from the selected ones; an RL-based policy reduces the number of evaluation prompts while keeping performance estimates accurate.
relation_to_specdx: Active acquisition of evaluation outcomes with a predictive model of unrun items, parallel to SpecDx's cell model predicting unrun scenario cells; SpecDx's acquisition targets defect diagnosis.

title: Active Statistical Inference
authors: Tijana Zrnic; Emmanuel Candes
venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 235
subtopics: active inference; label budget; valid confidence intervals
summary: Active inference uses a black-box ML model to decide which points to label under a budget (label where the model is uncertain, rely on predictions where confident) and still produces valid confidence intervals and tests, with fewer labels than non-adaptive baselines.
relation_to_specdx: Template for making SpecDx's adaptively collected evidence support valid statistical statements (e.g., defect-rate intervals) while spending runs where the cell model is uncertain.

title: Automated black-box boundary value detection
authors: Felix Dobslaw; Robert Feldt; Francisco Gomes de Oliveira Neto
venue: PeerJ Computer Science
subtopics: boundary value detection; black-box testing; search
summary: Proposes an automated black-box boundary value detection method that searches for pairs of nearby inputs with highly different outputs (using a program-derivative measure), supporting systematic boundary value analysis even without a specification or model.
relation_to_specdx: Black-box alternative for SpecDx's boundary values: it would find where executor behaviour changes without reading clause literals. SpecDx compares the executors' boundary with the boundary the clause declares, which this method cannot do alone.

title: Adaptive Testing and Debugging of NLP Models
authors: Marco Tulio Ribeiro; Scott Lundberg
venue: Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
subtopics: adaptive testing; LLM-generated tests; NLP model debugging; human in the loop
summary: AdaTest pairs a large language model with human feedback to write unit tests that reveal bugs in a target NLP model, adapting test generation to what has been found and iterating a test-fix-retest loop; users are 5-10x more effective at finding bugs.
relation_to_specdx: Adaptive LLM-driven test generation; SpecDx is fully automatic (no human in the loop) and its tests are scenarios that probe the specification through a population of executors.

title: DeepHyperion: exploring the feature space of deep learning-based systems through illumination search
authors: Tahereh Zohdinasab; Vincenzo Riccio; Alessio Gambi; Paolo Tonella
venue: Proceedings of the 30th ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
subtopics: illumination search; MAP-Elites; feature map; DL system testing
summary: Uses illumination search (MAP-Elites) to find misbehaving and near-misbehaving test inputs spread across the cells of a map over interpretable features, giving developers a feature map of where a DL system fails, with a method to define the feature dimensions.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's 'scenario cells' are a grid over specification features much like a DeepHyperion feature map; SpecDx fills it by Thompson sampling with an information-gain reward instead of a quality-diversity archive with a failure-closeness fitness.

title: Operation is the Hardest Teacher: Estimating DNN Accuracy Looking for Mispredictions
authors: Antonio Guerriero; Roberto Pietrantuono; Stefano Russo
venue: 2021 IEEE/ACM 43rd International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
subtopics: operational testing; adaptive sampling; accuracy estimation; misprediction finding
summary: DeepEST selects operational test inputs with an adaptive sampling scheme that both yields an unbiased accuracy estimate and deliberately includes many mispredicting examples, so testing estimates accuracy and exposes failures at once.
relation_to_specdx: Shares SpecDx's dual aim (estimate and find defects) under a labeling budget; SpecDx's target failures are specification defects and its 'labels' are committee executions.

title: Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
authors: Steven R. Howard; Aaditya Ramdas; Jon McAuliffe; Jasjeet Sekhon
venue: The Annals of Statistics
subtopics: confidence sequences; anytime-valid inference; SPRT
summary: Develops time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences whose widths shrink to zero, connecting Cramer-Chernoff bounds, the law of the iterated logarithm and the SPRT, including empirical-Bernstein bounds.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's Hoeffding finite-sample bounds are fixed-sample; because scenarios are chosen adaptively and stopping is data-dependent, time-uniform confidence sequences are the correct tool for valid stopping guarantees.

title: Boosting fuzzer efficiency: an information theoretic perspective
authors: Marcel Böhme; Valentin J. M. Manès; Sang Kil Cha
venue: Proceedings of the 28th ACM Joint Meeting on European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering
subtopics: information-theoretic scheduling; fuzzing; entropy; power schedule
summary: Treats fuzzing as a learning process in which each execution reveals some information about the program's behaviours; within a probabilistic model of fuzzing, Shannon entropy over observed behaviours measures how much each input teaches and the rate at which the fuzzer discovers new behaviours, so efficient fuzzers maximise information (the basis of the authors' entropy-based seed schedule, Entropic).
relation_to_specdx: SE precedent for rewarding test selection by realised information gain, as SpecDx's Thompson sampler does over scenario cells; Entropic's information is about program behaviours, SpecDx's is about specification-defect hypotheses.

title: Boundary Value Exploration for Software Analysis
authors: Felix Dobslaw; Francisco Gomes de Oliveira Neto; Robert Feldt
venue: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation Workshops (ICSTW)
subtopics: boundary value analysis; boundary value exploration; program derivative
summary: Clarifies boundary value analysis and testing, which are poorly defined and hard to automate because subdomains must be identified from a specification, and introduces Boundary Value Exploration: techniques that search for input pairs whose outputs differ sharply, as a basis for automation.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx sidesteps the subdomain-identification problem BVE raises because executable clauses expose their literals; BVE-style search is the black-box fallback when T states a threshold that C does not.

title: Automatically testing self-driving cars with search-based procedural content generation
authors: Alessio Gambi; Marc Mueller; Gordon Fraser
venue: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
subtopics: search-based testing; procedural content generation; self-driving cars; scenario generation
summary: AsFault combines procedural content generation with search-based testing to create virtual road networks that make lane-keeping software of self-driving cars fail in simulation.
relation_to_specdx: Automatic generation of structured scenarios for a black-box system under test; SpecDx's scenarios are business states and requests constructed from clause literals, evaluated by an LLM population.

title: BatchBALD: Efficient and Diverse Batch Acquisition for Deep Bayesian Active Learning
authors: Andreas Kirsch; Joost van Amersfoort; Yarin Gal
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (NeurIPS 2019)
subtopics: BALD; batch acquisition; mutual information
summary: Develops BatchBALD, a greedy (1-1/e)-approximate estimate of the joint mutual information between a batch of points and model parameters, which avoids the redundant batches that top-k BALD selects.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx runs scenarios in batches on a shared GPU host; top-k Thompson draws can pick redundant cells that share one clause. BatchBALD gives a principled joint batch criterion.

title: Boosting operational DNN testing efficiency through conditioning
authors: Zenan Li; Xiaoxing Ma; Chang Xu; Chun Cao; Jingwei Xu; Jian Lü
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 27th ACM Joint Meeting on European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering
subtopics: operational testing; accuracy estimation; label budget; variance reduction
summary: Views operational testing as reliability estimation by statistical sampling, reinterprets structural coverage as conditioning for variance reduction, and conditions on the distribution of last-hidden-layer neuron outputs (sampled via cross-entropy minimisation), needing about half the labels of simple random sampling for the same precision.
relation_to_specdx: SE counterpart of active testing: choosing which field inputs to label to estimate accuracy. SpecDx selects scenarios to diagnose the specification, but variance-reduction sampling matters when it reports defect prevalence.

title: Testing autonomous cars for feature interaction failures using many-objective search
authors: Raja Ben Abdessalem; Annibale Panichella; Shiva Nejati; Lionel C. Briand; Thomas Stifter
venue: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM/IEEE International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: search-based testing; critical scenario generation; many-objective search; feature interaction
summary: Casts detection of feature-interaction failures in autonomous cars as search-based test generation, defining hybrid test objectives that combine coverage heuristics with interaction-failure distances and a many-objective algorithm (FITEST) that generates simulation scenarios violating system requirements.
relation_to_specdx: Requirement-violation-guided scenario search; SpecDx also searches a scenario space for requirement-relevant behaviour, but its fitness is information about specification defects across a population of executors rather than failure distance of one system.

title: Testing vision-based control systems using learnable evolutionary algorithms
authors: Raja Ben Abdessalem; Shiva Nejati; Lionel C. Briand; Thomas Stifter
venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Software Engineering
subtopics: search-based testing; learnable evolutionary algorithms; critical scenario; surrogate classifier
summary: Tests vision-based control systems with learnable evolutionary algorithms: multi-objective search combined with decision-tree classifiers that learn which regions of the scenario space are critical, steering generation towards failure-inducing scenarios and characterising those regions.
relation_to_specdx: Model-guided scenario generation that learns where critical regions are, akin to SpecDx using its cell model to steer Thompson sampling; SpecDx's regions of interest are clause boundaries and disagreement, not failures of one system.

title: DeepXplore: Automated Whitebox Testing of Deep Learning Systems
authors: Kexin Pei; Yinzhi Cao; Junfeng Yang; Suman Jana
venue: Proceedings of the 26th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles
subtopics: differential testing; multiple oracles; test generation; neuron coverage
summary: DeepXplore is a whitebox framework that introduces neuron coverage and uses several DL systems with similar functionality as cross-referencing oracles, generating inputs by gradient-based joint optimisation of differential behaviour and coverage; it finds thousands of erroneous corner cases.
relation_to_specdx: Uses a population of similar models as each other's oracle and generates inputs that maximise their disagreement, close to SpecDx's committee idea. SpecDx adds the specification as an anchored rater and attributes consensus deviations to the specification rather than to the models.

title: Testing Cyber-Physical Systems through Bayesian Optimization
authors: Jyotirmoy Deshmukh; Marko Horvat; Xiaoqing Jin; Rupak Majumdar; Vinayak S. Prabhu
venue: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems
subtopics: falsification; Bayesian optimization; cyber-physical systems
summary: Treats CPS testing as black-box optimisation of a cost over output traces (e.g., robustness of a temporal-logic requirement) and provides a tool that applies Bayesian optimisation, with automated dimensionality reduction, to find falsifying inputs with few simulations.
relation_to_specdx: Surrogate-guided, sample-efficient search for requirement violations; SpecDx uses a Bayesian cell model and Thompson sampling instead of a GP over continuous inputs, and its objective is information about the specification, not falsification of the system.

title: Active Learning
authors: Burr Settles
venue: Synthesis Lectures on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
subtopics: active learning; survey; query by committee; uncertainty sampling
summary: Book-length treatment of active learning, in which the learner chooses which unlabeled instances an oracle should label; it is the later, extended form of the author's 2009 technical-report survey (the abstract was not available to us; summary from the record metadata).
relation_to_specdx: Standard survey to cite for query-selection vocabulary (uncertainty sampling, query-by-committee). SpecDx queries a committee of LLM executors on synthesised scenarios, and no single oracle is assumed correct.

title: Analysis of Thompson Sampling for the Multi-armed Bandit Problem
authors: Shipra Agrawal; Navin Goyal
venue: Proceedings of the 25th Annual Conference on Learning Theory (COLT), PMLR 23
subtopics: Thompson sampling; regret analysis; bandits
summary: First proof that Thompson sampling achieves logarithmic expected regret for the stochastic multi-armed bandit problem, giving regret bounds for two-armed and N-armed bandits.
relation_to_specdx: Theoretical backing for using Thompson sampling as SpecDx's scenario-cell selector; SpecDx's reward (realised information gain) is non-stationary and depends on the posterior, so these guarantees do not transfer directly.

title: A survey of combinatorial testing
authors: Changhai Nie; Hareton Leung
venue: ACM Computing Surveys
subtopics: combinatorial testing; covering arrays; survey
summary: Surveys two decades of combinatorial testing, which detects failures triggered by parameter interactions using covering-array test suites, classifying work into modelling, generation, constraints, failure diagnosis, prioritisation, metrics and applications.
relation_to_specdx: Covering arrays over scenario parameters are a non-adaptive alternative to SpecDx's Thompson-sampled cells; CT's failure-diagnosis line (locating failure-inducing combinations) is also related to localising the clause behind a deviation.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Thompson Sampling
authors: Olivier Chapelle; Lihong Li
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 24 (NIPS 2011)
subtopics: Thompson sampling; empirical evaluation; bandits
summary: Shows on simulated and real (display advertising, news recommendation) data that Thompson sampling is highly competitive with standard bandit heuristics and argues it should be a standard baseline because it is easy to implement.
relation_to_specdx: Empirical justification for choosing Thompson sampling as SpecDx's default selector; SpecDx's ablation A4 (random selection) and an IDS/UCB variant would mirror this kind of comparison.

title: A Global Information Approach to Computerized Adaptive Testing
authors: Hua-Hua Chang; Zhiliang Ying
venue: Applied Psychological Measurement
subtopics: computerized adaptive testing; item selection; KL information
summary: Argues that maximum-Fisher-information item selection is inefficient early in a CAT, when the ability estimate is poor, and proposes item selection based on average global (Kullback-Leibler) information, supported by simulations.
relation_to_specdx: Directly informs SpecDx's early rounds: with few runs the cell-model posterior is wide, so a global/expected-information criterion (or Thompson's posterior sampling) is preferable to plug-in local information.

title: Sequential Design of Experiments
authors: Herman Chernoff
venue: The Annals of Mathematical Statistics
subtopics: sequential design; active hypothesis testing; experiment selection
summary: Foundational paper on the sequential design of experiments, in which the experimenter adaptively chooses which experiment to perform next as well as when to stop and which hypothesis to accept.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's loop (choose scenario, observe committee, update, stop) is a Chernoff-style sequential design for identifying the defect hypothesis per cell.

title: On a Measure of the Information Provided by an Experiment
authors: D. V. Lindley
venue: The Annals of Mathematical Statistics
subtopics: information gain; experimental design; foundation
summary: Introduces a Shannon-based measure of the information an experiment provides relative to a prior over the parameter, uses it to compare experiments, and applies it to design problems whose aim is to gain knowledge rather than to reach decisions.
relation_to_specdx: Defines the information-gain quantity that SpecDx uses as the reward for a scenario; SpecDx computes a realised (post-hoc) version from the EM posterior.

title: Sequential Tests of Statistical Hypotheses
authors: A. Wald
venue: The Annals of Mathematical Statistics
subtopics: SPRT; sequential testing; early stopping
summary: Introduces the sequential probability ratio test, which keeps sampling until the likelihood ratio crosses one of two thresholds, reaching given error rates with fewer expected observations than a fixed-sample test.
relation_to_specdx: The principle behind SpecDx's stop/escalate decision per cell (stop after the pilot when evidence is decisive, otherwise run the full committee). SpecDx uses a posterior threshold from the cell model rather than a two-hypothesis likelihood ratio.

title: Automated Boundary Identification for Machine Learning Classifiers
authors: Felix Dobslaw; Robert Feldt
venue: Proceedings of the 17th ACM/IEEE International Workshop on Search-Based and Fuzz Testing
subtopics: boundary identification; ML classifiers; search-based testing
summary: Extends automated boundary-value identification (pairs of nearby inputs with highly differing outputs) from traditional software to machine-learning classifiers, so developers can judge whether a model's boundaries are where they should be.
relation_to_specdx: Boundary candidates for learned components; SpecDx's executors are LLM agents whose decision boundary is compared with the specification's declared one.

title: Efficient Benchmarking (of Language Models)
authors: Yotam Perlitz; Elron Bandel; Ariel Gera; Ofir Arviv; Liat Ein-Dor; Eyal Shnarch; Noam Slonim; Michal Shmueli-Scheuer; Leshem Choshen
venue: Proceedings of NAACL-HLT 2024 (Volume 1: Long Papers)
subtopics: efficient evaluation; benchmark reliability; HELM
summary: Defines efficient benchmarking (cutting LM evaluation cost without losing reliability), introduces the Decision Impact on Reliability (DIoR) measure, and shows on HELM that design choices such as removing low-ranked models can flip leaders, while a proposed algorithm cuts computation by 100x or more.
relation_to_specdx: Budget-aware evaluation context; SpecDx's run budget on the 48 GB host motivates the same concern but the object being assessed is the specification.

title: A Survey on Automated Driving System Testing: Landscapes and Trends
authors: Shuncheng Tang; Zhenya Zhang; Yi Zhang; Jixiang Zhou; Yan Guo; Shuang Liu; Shengjian Guo; Yan-Fu Li; Lei Ma; Yinxing Xue; Yang Liu
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
subtopics: survey; scenario-based testing; automated driving systems
summary: Surveys automated driving system testing at both the module level (sensing, perception, planning, control) and the system level, covering empirical studies of field issues, inter-module problems and the simulator-to-reality gap, and outlines trends and open problems.
relation_to_specdx: Survey pointer for the search-based scenario-generation literature that SpecDx's active synthesis borrows from.

title: Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference
authors: Aaditya Ramdas; Peter Grünwald; Vladimir Vovk; Glenn Shafer
venue: Statistical Science
subtopics: anytime-valid inference; e-processes; optional stopping
summary: Surveys safe anytime-valid inference: e-processes and confidence sequences built on test martingales that remain valid under continuous monitoring and optional stopping, with game-theoretic foundations.
relation_to_specdx: Reference for making SpecDx's escalation and stopping decisions valid under adaptive scenario choice.

title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
authors: Ethan Perez; Saffron Huang; Francis Song; Trevor Cai; Roman Ring; John Aslanides; Amelia Glaese; Nat McAleese; Geoffrey Irving
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
subtopics: automatic test generation; red teaming; LM-generated tests
summary: Uses one LM to generate test cases that elicit harmful behaviour from a target LM, judged by a classifier, comparing zero-shot, few-shot, supervised and RL generation for diversity and difficulty.
relation_to_specdx: Automatic LM-based test generation with an automatic judge; SpecDx's generator is grounded in clause literals and its judge is the executable check C itself, whose correctness is under test.

title: Practical Accuracy Estimation for Efficient Deep Neural Network Testing
authors: Junjie Chen; Zhuo Wu; Zan Wang; Hanmo You; Lingming Zhang; Ming Yan
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
subtopics: test selection; accuracy estimation; clustering; DNN testing
summary: PACE clusters test inputs by the functionality they exercise, then selects prototypes from each group with the MMD-critic algorithm (proportional to group size), so that labeling a small selected set precisely estimates DNN accuracy on the whole test set.
relation_to_specdx: Representative-subset selection for evaluation; a non-adaptive alternative to SpecDx's Thompson-EIG for choosing which scenario cells to execute.

title: Deep Bayesian Active Learning with Image Data
authors: Yarin Gal; Riashat Islam; Zoubin Ghahramani
venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 70
subtopics: BALD; deep active learning; Bayesian deep learning
summary: Combines Bayesian deep learning (MC-dropout Bayesian CNNs) with information-theoretic acquisition functions such as BALD and variation ratios, making active learning practical for high-dimensional image data.
relation_to_specdx: Shows BALD-style acquisition with approximate posteriors; SpecDx's committee of distinct LLM families plays the role of posterior samples, but the queried object is a business scenario, not an image.

title: A Knowledge-Gradient Policy for Sequential Information Collection
authors: Peter I. Frazier; Warren B. Powell; Savas Dayanik
venue: SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization
subtopics: knowledge gradient; ranking and selection; value of information
summary: Analyses the knowledge-gradient policy for Bayesian ranking and selection, which myopically maximises the expected increment in value of information, proving optimality for one-step and infinite horizons and bounding its suboptimality otherwise.
relation_to_specdx: Knowledge gradient is the value-of-information alternative to Thompson-EIG for choosing SpecDx's next scenario; it underlies the optimistic-KG crowdsourcing policy.

title: Software fault interactions and implications for software testing
authors: D.R. Kuhn; D.R. Wallace; A.M. Gallo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: combinatorial testing; interaction faults; empirical study
summary: Empirical study across domains showing that software failures are triggered by combinations of few conditions, so testing all n-way parameter combinations for small n can be effectively exhaustive.
relation_to_specdx: Supports constructing SpecDx's scenario space from small combinations of clause literals (pairwise coverage of conditions) rather than full cross-products.

title: QuickCheck: a lightweight tool for random testing of Haskell programs
authors: Koen Claessen; John Hughes
venue: Proceedings of the fifth ACM SIGPLAN international conference on Functional programming
subtopics: property-based testing; random testing; generators
summary: QuickCheck lets Haskell programmers state program properties as functions and test them automatically on random inputs drawn from customisable generators.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's executable clauses play the role of properties and the scenario synthesiser the role of generators; SpecDx adds an LLM population as executor and asks whether the property itself is wrong.

title: The AETG system: an approach to testing based on combinatorial design
authors: D.M. Cohen; S.R. Dalal; M.L. Fredman; G.C. Patton
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
subtopics: combinatorial testing; pairwise testing; test generation
summary: Presents AETG, which uses combinatorial designs to generate test sets covering all valid pairwise or n-way combinations of the parameters that define test scenarios, with test-set size growing logarithmically in the number of parameters.
relation_to_specdx: Classic non-adaptive scenario-space covering; a natural 'pairwise' alternative to random scenario selection (A4) for SpecDx's pilot round.

title: APPLICATION OF COMPUTERIZED ADAPTIVE TESTING TO EDUCATIONAL PROBLEMS
authors: DAVID J. WEISS; G. GAGE KINGSBURY
venue: Journal of Educational Measurement
subtopics: computerized adaptive testing; mastery testing; IRT
summary: Describes three IRT-based CAT applications in education: adaptive mastery testing, adaptive grading, and adaptive self-referenced testing for measuring change, with evidence that adaptive mastery testing reaches decisions with fewer items.
relation_to_specdx: Adaptive mastery testing (stop as soon as a classification is confident) is the psychometric twin of SpecDx's per-cell escalation-and-stop rule.

title: A Multiple Testing Procedure for Clinical Trials
authors: Peter C. O'Brien; Thomas R. Fleming
venue: Biometrics
subtopics: group sequential design; early stopping; multiple testing
summary: Proposes a multiple-testing procedure for comparing two treatments with repeated chi-square tests at a fixed maximum number of looks, keeping overall size and power close to a single fixed-sample test while allowing early termination (the O'Brien-Fleming boundary).
relation_to_specdx: Alternative stopping boundary for SpecDx's stage-wise escalation; conservative early boundaries would make a pilot-only defect decision rare.

title: Group sequential methods in the design and analysis of clinical trials
authors: S. J. POCOCK
venue: Biometrika
subtopics: group sequential design; interim analysis; early stopping
summary: Proposes group sequential designs that split entry into equal-sized groups and decide after each group whether to stop, using repeated significance tests, with exact results for normal responses and guidance on the number and size of groups.
relation_to_specdx: SpecDx's pilot (one model per family) then full committee is a two-stage group-sequential design; Pocock-style boundaries are a way to control the false-escalation rate.

title: Agentic Business Process Management: A research manifesto
authors: Diego Calvanese; Angelo Casciani; Giuseppe De Giacomo; Marlon Dumas; Fabiana Fournier; Timotheus Kampik; Emanuele La Malfa; Lior Limonad; Andrea Marrella; Andreas Metzger; Marco Montali; Daniel Amyot; Peter Fettke; Artem Polyvyanyy; Stefanie Rinderle-Ma; Sebastian Sardiña; Niek Tax; Barbara Weber
venue: Information Systems
subtopics: agentic BPM; manifesto; framed autonomy
summary: A research manifesto for Agentic Business Process Management (APM), in which software and human agents execute processes within explicit process frames; it introduces core abstractions and architecture and four capabilities APM agents need: framed autonomy, explainability, conversational actionability and self-modification.
relation_to_specdx: Positions LLM agents as executors of business process specifications, SpecDx's setting; the manifesto assumes the process frame is the reference for alignment, while SpecDx shows how the frame itself can be diagnosed from agents' deviations.

title: Ambiguity Detection and Elimination in Automated Executable Process Modeling
authors: Ion Matei; Praveen Kumar Menaka Sekar; Maksym Zhenirovskyy; Hon Yung Wong; Sayuri Kohmura; Shinji Hotta; Akihiro Inomata
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: ambiguity detection; repeated LLM generation; model-based diagnosis; text repair
specdx_components: ddmin; defect taxonomy; set-valued truth; baseline B4
summary: Detects when a natural-language process specification fails to support a stable executable interpretation: BPMN models are generated and simulated repeatedly, behavioural inconsistency is detected from the empirical KPI distribution, localised to gateway logic by model-based diagnosis, mapped back to verbatim narrative segments, and the text is repaired; demonstrated on health-guidance policies.
relation_to_specdx: The closest threat in this theme: it uses repeated LLM interpretations without ground truth to detect and localise ambiguity in T, as SpecDx's components 1 and 5 do. It differs by covering only ambiguity (not contradiction, hidden requirement or weak check), using one generator rather than a multi-family population with an error model, having no executable checks C or anchors, and giving no refutation witnesses.
baseline_notes: Inputs: a NL process specification (T); it repeatedly generates executable BPMN with an LLM, simulates it, and uses the KPI distribution to detect unstable interpretations, then localises divergence to gateways and maps it to verbatim text segments. Adaptation: treat TonomyX requirement documents or τ²-bench policy sections as the narrative, use SpecDx's agent runs (or regenerated executable models) in place of BPMN simulations, and use KPI/outcome dispersion per cell as the ambiguity signal; compare its text localisation with SpecDx's ddmin. Code status: not stated in the abstract.

title: MANTRA: Synthesizing SMT-Validated Compliance Benchmarks for Tool-Using LLM Agents
authors: Ashwani Anand; Ivi Chatzi; Ritam Raha; Anne-Kathrin Schmuck
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: compliance benchmark synthesis; SMT validation; procedural manuals
specdx_components: MUS/MCS; refutation; active synthesis; defect taxonomy
summary: MANTRA synthesises machine-checkable compliance benchmarks from natural-language procedural manuals and tool schemas: it separately generates a symbolic world model and trace-level compliance checks, validates their mutual consistency with SMT solving, repairs inconsistencies in a loop, and derives tasks of tunable complexity.
relation_to_specdx: Threatens part of SpecDx's novelty: it automatically detects inconsistencies between NL-derived checks and a model of the manual using a solver. It differs in that it validates checks it generated itself, uses no population of executors, and gives no typed diagnosis of ambiguity or weak checks in a pre-existing specification.

title: Solver-Aided Verification of Policy Compliance in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
authors: Cailin Winston; Claris Winston; René Just
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: SMT policy checking; tau-bench; NL policy formalisation
summary: Translates natural-language tool-use policies into SMT-LIB constraints with an LLM-assisted, human-guided process; at runtime each planned tool call is checked with Z3 as a precondition and blocked if it violates the policy; evaluated on τ-bench with fewer violations at unchanged task accuracy.
relation_to_specdx: Shares SpecDx's use of solvers over τ-bench policy clauses, but for enforcement on agents; it does not use the solver to test the policy/check pair for contradictions or looseness.
baseline_notes: Inputs: NL tool-use policy (τ-bench airline/retail policy text). It translates policies into SMT-LIB constraints over agent-observable state and tool arguments and checks planned tool calls with Z3. As a baseline for SpecDx's B5 (symbolic analysis without interpreters): conjoin the formalised policy constraints with the benchmark's checks C and query Z3 for unsatisfiability (contradiction) or for models that satisfy C but violate the policy (weak check). Code status: not found in the abstract; translation is LLM-assisted with human guidance, so a fully automatic run needs the LLM step only.

title: ST-WebAgentBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Safety and Trustworthiness in Web Agents
authors: Ido Levy; Ben Wiesel; Sami Marreed; Alon Oved; Avi Yaeli; Segev Shlomov
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026)
subtopics: agent benchmark; policy adherence; safety and trust
summary: ST-WebAgentBench pairs enterprise web tasks with explicit safety and trustworthiness policies scored on six dimensions, and introduces Completion-under-Policy, which credits only completions that respect all policies, plus a Risk Ratio of breaches.
relation_to_specdx: Policies are explicit clauses checked over agent behaviour, as in SpecDx's C; the benchmark measures agents against them, while SpecDx asks whether the policy clauses themselves are contradictory, hidden or weak.

title: IntellAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Conversational AI Systems
authors: Elad Levi; Ilan Kadar
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: policy-driven test generation; conversational agents; policy graph; policy-driven scenario generation; user simulation
summary: IntellAgent is an open-source multi-agent framework that builds a graph of policies (nodes weighted by complexity, edges by co-occurrence), samples multi-policy events and user goals from it, simulates user-agent dialogues and critiques the agent's policy adherence for fine-grained diagnostics.
relation_to_specdx: Shares SpecDx's policy-driven scenario generation and fine-grained per-policy diagnosis, but its goal is to diagnose the agent and it treats the policy as correct; SpecDx diagnoses the policy/check pair from a population of agents. | Closest prior work on synthesising business scenarios from policies for tau-bench-style agents. IntellAgent samples policy combinations to evaluate the agent and trusts the policies; SpecDx chooses scenarios adaptively (Thompson-EIG, clause boundaries) to diagnose defects in the policies and checks themselves.
baseline_notes: Inputs: the policy text T (τ²-bench airline/retail policy or TonomyX requirement documents) plus tool schemas and a database. IntellAgent builds a policy graph and samples multi-policy scenarios with expected behaviour; adapting it, we would (i) replace SpecDx's Thompson-sampling scenario synthesiser with IntellAgent's policy-graph sampler as an ablation of component 6, and (ii) use its critique agent's per-policy verdicts over our agent runs as a single-judge defect detector. Code: Apache-2.0, Python, LangGraph; it can run with local models through LangChain, so offline use is feasible. | Scenario-generator baseline: use IntellAgent's policy-graph sampling (complexity-weighted random walks over co-occurring policies) as the scenario source instead of SpecDx's Thompson-EIG cells, keeping SpecDx's diagnosis fixed; compare defects found per LLM run. Code: plurai-ai/intellagent (repository exists; stars/licence not checked because the GitHub API was rate-limited); uses LLM APIs but can be pointed at local Ollama models via its LangChain configuration (to confirm).

title: SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints
authors: Zekun Li; Shinda Huang; Jiangtian Wang; Nathan Zhang; Antonis Antoniades; Wenyue Hua; Kaijie Zhu; Sirui Zeng; Chi Wang; William Yang Wang; Xifeng Yan
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: agent benchmark; SOP following; rule-based verifiers; test generation
summary: SOPBench turns service-specific SOP code programs into directed graphs of executable functions across seven customer-service domains; agents must follow the natural-language SOP, the original code acts as a rule-based oracle verifier, and an automated generator produces 900+ verified test cases.
relation_to_specdx: Closest benchmark design to SpecDx's setting: NL SOP (T) paired with executable verifier code (C) and generated scenarios (Π). SOPBench assumes the code oracle matches the text; SpecDx tests that assumption and localises mismatches.

title: Towards Enforcing Company Policy Adherence in Agentic Workflows
authors: Naama Zwerdling; David Boaz; Ella Rabinovich; Guy Uziel; David Amid; Ateret Anaby Tavor
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
subtopics: policy-to-guard-code compilation; tau-bench airline; business policy adherence
summary: Compiles company policy documents offline into verifiable guard code attached to each tool, and runs the guards before each agent action at runtime, giving deterministic and transparent policy enforcement; demonstrated on the τ-bench airline domain.
relation_to_specdx: Works on exactly SpecDx's τ-bench airline subject and makes T executable as guards, but trusts the policy and the compilation; SpecDx's comparison of T, C and agent behaviour would expose where ToolGuard's guards and the benchmark checks disagree.
baseline_notes: Inputs: the policy document T and tool schemas (τ-bench airline policy is its own evaluation domain). Its buildtime stage compiles each policy into Python guard functions per tool. As a baseline: compile T into guards, then (a) compare guards against the benchmark's checks C to flag clauses that no guard justifies (hidden requirement) or guards that no clause enforces (weak check), and (b) run the guards on the agent population's traces. Code: open source at github.com/AgentToolkit/toolguard (Apache-2.0, Python, pushed 2026-08; referenced by Langflow's Policies component), runnable with any LangChain-compatible LLM, so offline use with local models is feasible.

title: Measuring Inconsistency in Declarative Process Specifications
authors: Carl Corea; John Grant; Matthias Thimm
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
subtopics: inconsistency measurement; LTLff; paraconsistent semantics
summary: Shows that classical inconsistency measures cannot assess inconsistency in LTL with temporal operators, proposes a paraconsistent semantics for LTL on fixed traces, and defines two inconsistency measures with desirable properties for declarative process specifications, with a complexity analysis.
relation_to_specdx: Quantifies how inconsistent a declarative specification is, with MUS-based measures among the baselines; SpecDx localises and types contradictions from behaviour and refutes candidates with witnesses, which these measures do not.
baseline_notes: Inputs: a set of LTL-on-fixed-traces formulas (declarative constraints). Adaptation: encode SpecDx's clause set C (temporal and state clauses for a scenario of bounded length) as LTLff, compute the paper's paraconsistent inconsistency measures to rank clause sets by degree of conflict and compare with SpecDx's contradiction scores. Code: per the authors' publication list, a follow-up ASP-based framework (Kuhlmann, Corea, Grant) implements satisfiability checking and two inconsistency measures; no repository was verified.

title: Checking process compliance against natural language specifications using behavioral spaces
authors: Han van der Aa; Henrik Leopold; Hajo A. Reijers
venue: Information Systems
subtopics: compliance checking; behavioural space; ambiguity
summary: Journal version of the behavioural-space approach: a behavioural space systematically captures all interpretations of an ambiguous textual process description, so that compliance checking against the text avoids committing to one possibly wrong reading; evaluated on 47 textual descriptions.
relation_to_specdx: Compliance against all readings of T parallels SpecDx's satisfaction-based defect definitions over set-valued truth; SpecDx adds executable clauses and automatic detection of which statements are ambiguous.

title: Conformance Checking: Relating Processes and Models
authors: Josep Carmona; Boudewijn van Dongen; Andreas Solti; Matthias Weidlich
subtopics: conformance checking; alignments; precision; textbook
summary: Book by Carmona, van Dongen, Solti and Weidlich that formalises the relation between modelled and recorded behaviour and surveys conformance-checking techniques (alignments, fitness, precision, generalisation) at an intuitive and formal level.
relation_to_specdx: Gives the vocabulary for SpecDx's analogy: a fitness failure shared by many traces at the same place can mean the model (specification) is wrong; precision failures correspond to SpecDx's weak checks.

title: Semantics, Analysis and Simplification of DMN Decision Tables
authors: Diego Calvanese; Marlon Dumas; Ülari Laurson; Fabrizio M. Maggi; Marco Montali; Irene Teinemaa
venue: Information Systems
subtopics: DMN; decision table analysis; simplification
summary: Journal version: a formal semantics of DMN decision tables, a general geometric approach to analyse and refactor them, efficient algorithms for detecting overlapping and missing rules, and a table simplification by rule merging, evaluated on real and synthetic tables.
relation_to_specdx: The strongest symbolic baseline for rule-shaped clauses: it finds conflicts and gaps in C by geometry alone. SpecDx differs by relating C to the NL text T through executor readings, and by typing hidden requirements and weak checks that are invisible inside C alone.
baseline_notes: Inputs: decision tables (input intervals/enumerations to outputs). Adaptation: encode the rule-like parts of C (e.g., τ²-bench airline refund/cancellation eligibility, or TonomyX approval thresholds and SQL policy functions) as DMN tables over the clause variables, then run overlap detection (candidate ambiguity/contradiction among clauses) and missing-rule detection (inputs no clause decides, candidate weak checks). It needs a manual or LLM-assisted encoding of C into tables and sees only C, not T or agent behaviour. Code: the paper reports an implementation; no maintained public repository was verified, so a re-implementation of the geometric overlap/gap sweep (straightforward for interval inputs) is the practical route.

title: Comparing textual descriptions to process models – The automatic detection of inconsistencies
authors: Han van der Aa; Henrik Leopold; Hajo A. Reijers
venue: Information Systems
subtopics: text-model inconsistency; NLP; process models; business process; BPM
summary: Automatically detects inconsistencies between a process model and its textual description by aligning sentences to model activities with NLP and flagging activities described in different orders and model activities missing from the text; evaluated on 53 real model-text pairs.
relation_to_specdx: Directly detects T-versus-C-style inconsistencies between two representations of a process, which is SpecDx's goal for T and C. It uses linguistic alignment of one model and one text, with no executors, no ambiguity type and no executable checks. | A business-specification analogue of the T-versus-C gap: text versus a formal artefact. SpecDx compares T and C through executions rather than by NLP alignment, and also types defects (Hidden requirement, Weak check).
baseline_notes: Inputs: a textual process description plus a process model; output: activities described in different orders and model activities missing from the text. Adaptation: render each TonomyX workflow (or τ²-bench policy procedure) as a model derived from C (the sequence of guarded actions and expected actions) and compare it with the sentences of T; flagged order conflicts map to contradictions/hidden requirements and missing activities to hidden requirements. Code: no public implementation found; it is a pre-LLM NLP pipeline, so a re-implementation (or an LLM-based reimplementation) would be needed.

title: Resolving inconsistencies and redundancies in declarative process models
authors: Claudio Di Ciccio; Fabrizio Maria Maggi; Marco Montali; Jan Mendling
venue: Information Systems
subtopics: Declare; inconsistency resolution; redundancy; automata product
summary: Discovered Declare models can contain mutually contradicting constraints that accept no trace; the paper resolves such inconsistencies and removes redundancies automatically using automata products (an automata-product monoid), keeping the most interesting constraints while guaranteeing a consistent model.
relation_to_specdx: Directly addresses contradiction in a declarative clause set, i.e., SpecDx's contradiction type, with automata rather than sampled correction sets; it decides which constraints to drop by interest heuristics, not by evidence from executors or the NL text.
baseline_notes: Inputs: a Declare constraint set. Adaptation: express SpecDx's temporal clauses (e.g., 'verify identity before modifying a reservation', 'no refund after cancellation') as Declare/LTLf templates; the MINERful implementation then removes constraints until the set is satisfiable (yielding conflict sets comparable to SpecDx's candidate MUSes) and prunes redundant ones. Sees only C. Code: the technique is implemented in MINERful (Java, GPL-3.0; a repository exists at github.com/Process-in-Chains/MINERful, reached via the authors' account, but the paper itself was not checked for the link).

title: Dealing with Behavioral Ambiguity in Textual Process Descriptions
authors: Han van der Aa; Henrik Leopold; Hajo A. Reijers
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
subtopics: behavioural ambiguity; textual process descriptions; behavioural space
summary: Introduces the behavioural space, which systematically captures all interpretations of ambiguous statements in a textual process description, and uses it for compliance checking on 47 texts, balancing between ignoring ambiguous statements and fixing one interpretation.
relation_to_specdx: Represents an ambiguous text by its set of readings, the same idea as SpecDx's set-valued entailment set A_c={x,y}. SpecDx estimates the readings empirically from LLM executors rather than enumerating them linguistically.

title: Impact-Driven Process Model Repair
authors: Artem Polyvyanyy; Wil M. P. Van Der Aalst; Arthur H. M. Ter Hofstede; Moe T. Wynn
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
subtopics: model repair; cost-bounded repair; alignments
summary: Impact-driven model repair assigns costs to repair actions (inserting or skipping activities) and, under a bound on the degree of change, searches for the repaired model that best improves alignment with the log.
relation_to_specdx: Treats specification repair as an optimisation over minimal changes, related to SpecDx's minimal correction sets; it trusts the log fully, whereas SpecDx models executor fallibility.

title: In Log and Model We Trust? A Generalized Conformance Checking Framework
authors: Andreas Rogge-Solti; Arik Senderovich; Matthias Weidlich; Jan Mendling; Avigdor Gal
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
subtopics: generalized conformance; log and model uncertainty; trust
summary: Notes that conformance checking assumes either the log or the model can be fully trusted, and proposes a generalized conformance-checking framework for the common case where neither is fully trusted, balancing repairs of log and model; it generalises standard techniques.
relation_to_specdx: Closest BPM idea to SpecDx's anchored model: both the specification (anchor) and the observations are fallible and the method decides which to correct. It differs by working on one log of process traces rather than a population of LLM executors, without executor accuracy/item-difficulty parameters, typed defects or witnesses.

title: Semantics and Analysis of DMN Decision Tables
authors: Diego Calvanese; Marlon Dumas; Ülari Laurson; Fabrizio M. Maggi; Marco Montali; Irene Teinemaa
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
subtopics: DMN; decision table analysis; overlapping and missing rules
summary: Gives a formal semantics for DMN decision tables, defines analysis tasks such as correctness and completeness, and provides scalable algorithms, based on a geometric interpretation of tables, to detect overlapping rules and missing rules.
relation_to_specdx: Overlapping rules (two outputs for one input) and missing rules (no output) are table-level analogues of SpecDx's ambiguity and contradiction/gap types, found symbolically without executors; SpecDx's policy clauses could be encoded as decision tables for this B5-style check.

title: Model repair — aligning process models to reality
authors: Dirk Fahland; Wil M.P. van der Aalst
venue: Information Systems
subtopics: model repair; alignments; subprocess insertion
summary: Repairs a process model with respect to an event log so that the repaired model replays the log while staying as similar as possible to the original, by aligning log and model, grouping deviations into sublogs and adding loops or subprocesses at the right location.
relation_to_specdx: The core analogy for SpecDx: systematic deviations at the same location are evidence that the model should change. Model repair assumes the log is correct and repairs everything; SpecDx must separate specification defects from scattered executor errors before blaming the specification.

title: AgentLTL: A Trace-Verification Framework for Measuring, Enforcing, and Training Procedural Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
authors: Laïla Elkoussy; Julien Perez
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: FO-LTL; trace verification; procedural compliance
summary: AgentLTL is a first-order LTL-derived language for procedural rules over agent traces that yields a deterministic, judge-free compliance score, used both to gate tool calls online and as a dense reward for fine-tuning.
relation_to_specdx: Gives a trace-level clause language like SpecDx's C; it scores agents against the clauses, while SpecDx scores the clauses against a population of agents.

title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
authors: Haoyu Wang; Christopher M. Poskitt; Jun Sun
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering
subtopics: runtime enforcement; agent guardrails; DSL
summary: AgentSpec is a lightweight DSL for runtime constraints on LLM agents: rules combine triggers, predicates and enforcement actions, and are applied to code-execution, embodied and autonomous-driving agents with millisecond overhead; LLM-generated rules are also evaluated.
relation_to_specdx: AgentSpec rules are executable clauses like SpecDx's guardrail triggers; it enforces them as given, while SpecDx asks whether such rules are contradictory, too strict or too weak relative to the text.

title: Autoformalization of Agent Instructions into Policy-as-Code
authors: Adam Mondl; Matthew Maisel; John H. Brock
venue: Second Workshop on Agents in the Wild (AIWILD) at ICML 2026 (arXiv preprint)
subtopics: autoformalization; Cedar policies; policy coverage
summary: Translates agent prompts, MCP tool descriptions and natural-language policy documents into formally verified Cedar policies with an LLM generator-critic loop, covering more of the source specification on MedAgentBench than hand-coded symbolic enforcement.
relation_to_specdx: Measures how much of T a formal policy covers, i.e., the hidden-requirement/weak-check gap between T and C that SpecDx detects statistically; its coverage is judged against the text, not via executor behaviour.

title: Beyond IVR: Benchmarking Customer Support LLM Agents for Business-Adherence
authors: Sumanth Balaji; Piyush Mishra; Aashraya Sachdeva; Suraj Agrawal
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: agent benchmark; policy adherence; customer support; journey graph
summary: JourneyBench uses graph representations of support workflows to generate customer-support scenarios and measures policy adherence with a User Journey Coverage Score, comparing a static-prompt agent with a dynamic-prompt agent that explicitly models policy control.
relation_to_specdx: Graph-based scenario generation from business policies resembles SpecDx's scenario synthesis; it scores agents, not the policy graph.

title: CompliBench: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Compliance Violation Detection in Dialogue Systems
authors: Jingbo Yang; Guanyu Yao; Bairu Hou; Xinghan Yang; Nikolai Glushnev; Iwona Bialynicka-Birula; Duo Ding; Shiyu Chang
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: LLM judge; policy violation detection; flaw injection
summary: CompliBench evaluates whether LLM judges can detect and localise guideline violations in multi-turn agent dialogues, using an automated pipeline with controllable flaw injection that yields ground-truth labels of the violated guideline and turn.
relation_to_specdx: Its controllable flaw injection with exact ground truth parallels SpecDx's mutation operators, but flaws are injected into agent behaviour, not into the specification; LLM-judge verdicts are a possible single-judge baseline.

title: PolicyGuard: A Dialogue-Grounded Sub-Agent Verifier for Policy Adherence in LLM Agents
authors: Seongjae Kang; Taehyung Yu; Sung Ju Hwang
venue: arXiv preprint (poster at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop 'Who Verifies the Agents?')
subtopics: policy adherence verifier; tau2-bench airline; dialogue context
summary: PolicyGuard is a sub-agent verifier that shares the agent's dialogue view, intercepts mutating tool calls, reasons over the raw policy text in context and returns remediation feedback; on τ²-bench airline it raises pass^4 by 6-12 points across three vendors and transfers to retail and telecom.
relation_to_specdx: Evaluated on SpecDx's τ²-bench subject and reasons directly over the policy text T; it treats T as authoritative and fixes agents, so residual disagreements between PolicyGuard and the benchmark checks are candidate specification defects SpecDx would type.

title: ProbGuard: Proactive Runtime Monitoring for LLM Agent Safety via Probabilistic Prediction
authors: Haoyu Wang; Christopher M. Poskitt; Jiali Wei; Jun Sun
venue: Proceedings of the 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
subtopics: runtime monitoring; probabilistic model checking; DTMC
summary: ProbGuard abstracts agent executions into symbolic states, learns a discrete-time Markov chain from traces, and proactively intervenes when the predicted probability of reaching an unsafe state exceeds a threshold, with PAC-style guarantees on the estimates.
relation_to_specdx: Like SpecDx it learns a statistical model from many agent traces, but it uses it to predict and prevent agent violations of a trusted specification rather than to diagnose the specification.

title: A Compliance Checking Framework Based on Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Jingyun Sun; Zhongze Luo; Yang Li
venue: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Computational Linguistics (COLING 2025), pages 2603-2615
subtopics: LLM compliance checking; RAG; regulations
summary: A retrieval-augmented framework for text-based compliance checking of business processes against laws and regulations, with static, dynamic and computational layers and an event-centric graph of regulatory knowledge; it reports state-of-the-art results on Chinese and English datasets.
relation_to_specdx: An LLM-based checker of business processes against regulatory text, a candidate form of SpecDx's static LLM review (B1); it assumes the regulation is authoritative rather than diagnosing it.

title: CRMArena-Pro: Holistic Assessment of LLM Agents Across Diverse Business Scenarios and Interactions
authors: Kung-Hsiang Huang; Akshara Prabhakar; Onkar Thorat; Divyansh Agarwal; Prafulla Kumar Choubey; Yixin Mao; Silvio Savarese; Caiming Xiong; Chien-Sheng Wu
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: agent benchmark; CRM; sales and CPQ; confidentiality
summary: CRMArena-Pro extends CRMArena with 19 expert-validated tasks across sales, service and configure-price-quote processes for B2B and B2C, multi-turn persona-driven interactions and confidentiality-awareness assessment; leading agents reach about 58% single-turn success.
relation_to_specdx: Covers the sales/quote processes of TonomyX's domain; a candidate subject on which SpecDx's diagnosis could be run, but it does not itself analyse specification defects.

title: CRMArena: Understanding the Capacity of LLM Agents to Perform Professional CRM Tasks in Realistic Environments
authors: Kung-Hsiang Huang; Akshara Prabhakar; Sidharth Dhawan; Yixin Mao; Huan Wang; Silvio Savarese; Caiming Xiong; Philippe Laban; Chien-Sheng Wu
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
subtopics: agent benchmark; CRM; business tasks
summary: CRMArena is a benchmark of nine customer-service tasks over a realistic Salesforce-style CRM environment with 16 interconnected business objects, designed with CRM experts, on which state-of-the-art agents perform poorly.
relation_to_specdx: A sales/service business environment close to the TonomyX procurement/sales case; its ground-truth answers are taken as correct, whereas SpecDx would audit them.

title: Enforcing Temporal Constraints for LLM Agents
authors: Adharsh Kamath; Sishen Zhang; Calvin Xu; Shubham Ugare; Gagandeep Singh; Sasa Misailovic
venue: arXiv preprint (ICLR 2026 Workshop VerifAI-2, per project listing)
subtopics: temporal safety; SMT; constrained decoding; retail and airline
summary: Agent-C offers a DSL for temporal safety properties of agent actions (e.g., authenticate before accessing data), translates them to first-order logic, uses SMT solving during token generation to detect non-compliant tool calls, and constrains decoding to compliant alternatives; evaluated on retail and airline customer-service domains.
relation_to_specdx: Formalises τ-bench-style retail/airline rules as temporal constraints; it assumes the rules are right and makes agents obey them, whereas SpecDx checks whether such rules and the benchmark checks are mutually consistent and faithful to T.

title: Evaluating large language models on business process modeling: framework, benchmark, and self-improvement analysis
authors: Humam Kourani; Alessandro Berti; Daniel Schuster; Wil M. P. van der Aalst
venue: Software and Systems Modeling
subtopics: LLM process modelling; benchmark; self-improvement
summary: Evaluates 16 LLMs on generating process models for a benchmark of 20 business processes with a conformance-based quality measure, finding large variation across models, consistent trends within LLM families, and gains from output optimisation.
relation_to_specdx: Its finding that performance clusters by LLM family supports SpecDx's modelling of family effects; it scores LLMs against reference models, while SpecDx scores the specification.

title: GuardAgent: Safeguard LLM Agents via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning
authors: Zhen Xiang; Linzhi Zheng; Yanjie Li; Junyuan Hong; Qinbin Li; Han Xie; Jiawei Zhang; Zidi Xiong; Chulin Xie; Carl Yang; Dawn Song; Bo Li
venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2025), PMLR 267:68316-68342
subtopics: guard agent; policy to code; access control
summary: GuardAgent is a guardrail agent that turns safety guard requests into a task plan and then into guardrail code that is executed to check a target agent's actions, using retrieved demonstrations from memory; it introduces EICU-AC and Mind2Web-SC benchmarks.
relation_to_specdx: Translates NL guard requests into executable checks, an automatic T-to-C step; SpecDx targets the defects such translation introduces (weak or over-strict checks).

title: ShieldAgent: Shielding Agents via Verifiable Safety Policy Reasoning
authors: Zhaorun Chen; Mintong Kang; Bo Li
venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2025), PMLR 267:8313-8344
subtopics: policy enforcement; rule extraction from policy documents; probabilistic rule circuits
summary: ShieldAgent extracts verifiable rules from policy documents, organises them into action-based probabilistic rule circuits, and checks a protected agent's trajectory against them with formal verification tools; it introduces ShieldAgent-Bench with 3,000 instruction/trajectory pairs.
relation_to_specdx: It compiles NL policy (T) into checkable rules (C) automatically, the step whose errors SpecDx detects; it does not examine whether extracted rules conflict with or under-approximate the policy text.

title: SOP-Bench: Complex Industrial SOPs for Evaluating LLM Agents
authors: Subhrangshu Nandi; Arghya Datta; Rohith Nama; Udita Patel; Nikhil Vichare; Indranil Bhattacharya; Prince Grover; Shivam Asija; Giuseppe Carenini; Wei Zhang; Arushi Gupta; Sreyoshi Bhaduri; Jing Xu; Huzefa Raja; Shayan Ray; Aaron Chan; Esther Xu Fei; Gaoyuan Du; Zuhaib Akhtar; Harshita Asnani; Weian Chan; Ming Xiong; Francesco Carbone; Jeetu Mirchandani
venue: arXiv preprint
subtopics: agent benchmark; SOP following; industrial procedures
summary: SOP-Bench contains 2,000+ tasks derived from expert-written standard operating procedures in 12 business domains, with AI-generated, human-validated tools, APIs and datasets that give executable interfaces and ground-truth outputs.
relation_to_specdx: Its SOPs (T) and ground-truth outputs (C) were partly generated by AI and then validated by humans, which is exactly the kind of S that can carry defects SpecDx targets.

title: ToolSandbox: A Stateful, Conversational, Interactive Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Tool Use Capabilities
authors: Jiarui Lu; Thomas Holleis; Yizhe Zhang; Bernhard Aumayer; Feng Nan; Haoping Bai; Shuang Ma; Shen Ma; Mengyu Li; Guoli Yin; Zirui Wang; Ruoming Pang
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2025
subtopics: agent benchmark; stateful tools; milestone evaluation
summary: ToolSandbox evaluates tool-using LLMs with stateful tool execution, implicit state dependencies between tools, an on-policy user simulator, and a dynamic evaluation over intermediate and final milestones on arbitrary trajectories.
relation_to_specdx: Milestones/minefields are executable clauses over trajectories, similar to SpecDx's C; ToolSandbox does not diagnose whether milestones are mis-specified.

title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
authors: Harsh Trivedi; Tushar Khot; Mareike Hartmann; Ruskin Manku; Vinty Dong; Edward Li; Shashank Gupta; Ashish Sabharwal; Niranjan Balasubramanian
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
subtopics: agent benchmark; state-based evaluation; unit tests
summary: AppWorld provides an execution engine of 9 everyday apps (457 APIs) populated with simulated users and a benchmark of 750 tasks requiring interactive code generation, evaluated by state-based unit tests that also check for collateral damage.
relation_to_specdx: Its programmatic state checks are clauses C in SpecDx's sense, including 'no collateral change' checks that can be weak or over-strict; AppWorld assumes they are correct, SpecDx would test them with a population of agents.

title: FlowBench: Revisiting and Benchmarking Workflow-Guided Planning for LLM-based Agents
authors: Ruixuan Xiao; Wentao Ma; Ke Wang; Yuchuan Wu; Junbo Zhao; Haobo Wang; Fei Huang; Yongbin Li
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
subtopics: agent benchmark; workflow-guided planning; SOP formats
summary: FlowBench is a benchmark for workflow-guided planning: 51 scenarios in 6 domains where workflow knowledge is given as text, code or flowcharts, with a multi-tier evaluation showing that even strong LLMs struggle to follow workflows.
relation_to_specdx: Studies how agents read a workflow specification (T) in different formats; SpecDx inverts the question and uses agents' readings to find where the workflow specification itself is defective.

title: Paraconsistent reasoning for inconsistency measurement in declarative process specifications
authors: Carl Corea; Isabelle Kuhlmann; Matthias Thimm; John Grant
venue: Information Systems
subtopics: inconsistency measurement; paraconsistent reasoning; declarative processes
summary: Journal extension that develops paraconsistent reasoning for measuring inconsistency in declarative process specifications on LTL over fixed traces, with new measures, their properties and complexity.
relation_to_specdx: As for the BPM 2022 paper: a symbolic measure of clause-set conflict that SpecDx's contradiction detection can be compared against.

title: ProMoAI: Process Modeling with Generative AI
authors: Humam Kourani; Alessandro Berti; Daniel Schuster; Wil M.P. van der Aalst
venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-ThirdInternational Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
subtopics: LLM process modelling; text to process model; tool
summary: ProMoAI is a tool that uses LLMs with prompt engineering, error handling and code generation to produce process models from textual descriptions, and refines them from user feedback.
relation_to_specdx: Produces a model from T automatically; repeated ProMoAI generations would be one way to obtain readings of T, but the tool itself does not compare readings or locate defects.

title: WorkArena: How Capable are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?
authors: Alexandre Drouin; Maxime Gasse; Massimo Caccia; Issam H. Laradji; Manuel Del Verme; Tom Marty; David Vazquez; Nicolas Chapados; Alexandre Lacoste
venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2024), PMLR 235:11642-11662
subtopics: agent benchmark; enterprise workflows; web agents
